The Starlight static site is now served by the **Hono host** via `apps/operator/bin/host-docs.ts` — it owns the bare-slug → `<slug>.html` resolution, the `Accept: text/markdown` → `<slug>.md` twin negotiation, and the `404.html` fallback. There is no `next.config.js` (it doesn’t exist) and no `proxy.ts`; the “Next rewrite in `afterFiles`” gotcha below is obsolete. The MCP adapter, the `dist/` → `public/internal/docs/` postbuild copy, the `build.format: 'file'` decision, and the URL contract are all unchanged.

## What changed in one paragraph

[Section titled “What changed in one paragraph”](#what-changed-in-one-paragraph)

We moved every internal-docs MDX page from `apps/operator/content/internal-docs/` to `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/` and rebuilt the surface on Astro 6 + Starlight 0.39 + starlight-llms-txt. The MCP `docs:*` tool surface (outline / get / search) keeps the same JSON shape via a new `starlightContentAdapter` in `packages/docs-engine/`. The docs site itself ships as static HTML in `apps/operator-docs/dist/`, copied into `apps/operator/public/internal/docs/` at build time so the **Hono host** (`bin/host-docs.ts`) serves it under the existing URL contract. (A couple of stale `agent-insights/` MDX files still linger under `apps/operator/content/internal-docs/` — the move was not byte-complete, but the live source is `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/`.)

## The agent contract still works

[Section titled “The agent contract still works”](#the-agent-contract-still-works)

* `GET /internal/docs/` — Starlight HTML home.
* `GET /internal/docs/<slug>` — HTML page (the Hono host’s `host-docs.ts` resolves a bare slug to `<slug>.html`).
* `GET /internal/docs/<slug>` with `Accept: text/markdown` — clean markdown twin (`<slug>.md`).
* `GET /internal/docs/llms.txt` — index produced by starlight-llms-txt.
* `GET /internal/docs/llms-full.txt` — full corpus.
* `GET /internal/docs/llms-small.txt` — abridged corpus (new; harmless).

Per-page `Accept: text/markdown` negotiation was originally dropped at the cutover and **restored separately**. `starlight-llms-txt` only emits aggregate `llms*.txt`; we restored the per-page channel by emitting `<slug>.md` twins from `apps/operator-docs/scripts/emit-md-twins.ts` (runs after `astro build`, uses `@papercusp/docs-engine`’s `renderMdxToMarkdown` + `withPreamble`). The **Hono host** (`apps/operator/bin/host-docs.ts`) rewrites `Accept: text/markdown` on a bare slug to the static `<slug>.md` (this used to be `proxy.ts` under Next). Agents can also use the `docs:get` MCP tool (engine-side, not HTTP) or pull from `/llms-full.txt`.

## Where things live now

[Section titled “Where things live now”](#where-things-live-now)

| Concern                      | Path                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| MDX source                   | `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/<section>/<slug>.mdx`                                                 |
| Astro config                 | `apps/operator-docs/astro.config.mjs`                                                                      |
| Build output                 | `apps/operator-docs/dist/`                                                                                 |
| Served from                  | `apps/operator/public/internal/docs/` (postbuild copy), via the Hono host `apps/operator/bin/host-docs.ts` |
| MCP docs adapter             | `packages/docs-engine/src/adapters/starlight.ts`                                                           |
| Engineering adapter selector | `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/docs/_engineering-adapter.ts`                                      |
| Sidebar config               | per-page frontmatter `sidebar.order` (used to be `meta.json`)                                              |
| MCP Resources                | `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/docs/resource-{index,section}.ts`                                  |

## Gotchas to know

[Section titled “Gotchas to know”](#gotchas-to-know)

### 1. `build.format: 'file'` is load-bearing

[Section titled “1. build.format: 'file' is load-bearing”](#1-buildformat-file-is-load-bearing)

Starlight default is `format: 'directory'` which emits `dist/<slug>/index.html`. We use `format: 'file'` (set in `astro.config.mjs`) which emits `dist/<slug>.html` instead. Why: serving the static files from `public/` without `format: 'file'` would need directory-index trailing-slash semantics. With `.html` files at the explicit path, the host resolves a bare slug to `<slug>.html` directly. (Originally this was a single Next rewrite; now `apps/operator/bin/host-docs.ts` does the bare-slug → `.html` resolution.)

### 2. (Obsolete) The Next rewrite is in `afterFiles`, not the top-level array

[Section titled “2. (Obsolete) The Next rewrite is in afterFiles, not the top-level array”](#2-obsolete-the-next-rewrite-is-in-afterfiles-not-the-top-level-array)

**Obsolete — Next is retired and `next.config.js` no longer exists.** This gotcha described where the docs rewrite rule lived in the Next config object (`rewrites() { return { beforeFiles, afterFiles, fallback } }`). The slug → `.html` resolution is now done in code by the Hono host (`apps/operator/bin/host-docs.ts`), not by a Next rewrite. Disregard.

### 3. Postbuild copy is in `apps/operator-docs/package.json`

[Section titled “3. Postbuild copy is in apps/operator-docs/package.json”](#3-postbuild-copy-is-in-appsoperator-docspackagejson)

The build script is `"build": "astro build && tsx scripts/emit-md-twins.ts && bash scripts/postbuild-copy.sh"`. If you run `astro build` directly (or just `npx astro build`), the `.md`-twin emit and the static copy steps are skipped and the host will serve stale content (and lose the `Accept: text/markdown` twins). Always run `npm run build` from `apps/operator-docs/`.

### 4. Both fumadocs setups were removed

[Section titled “4. Both fumadocs setups were removed”](#4-both-fumadocs-setups-were-removed)

`apps/operator/source.config.ts`, `apps/operator/lib/source.ts`, `apps/operator/app/(docs)/**`, `apps/operator/app/llms.txt/`, `apps/operator/app/llms-full.txt/`, `apps/operator/app/llms.mdx/`, `apps/operator/app/api/search/` are all gone. Same paths in the old `@papercup/web` app (now retired under `_retired/papercup/`). If you find references to those, they’re stale; remove or update.

### 5. The `fumadocs` plugin slug is unrelated

[Section titled “5. The fumadocs plugin slug is unrelated”](#5-the-fumadocs-plugin-slug-is-unrelated)

`@papercupai/fumadocs` (with the `@` prefix) is the name of an internal Papercusp plugin for per-harness docs viewing — NOT the npm package we removed. Plugin manifests, route handlers, and UI code may legitimately reference `fumadocs` as a slug. Don’t remove those.

### 6. `<Callout>` → `<Aside>`

[Section titled “6. \<Callout> → \<Aside>”](#6-callout--aside)

47 occurrences across 44 MDX files were rewritten. Type map:

* `<Callout type="info">` → `<Aside type="note">`
* `<Callout type="warn">` → `<Aside type="caution">`
* `<Callout type="warning">` → `<Aside type="caution">`

Import path: `import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';`

## Performance

[Section titled “Performance”](#performance)

A full `astro build` of the 129-page site completes in \~21s, with Pagefind search indexing adding \~0.5s. The output is plain static HTML: the operator serves it straight from `public/internal/docs/`, so there is **no runtime docs cost** — no second Node process, and no per-request MDX compilation (fumadocs compiled MDX inside the Next request path).

A head-to-head build-time / bundle-size comparison against the old fumadocs setup isn’t possible — the F10 cutover removed it before a baseline was captured. The concrete, measurable win is the runtime one above: docs rendering moved entirely out of the request path.

## Migration plan + companion docs

[Section titled “Migration plan + companion docs”](#migration-plan--companion-docs)

* Plan: [`apps/operator/docs/plans/fumadocs-to-starlight-2026-05-20.md`](../../docs/plans/fumadocs-to-starlight-2026-05-20.md) (in repo)
* Deferred companion: Next-removal plan at the same date — see the same plans/ directory.
* The `papercusp-su.tools.md` prompt and `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` reflect the new paths and components list. Re-run `apps/operator/scripts/install-standalone-mcp.sh` if your CLAUDE.md still says “fumadocs”.

# Fleet state is queried, not chatted — query vs change-feed vs message

> "Who's on what" is a table query (fleet:assignments over the harness_shared.fleet_assignment view), change-awareness is the fleet_assignment PG NOTIFY feed, and the coord message channel carries only the unpredictable. Never reconstruct fleet state by replaying coord messages.

## The line (the principle)

[Section titled “The line (the principle)”](#the-line-the-principle)

Three different needs, three different surfaces — mixing them is how the coord inbox became a \~360-events/6h state-replay log (`state-not-chat-fleet-state-2026-06-05` D-001):

| You want…                                                                                  | Use                                                                                                                                     | Never                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| to **know** current state (“who’s running / what is X doing / is anyone on plan P”)        | `fleet:assignments` / `coord:presence` — one table query                                                                                | scan/replay the coord inbox to derive it                                |
| to be **notified** of a state change                                                       | the `fleet_assignment` PG NOTIFY change-feed (`packages/operator-core/lib/fleet-assignment-bus.ts`), or your scoped coord subscriptions | poll the message stream                                                 |
| to **say** something genuinely unpredictable (a question, a design call, a SPLIT proposal) | `coord:send`                                                                                                                            | encode state in prose (“DONE + tested…” — that’s `work_items:complete`) |

This is the “DB is not a transport” principle pointed the other way: **the message bus is not a state store.**

## The canonical state query

[Section titled “The canonical state query”](#the-canonical-state-query)

“Is agent X on plan P” used to require knowing *which of three tables* to check (`coord_presence.current_plan_slug`, `plan_item_claims`, `work_items.taken_by`). Migration 165 unifies them at read time in **`harness_shared.fleet_assignment`**, read via **`fleet:assignments`** (`{ agent }` = what is X doing; `{ plan }` = who’s on P) or `packages/operator-core/lib/fleet/assignments.ts` in code. `/api/adv/roster` serves the same view (per-entry `claims` + top-level `orphanedClaims`).

The view is **claim-primary**: a live lease whose holder crashed still surfaces (`orphaned: true`) — the single most important signal (abandoned/stuck work). A presence-primary join would silently drop it. It also flags `declaredUnclaimed` — an agent whose self-declared plan is backed by no actual claim.

## The change-feed

[Section titled “The change-feed”](#the-change-feed)

Migration 165 fires `NOTIFY fleet_assignment` (`<workspace>::<source>::<agent>`) on **meaningful** changes only — presence intent/plan/files, claim acquire/release/owner-change, `taken_by`/`assignee` flips. Heartbeat-only presence bumps and lease renewals are deliberately silent (they happen per tool call, fleet-wide). Subscribe with `onFleetAssignmentChange()` from `packages/operator-core/lib/fleet-assignment-bus.ts` (the notification is a wake — re-query the view; don’t treat the payload as the record).

## The lifecycle messages are projections, not the record

[Section titled “The lifecycle messages are projections, not the record”](#the-lifecycle-messages-are-projections-not-the-record)

The auto-emits (”▶ now working on…”, ”✓ DONE…”, “Taking X”) fire *after* the table write (`onlyOnSuccess`) and render *from* it — they are one-directional, human-readable projections (`packages/operator-core/lib/coord-lifecycle/lifecycle-rules.ts`, `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/complete.ts`). Combined with Brief 28’s audience scoping ([coord-emit-subscription-scoping](/internal/docs/agent-insights/coord-emit-subscription-scoping)), they reach only watching subscribers. If you find code (or a prompt) deriving “who’s on what” from these messages, that’s the bug — point it at the view.

# Substrate diagnostic stack — what to use when the Hyperbee flag flips

> The full flag-gated substrate boot + claim + bootstrap-progress + admin diagnostic stack. What each piece does, what URL surfaces them, and how to verify a substrate-enabled harness end-to-end.

Update (Model B, Stage 4d): the substrate is no longer flag-gated

The `PAPERCUSP_DOGFOOD_SUBSTRATE_ENABLE=1` opt-in gate **was removed** — the Model B substrate now **always boots** in-process (verified: `in-process-status.ts`

* `share-finalize.ts` only mention the var in “the gate was removed” comments; no code reads `process.env.PAPERCUSP_DOGFOOD_SUBSTRATE_ENABLE` anymore, and `.env.local` setting it is a no-op). `substrateActive` is constant-`true` at runtime; it is `false` ONLY when a test forces `forceDisabledForTest`. So the diagnostic surfaces below are still real and useful, but the “set the env var and restart” framing throughout this page is stale — there is no flag to flip. Read the surfaces as “always-on diagnostics,” not “flag-gated.”

## What this is

[Section titled “What this is”](#what-this-is)

The Model B substrate gives every workspace a per-harness Hyperbee + Autobase substrate running in-process. Several diagnostic surfaces let you verify the substrate is alive, ops are merging, and the orchestrator is using the distributed claim engine.

The pieces are layered so each can be exercised in isolation. If you have to debug a substrate problem, walk the layers top-down until you find the one that’s silent.

## The layers, top to bottom

[Section titled “The layers, top to bottom”](#the-layers-top-to-bottom)

### 1. `/admin/dogfood-substrate` — one URL to verify everything

[Section titled “1. /admin/dogfood-substrate — one URL to verify everything”](#1-admindogfood-substrate--one-url-to-verify-everything)

SSR page that composes every diagnostic surface below. Shows:

* Top: `<SubstrateStatusBadge>` reflecting `enabled + bootedCount`.

* Table row per booted `(workspaceId, harnessSlug)` with:

  * `<BootstrapProgressIndicator>` (live merge progress)
  * `<ClaimAttemptStatsPill>` (won/lost/error counts)

If this page says “Substrate off,” nothing else below it will produce data — set the env var and restart.

### 2. `GET /api/admin/dogfood-substrate-status`

[Section titled “2. GET /api/admin/dogfood-substrate-status”](#2-get-apiadmindogfood-substrate-status)

JSON read of the in-process boot map:

```json
{ "enabled": true,
  "booted": [{ "workspaceId": "ws-1", "harnessSlug": "papercup" }],
  "bootedCount": 1 }
```

Used by the admin page + `<SubstrateStatusBadgeClient slug={...}/>` in chrome headers.

### 3. `GET /api/harness/:slug/bootstrap-progress`

[Section titled “3. GET /api/harness/:slug/bootstrap-progress”](#3-get-apiharnessslugbootstrap-progress)

Per-harness live merge progress:

```json
{ "progress": { "mergedOps": 7, "highestSeen": 12,
                "lastChangeMs": 1700000000000, "caughtUp": false }}
```

Drives `<BootstrapProgressIndicatorClient slug={...}/>`. Returns `{ progress: null }` when the substrate hasn’t recorded merge activity for this harness yet — the client renders nothing in that case (so the badge is invisible until there’s something to show).

### 4. `GET /api/harness/:slug/claim-attempts`

[Section titled “4. GET /api/harness/:slug/claim-attempts”](#4-get-apiharnessslugclaim-attempts)

Two read modes via query param:

* `?stats=1` → `{ stats: { total, won, lost, error } }`
* (default) → `{ attempts: ClaimAttemptRow[] }`

Reads `harness_shared.claim_audit`. Used by the admin page and any debug surface that wants to see claim outcomes. Defensive against missing table — returns empty / zero.

### 5. Orchestrator decision

[Section titled “5. Orchestrator decision”](#5-orchestrator-decision)

Production claim path branches on `getClaimStrategy({ workspaceId, harnessSlug })`:

* `'single-writer'` → legacy claim path (unchanged).
* `'distributed'` → `await attemptDistributedClaim({ ... })`.

`attemptDistributedClaim` returns one of three reasons:

* `'substrate-not-booted'` (handle missing) → caller falls back.
* `'pubkey-unresolved'` (handle present but `local.key` missing).
* `'attempted'` (real result; includes `won` + audit outcome).

### 6. Substrate boot

[Section titled “6. Substrate boot”](#6-substrate-boot)

`bootHarnessSubstrate({ workspaceRoot, workspaceId, harnessSlug })` (`packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/boot.ts`):

1. Open per-harness corestore.
2. Build Autobase view with schema-version filter.
3. Register all per-table PG projection writers via `registerAllHarnessProjections` (`projections/register-all.ts` — the `buildHarnessProjections` array is the single source of truth for the set; it has grown well past the original 8, so trust the array, not any “N projections” comment).
4. Start `startBootstrapProgressPoller`. Polls `base.view.length` every 1s and calls `recordMergedOps`.

`close()` reverses in inverse order (poller stop → autobase close → store close).

Boot is invoked during the join/default-boot wiring, gated by the env var.

## End-to-end verification checklist

[Section titled “End-to-end verification checklist”](#end-to-end-verification-checklist)

1. (No flag to set — the substrate always boots.) Open `/admin/dogfood-substrate` — top badge should be green “Substrate live (N harnesses)”.
2. Per-row bootstrap pill should appear once any ops merge.
3. Trigger a feature claim race. The claim-audit pill should grow `won` and (if multi-writer) `lost` counts.
4. Pick a slug → curl `/api/harness/<slug>/claim-attempts` — rows should match the pill.

## Gating (historical — the flag is gone)

[Section titled “Gating (historical — the flag is gone)”](#gating-historical--the-flag-is-gone)

**Update:** this section described the now-removed `PAPERCUSP_DOGFOOD_SUBSTRATE_ENABLE` gate. With Model B / Stage 4d the substrate always boots, so the “inert when unset” behavior no longer exists. The orchestrator still falls back to the single-writer path **per (workspace, harness) when a substrate handle is absent** — `getClaimStrategy` returns `'distributed'` only when `getBootedHandle` finds a booted handle, else `'single-writer'`, and `attemptDistributedClaim` still returns `substrate-not-booted` when the handle is missing — but that is now driven by boot success, not by a flag.

# Substrate flag-flip runbook — what to do when you enable the Hyperbee substrate

> Step-by-step procedure for flipping PAPERCUSP_DOGFOOD_SUBSTRATE_ENABLE=1, what to expect at each stage, how to verify success, and how to roll back cleanly if something goes wrong.

Superseded: there is no flag to flip anymore (Model B / Stage 4d)

The `PAPERCUSP_DOGFOOD_SUBSTRATE_ENABLE` opt-in gate **was removed** with the Model B substrate rewrite — the substrate now **always boots** in-process and no code reads the env var (it survives only in “the gate was removed” comments in `in-process-status.ts` / `share-finalize.ts`, and setting it in `.env.local` is a no-op). This whole “set the env var → restart → verify the flag took effect → roll back by unsetting it” procedure is therefore **obsolete**. What is still real and useful below: the diagnostic surfaces (`substrate:status` CLI, `/admin/dogfood-substrate`, `/api/admin/dogfood-substrate-health`, `/api/harness/<slug>/claim-attempts`, the boot-history table) and the boot-error troubleshooting table — read those as “verify the always-on substrate,” not “verify the flag.” (Note: step 5’s `<HarnessChromeHeaderBadges>` component does not exist; the live pills are `SubstrateHealthPill` / `BootstrapProgressIndicator` in `app/harness/insights/`.) For the current diagnostic walkthrough see [Substrate diagnostic stack](/internal/docs/agent-insights/substrate-diagnostic-stack).

## Before you start

[Section titled “Before you start”](#before-you-start)

* This is a **one-process toggle** — restart the operator after editing the env var. It is not picked up live.
* Substrate boot opens real Hyperswarm peer connections + writes to local Hypercore stores under `~/.papercusp-workspaces/<workspace>/.papercusp/<harness>/hyperbee/`. Leaves disk artefacts after the first run; rolling back the flag does NOT delete them.
* Native dependencies must be installed (corestore, hypercore, autobase, hyperswarm, b4a). If `npm install` skipped them (rare; usually `--no-optional` or similar) the boot fails fast in `boot-history` with a clear error.
* Has **no effect** on the legacy single-writer claim path. The orchestrator only switches to the distributed path if your code calls `getClaimStrategy()` — see “Orchestrator wiring” below.

## Steps

[Section titled “Steps”](#steps)

### 1. Set the env var + restart

[Section titled “1. Set the env var + restart”](#1-set-the-env-var--restart)

```bash
export PAPERCUSP_DOGFOOD_SUBSTRATE_ENABLE=1
# kill -HUP / restart the operator process so instrumentation-node.ts
# picks it up.
```

### 2. Verify the flag took effect

[Section titled “2. Verify the flag took effect”](#2-verify-the-flag-took-effect)

```bash
cd apps/operator && npm run substrate:status
```

Or open `/admin/dogfood-substrate` in a browser.

Expected:

```plaintext
Substrate flag: ✓ ON   booted: 0 harnesses
  → flag is on but no handles in boot map yet.
```

If you see `· off`, the env var didn’t propagate — check whether you restarted the right process.

### 3. Wait for harnesses to boot

[Section titled “3. Wait for harnesses to boot”](#3-wait-for-harnesses-to-boot)

`instrumentation-node.ts` boots harnesses in parallel during startup (typically `<30s` for a handful of harnesses on local disk). The boot table on `/admin/dogfood-substrate` populates as each one comes up.

If a boot **fails**, the `boot-history` section at the bottom of the page shows the error message. Common causes:

| Error pattern               | Likely cause                                              |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `corestore lock contention` | Two processes opening the same store. Kill the other one. |
| `bootstrap timeout`         | Hyperswarm can’t reach any peer (firewall / no internet). |
| `schema_version mismatch`   | A peer is on a newer Papercusp. Update or wait.           |
| `permission denied`         | Disk perms on `~/.papercusp-workspaces/...`.              |

### 4. Check the health verdict per harness

[Section titled “4. Check the health verdict per harness”](#4-check-the-health-verdict-per-harness)

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:3070/api/admin/dogfood-substrate-health | jq
```

Or look at the per-row `SubstrateHealthPill` on the admin page. Verdict should be `healthy` once boot completes and no claim attempts have errored.

### 5. (Optional) Surface in chrome

[Section titled “5. (Optional) Surface in chrome”](#5-optional-surface-in-chrome)

Drop `<HarnessChromeHeaderBadges slug={...} />` into the harness header to show the 3-pill row (status / health / bootstrap) live in-app.

### 6. (Optional) Wire orchestrator

[Section titled “6. (Optional) Wire orchestrator”](#6-optional-wire-orchestrator)

The distributed claim path is off until production code calls `getClaimStrategy()` + branches. This is a code change, not a runtime toggle — see `lib/orchestrator/distributed-claim.ts` for the pattern.

## What you’ll see when things go well

[Section titled “What you’ll see when things go well”](#what-youll-see-when-things-go-well)

* `/admin/dogfood-substrate` top bar: green “Substrate live” pill + green health pill with `N✓` count.
* Per-harness row: green health pill + bootstrap “Up to date” pill.
* Boot history: 1 boot\_start + 1 boot\_ok per harness.
* `substrate:status` CLI exits 0.

## What you’ll see when things go wrong

[Section titled “What you’ll see when things go wrong”](#what-youll-see-when-things-go-wrong)

* Top bar: green “Substrate live” but yellow/red health pill.
* Per-row: health pill in `degraded` or `unhealthy` state. Tooltip lists the reasons (e.g. `claim error rate 30% ≥ 25%`).
* Boot history: `boot_fail` rows with the error message.
* `substrate:status` CLI exits 1.

## Rolling back

[Section titled “Rolling back”](#rolling-back)

The flag is a no-op when unset. To disable:

```bash
unset PAPERCUSP_DOGFOOD_SUBSTRATE_ENABLE
# restart the operator
```

What happens:

* Substrate boot is skipped on the next start.
* The boot map stays empty.
* `attemptDistributedClaim` returns `substrate-not-booted` for every call — production code falls back to the legacy single-writer path.
* Health pill shows `disabled`.
* The on-disk Hypercore stores from previous boots stay where they are (safe to leave; harmless when not opened).

To wipe the on-disk substrate entirely (use only if rotating keys or starting fresh):

```bash
rm -rf ~/.papercusp-workspaces/*/.papercusp/*/hyperbee/
```

## Telemetry checkpoint

[Section titled “Telemetry checkpoint”](#telemetry-checkpoint)

After the first 24h with the flag on, sanity-check:

* `/api/admin/dogfood-substrate-boot-history?kinds=boot_fail` — should be empty or only show transient errors.
* `/api/harness/<slug>/claim-attempts?stats=1` — `error` count should be < 5% of `total`.
* `/api/admin/dogfood-substrate-health` — every harness `healthy`.

If any of these stay degraded for hours, file an issue with the boot- history entries attached.

# Substrate revocation — the trust model (read before touching admission)

> How peer revocation works in the Model B substrate — self vs owner, the GitHub-anchored authority, the re-verify enforcement, and why it's fail-open.

If you’re about to change substrate admission/revocation, or a security review flags something here as a “gap,” read this first — several of these are **intentional** trust-model decisions, not bugs.

## Two flavors of revocation (both enforced)

[Section titled “Two flavors of revocation (both enforced)”](#two-flavors-of-revocation-both-enforced)

1. **Self-revocation** (`papercusp-substrate-revocation-v1-2026-06-01`). A contributor revokes their OWN device key (lost/rotated device). Mechanism: the device pubkey is added to that contributor’s own `revoked_pubkeys` (a `TEXT[]` on `harness_shared.contributors`, replicated via the substrate). Trigger: `revokeSelfDevice` / `POST /api/admin/substrate/revoke-self-device` / the `substrate:revoke_self_device` MCP tool — guarded by `not_your_key` (you can only revoke keys in your OWN `device_attestations`). Enforcement: `boot.ts` seeds the admission `revoked` Set from `loadRevokedPubkeys` at startup (unconditional, fail-open) AND refreshes it inside every `mergeNow`.

2. **Owner-revocation** (`papercusp-substrate-revocation-v2-owner-2026-06-01`, Component A). Kicking out a different contributor (a bad actor). Authority is **GitHub**, not a papercusp-native owner: a repo admin **deletes the contributor’s `user/<id>` branch** (the channel-2 artifact). Enforcement: `boot.ts` periodically **re-verifies admitted peers’ channel-2** (throttled inside `mergeNow`, default \~15 min) and drops any whose binding conclusively `fail`s.

The gap that motivated rev-v2

Model B verified a peer’s channel-2 binding ONCE at admission and re-checked only PENDING peers. An already-**admitted** peer was NEVER re-verified — so a deleted GitHub binding was not noticed. If you see admission logic that only checks at admit-time, that gap is back.

## Why GitHub-anchored authority (not a papercusp owner gate)

[Section titled “Why GitHub-anchored authority (not a papercusp owner gate)”](#why-github-anchored-authority-not-a-papercusp-owner-gate)

Deliberate, consistent with `papercusp-trust-model-2026-05-31` + the **no-collaborator-gate** decision + Phase-1b §8 / D-009: **GitHub is the real authority** for the thing that matters (merging code); peer-synced state is **advisory**. An owner-signed revocation list was considered and rejected — it reintroduces exactly the papercusp-side authority gate that decision avoided, and the P-068 “owner” is only *provisional*/contestable. Re-verifying channel-2 is **not** a collaborator gate; it re-applies the *same* check admission already requires, just periodically.

## Intentional decisions a reviewer will want to “fix” (don’t, without re-deciding the posture)

[Section titled “Intentional decisions a reviewer will want to “fix” (don’t, without re-deciding the posture)”](#intentional-decisions-a-reviewer-will-want-to-fix-dont-without-re-deciding-the-posture)

* **Fail-OPEN on a revocation/re-verify LOAD failure** (rev-v1 D-006, rev-v2 D-004). If the PG read or the GitHub API fails, admission continues WITHOUT the (new) revocation rather than evicting peers. Rationale: advisory substrate + GitHub-is-authority → a transient blip must not self-inflict a federation outage. It’s **visible** (`merge_error`/`announce_error` events) and **self-healing** (re-checked next cycle). A channel-2-`fail` (conclusive) DOES drop; only transient (`pending`/api-down) keeps. Fail-secure (evict-on-failure) is the wrong trade here.
* **A channel-2-fail drop does NOT blocklist the pubkey.** A re-published binding is re-admitted by normal admission; a still-deleted binding is rejected (`binding_invalid`) — no flap. (Self-revocation DOES persist via `revoked_pubkeys` — that’s the difference.)
* **Revocation is non-retroactive.** Ops a peer already merged remain (advisory; GitHub is authority). True cryptographic removal isn’t a goal.

## Not built (intentional)

[Section titled “Not built (intentional)”](#not-built-intentional)

* **Rev-v2 Component B** — an in-app “delete a contributor’s `user/<id>` branch via the GitHub API” trigger. It’s a destructive outward-facing action + optional (a repo admin deletes the branch on GitHub directly; Component A enforces it). Held pending an explicit decision.
* **Un-revoke / re-instate** — YAGNI; revocation is append-only.
* **Multi-device per login** — see `phase1b-federation-limitations`.

# Substrate write-side stack — one shape per Hyperbee table

> The 7-layer pattern for shipping a new Hyperbee-backed write path (substrate write helper → PG projection → HTTP wrapper → polling read hook → pure UI → client wrapper → list integration). Shipped in batch for feature_queue (P-032) and contributors (P-033) on 2026-05-25; document so the next per-table pickup can replicate without rediscovering.

Update: server layers moved to operator-core; the worked-example UI is gone

The **server layers (1–4)** all moved out of `apps/operator/lib/` into `packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/**` and `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/harness/**` — the write helpers, projections, `load-queue-membership`, and the `feature-queue` route still exist there and the route is still mounted. But the **UI layers (5–7)** named in the worked examples below — `useQueueMembership`, `QueueAvatarCluster`, `PullToQueueButton(Client)`, the `FeatureList.tsx`/`FeatureFilterChips` integration, and the `ContributorsTab`/`ContributorRow` surfaces — **no longer exist** in the tree (the operator UI moved to the Vite SPA and those write-side surfaces were not carried over). Treat the 7-layer shape as the still-valid *pattern*, but don’t expect to find those exact UI files. The `app/harness/insights/` directory today holds the substrate-*diagnostic* components (`SubstrateStatusBadge`, `BootstrapProgressIndicator`, `ClaimAttemptStatsPill`, …), not the feature-queue write UI.

## When this applies

[Section titled “When this applies”](#when-this-applies)

You are adding (or wiring up) a Hyperbee-backed table that users can *write to* from the UI. The read-side projection probably already exists; the write path needs all 7 layers below.

Skip this insight when you’re only consuming (read-only) — the projection writes to PG and a normal PG-read endpoint is fine.

## The 7-layer stack

[Section titled “The 7-layer stack”](#the-7-layer-stack)

Each Hyperbee write-table follows the same shape:

```plaintext
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. Substrate write helper                                  │
│    packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/write-<table>.ts│
│    Pure: takes BootedHarnessHandle + row, appends op.      │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 2. PG projection (existing)                                │
│    .../lib/sync/hyperbee/projections/<table>.ts            │
│    Substrate's applyHyperbeeOpToPg fans the op to here.    │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 3. PG reader                                               │
│    .../lib/sync/hyperbee/load-<table>-membership.ts        │
│    Pure: SELECT joined with `contributors` for UI.         │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 4. HTTP wrapper                                            │
│    .../lib/endpoint-route/routes/harness/<table>.ts        │
│    GET membership; POST per write verb.                    │
│    substrate-off → 200 + reason='substrate-off'.           │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 5. Polling read hook                                       │
│    use<Table>Membership.ts (UI layer)                      │
│    Polls every 8s; pauses when document.hidden.            │
│    Returns {map, membersFor, isQueued, refresh}.           │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 6. Pure UI primitives                                      │
│    <Table>AvatarCluster.tsx (read) / <Action>Button.tsx    │
│    No state; consumer feeds props.                         │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 7. Client wrapper                                          │
│    <Action>ButtonClient.tsx                                │
│    Optimistic flip + POST + revert on failure.             │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                          │
                          ▼
        List integration (FeatureList.tsx, FeaturePage, etc.)
        — drops hook + UI + client into the row render.
```

## Cardinality + contract

[Section titled “Cardinality + contract”](#cardinality--contract)

* **One write helper module per table** — exports `enqueueX` / `dequeueX` / `publishXRow`. Both put-ops with semantic differences (e.g. dequeue is soft-delete `removed_at = now`, not a `del` op; the projection treats `del` as hard delete).
* **One PG reader per table** — pure; injectable `runQuery`; returns `{}` when the substrate table doesn’t exist yet (not booted, flag off, etc.).
* **One HTTP route file per table** with N tools (one GET + enqueue/dequeue/etc. POSTs). The route’s `parseWriteBody` exported so unit tests can hit it directly without spinning a fake Request.
* **The hook + UI tests use vitest + @testing-library/react with `@vitest-environment jsdom`** and `afterEach(() => cleanup())` — the project’s house style.

## Substrate-off behavior contract

[Section titled “Substrate-off behavior contract”](#substrate-off-behavior-contract)

Every layer must handle “substrate not booted” cleanly:

| Layer           | substrate-off shape                         |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Write helper    | Caller’s problem — helper assumes handle.   |
| HTTP write POST | `{ok: false, reason: 'substrate-off'}` 200. |
| Client wrapper  | Reverts optimistic flip on `ok: false`.     |
| PG read         | `{}` when projection table doesn’t exist.   |
| Read hook       | `loaded: true` with empty map.              |
| Avatar cluster  | Renders em-dash for empty members.          |

The point: a flag-flip toggles the entire stack alive without route changes. The UI shows ”—” before flip, real data after.

## Worked example — contributors
