# /admin command reference

> Every command wired into the /admin ops dashboard — what it runs, what it depends on, what it produces.

History: the operator frontend was Next.js until mid-2026

Next.js is **fully removed** (`finish-next-removal-2026-06-01`): no `next` dependency, no `next.config.js`, no `next/*` shims. The operator frontend is the **Vite** SPA (`@papercusp/operator-vite`, TanStack Router, `:3055` in dev) served by the `:3070` **Hono host** (`apps/operator/bin/hono-host.ts`); the `/admin` run route is a Hono `endpoint-route` handler. See the `operator-next-is-retired` insight.

## How the page works

[Section titled “How the page works”](#how-the-page-works)

`http://localhost:3055/admin` lists every build/install/sim command as a card with Run/Stop buttons and a live log box (5000-line ring, stderr in red).

Mechanism:

* **Source of truth**: `packages/operator-core/lib/admin-commands.ts` exports `ADMIN_COMMANDS` — the server-side allow-list. Each entry is `{id, label, section, description?, command, cwd?}` where `section` is `'building' | 'running' | 'simulators' | 'packaged-build'`. The client only sends `cmd: <id>`; the server never accepts raw shell.
* **Spawning**: `GET /api/admin/run?cmd=<id>` opens an SSE stream (the Hono route `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/admin/run.ts`). It forks `bash -lic <command>` as a detached process group (so closing the stream `process.kill(-pid, 'SIGTERM')`s the whole tree). Output is line-buffered: a `meta` event up front (`{commandId, label, command, cwd?, pid, startedAt}`), `log` events (`{stream: 'stdout'|'stderr', line}`), an `error` event on spawn failure, and an `exit` event on close (`{code, signal}`).
* **Why `-lic`**: `-l` sources `.profile`, `-i` makes the shell interactive so `.bashrc`’s non-interactive guard short-circuit doesn’t fire — so the spawn inherits `NVM_DIR`, `BUN_INSTALL`, `COMPOSIO_INSTALL_DIR`, `HINDSIGHT_API_URL`, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, etc. exactly as your interactive terminal would. The two cosmetic warnings `-i`-without-TTY emits (`cannot set terminal process group`, `no job control in this shell`) are filtered out server-side.

## Auth

[Section titled “Auth”](#auth)

**None.** The admin page is loopback-only (operator binds `127.0.0.1:3055` by default) and is intentionally NOT linked from any nav. Reach it by typing the URL. There is no `requireFlag()` check — earlier versions had one tied to `papercusp-admin`, removed 2026-05-13.

## Building section

[Section titled “Building section”](#building-section)

### `build-linux-prod` — Linux Prod Build

[Section titled “build-linux-prod — Linux Prod Build”](#build-linux-prod--linux-prod-build)

Runs locally on the dev host (`cwd` = `papercusp-desktop`). Produces both `.deb` and `.rpm` in one pass, then audits each.

```plaintext
cd /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercup/papercusp-desktop
npm run build              # = tauri build (the sidecar must already be built — see note)
bin/audit-bundle.sh src-tauri/target/release/bundle/deb/Papercusp_0.0.1_amd64.deb
bin/audit-bundle.sh src-tauri/target/release/bundle/rpm/Papercusp-0.0.1-1.x86_64.rpm
```

> **Note:** `npm run build` is just `tauri build` (`beforeBuildCommand` is empty). The bundled `serve.mjs` sidecar is produced by a **separate** `bin/build-desktop-sidecar.sh` step — `bin/release-local.sh` runs it before `tauri build`. If you only run `tauri build` you’ll bundle a stale/empty `sidecar/`.

\~10 minutes if the Rust target dir is warm, \~30 if cold.

**Outputs** (verify via the auditor card afterward, too):

* `src-tauri/target/release/bundle/deb/Papercusp_0.0.1_amd64.deb` (\~700 MB)
* `src-tauri/target/release/bundle/rpm/Papercusp-0.0.1-1.x86_64.rpm` (\~715 MB)

### `build-mac-prod` — Mac Prod Build

[Section titled “build-mac-prod — Mac Prod Build”](#build-mac-prod--mac-prod-build)

SSHes into the macOS VM (`ssh -i ~/.ssh/papercup-vm-mac -p 2222 aviweiss@127.0.0.1`), builds inside `~/papercupai/papercusp-desktop`, scps the DMG back to the dev host, then audits it.

```plaintext
ssh -i /home/marsh-office/.ssh/papercup-vm-mac -p 2222 aviweiss@127.0.0.1 'bash -lc "
  . $HOME/.nvm/nvm.sh; nvm use 22
  cd ~/papercupai/papercusp-desktop
  NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 npm install --legacy-peer-deps
  NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 npm run build
"'
scp -i /home/marsh-office/.ssh/papercup-vm-mac -P 2222 \
  aviweiss@127.0.0.1:papercupai/papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/dmg/Papercusp_0.0.1_x86_64.dmg /home/marsh-office/
bin/audit-bundle.sh /home/marsh-office/Papercusp_0.0.1_x86_64.dmg
```

\~30–45 min. NEEDS the Mac VM running with disk room (≥10 GB free). See [VMs](/internal/docs/build-system/vms).

**Hard-coded requirements** (all currently met on the VM):

* Node 22 via nvm (script does `nvm use 22`)
* `--legacy-peer-deps` (workspace install hangs without it — see [VMs](/internal/docs/build-system/vms#npm---legacy-peer-deps-is-required))
* `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192` (without it, npm OOMs on the 16-GB VM)

### `build-windows-prod` — Windows Prod Build

[Section titled “build-windows-prod — Windows Prod Build”](#build-windows-prod--windows-prod-build)

SSHes into the Windows VM (`ssh -i ~/.ssh/papercup-vm-win -p 2223 User@127.0.0.1`) and runs `win-build.ps1`. Same shape as Mac. Copies back `.msi` (from `bundle/msi/`) and NSIS `.exe` (from `bundle/nsis/`) to `/home/marsh-office/`, then audits both.

```plaintext
ssh -i /home/marsh-office/.ssh/papercup-vm-win -p 2223 User@127.0.0.1 \
  "powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File win-build.ps1"
scp -i /home/marsh-office/.ssh/papercup-vm-win -P 2223 User@127.0.0.1:papercupai/papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/msi/Papercusp_0.0.1_x64_en-US.msi /home/marsh-office/
scp -i /home/marsh-office/.ssh/papercup-vm-win -P 2223 User@127.0.0.1:papercupai/papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/nsis/Papercusp_0.0.1_x64-setup.exe /home/marsh-office/
bin/audit-bundle.sh /home/marsh-office/Papercusp_0.0.1_x64_en-US.msi /home/marsh-office/Papercusp_0.0.1_x64-setup.exe
```

\~30–45 min. The Windows VM has crashed 6+ times during builds in past sessions — **expect to retry**. See [VMs / Windows VM crash recovery](/internal/docs/build-system/vms#windows-vm-crashes-routinely).

### `rebuild-3070` — Rebuild 3070 host

[Section titled “rebuild-3070 — Rebuild 3070 host”](#rebuild-3070--rebuild-3070-host)

Runs `bin/prod` in the papercup repo (`cwd` = the papercup repo). It builds the operator (`npm --workspace @papercusp/web run build` = the `@papercupai/operator-docs` Starlight docs + the `@papercusp/operator-vite` SPA) and restarts the Hono host (`bin/hono-host.ts`) on `:3070`, detached (survives the SSE stream closing). This is **not** the desktop bundle — `:3070` serves the same operator UI/API that the packaged Tauri sidecar runs.

```plaintext
cd /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercup
bin/prod
```

## Running section

[Section titled “Running section”](#running-section)

### `install-linux-deb` — Install + launch Linux .deb

[Section titled “install-linux-deb — Install + launch Linux .deb”](#install-linux-deb--install--launch-linux-deb)

Installs the most-recently-built local `.deb` and launches `papercusp` (the installed binary on `/usr/bin/papercusp`). Requires `NOPASSWD` sudo for `dpkg`.

```plaintext
sudo -n dpkg -i /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercup/papercusp-desktop/.../Papercusp_0.0.1_amd64.deb
setsid /usr/bin/papercusp >/dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null &
```

### `install-mac-dmg` — Install + launch Mac .dmg

[Section titled “install-mac-dmg — Install + launch Mac .dmg”](#install-mac-dmg--install--launch-mac-dmg)

SSH macOS VM → mount the DMG → copy `Papercusp.app` to `/Applications/` → strip Gatekeeper quarantine → `open`. View via SPICE.

```plaintext
hdiutil attach ~/Papercusp_0.0.1_x86_64.dmg
rm -rf /Applications/Papercusp.app
cp -R /Volumes/Papercusp/Papercusp.app /Applications/
hdiutil detach /Volumes/Papercusp
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Papercusp.app
open /Applications/Papercusp.app
```

### `install-windows-msi` — Install + launch Windows .msi

[Section titled “install-windows-msi — Install + launch Windows .msi”](#install-windows-msi--install--launch-windows-msi)

SSH Windows VM → `msiexec /i ... /quiet` → `Start-Process Papercusp.exe`. Installs to `C:\Program Files\Papercusp\`.

### `launch-linux-dev` — Launch Linux Desktop DEV

[Section titled “launch-linux-dev — Launch Linux Desktop DEV”](#launch-linux-dev--launch-linux-desktop-dev)

Detached `npm run dev` in `papercusp-desktop/` (Tauri dev mode against `:3055`). Survives closing the stream. Tails `/tmp/papercusp-desktop-dev.log`. In dev mode the Tauri shell doesn’t spawn the `serve.mjs` sidecar — it expects the operator dev stack (Vite `:3055` + Hono `:3070`) running externally; its `beforeDevCommand` (`bin/dev-operator-ifneeded.sh`) brings that stack up if it isn’t already.

### `restart-3055` — Restart dev stack (3055 + 3070)

[Section titled “restart-3055 — Restart dev stack (3055 + 3070)”](#restart-3055--restart-dev-stack-3055--3070)

Runs `bin/dev` in the papercup repo. This (re)starts **two** systemd `--user` transient units: `papercup-dev` (the **Vite** SPA dev server on `:3055`, `@papercusp/operator-vite`) and `papercup-dev-api` (the Hono API host on `:3070`, `tsx bin/hono-host.ts`). The `/admin` page goes offline for a few seconds while the Hono host re-imports; the Vite side comes back via HMR almost immediately — you’ll lose your SSE log stream and need to refresh.

### `audit-prod-bundles` — Audit prod bundles for PostHog leaks

[Section titled “audit-prod-bundles — Audit prod bundles for PostHog leaks”](#audit-prod-bundles--audit-prod-bundles-for-posthog-leaks)

Standalone re-run of `papercusp-desktop/bin/audit-bundle.sh` against every prod artifact present on disk — the local `.deb`/`.rpm` plus any `.dmg`/`.msi`/`.exe` in `/home/marsh-office/`. Fails (`exit 1`) if no artifacts are found, or if any contains a real PostHog key. See [Privacy audit](/internal/docs/build-system/privacy-audit) for the full contract.

### `env-probe` — Env probe

[Section titled “env-probe — Env probe”](#env-probe--env-probe)

Prints whether key env vars are set (NVM, BUN, COMPOSIO, HINDSIGHT\_API\_URL, ELEVENLABS, CLOUDFLARE, ANTHROPIC, OPENAI). Use this to diagnose “command can’t find X” issues — these are sourced from your `.bashrc` and pass through via `bash -lic`.

## Adding a new command

[Section titled “Adding a new command”](#adding-a-new-command)

Edit `packages/operator-core/lib/admin-commands.ts`. Each entry:

```ts
{
  id: 'my-thing',                  // url-safe, used in /api/admin/run?cmd=
  label: 'Human label',
  section: 'building' | 'running' | 'simulators' | 'packaged-build',
  description: 'What it does + caveats',  // optional
  command: 'set -e; echo hello',   // raw bash, executed via `bash -lic`
  cwd: '/optional/work/dir',       // optional
}
```

After editing, the new card appears immediately — the page fetches the list via `/api/admin/commands` on mount. (The Hono host runs `tsx` with no file-watch, so a `packages/operator-core` edit needs the host to reload — restart `papercup-dev-api` or reload the Tauri shell — before the new command id resolves server-side.)

# Architecture

> How a production Papercusp binary is laid out, what it spawns at startup, and how the browser webview finds the operator server.

History: the operator frontend was Next.js until mid-2026

Next.js is **fully removed** (`finish-next-removal-2026-06-01`): no `next` dependency, no `next.config.js`, no `next/*` shims — the former `next/{navigation,link,dynamic}` adapter hooks live on as `apps/operator/lib/router-compat/*`. The operator frontend is the **Vite** SPA (`@papercusp/operator-vite`, TanStack Router, `:3055` in dev) served by the `:3070` **Hono host** (`apps/operator/bin/hono-host.ts`); the shipped sidecar is an esbuild-bundled `serve.mjs`. `apps/operator/app/**` is **not** dead code — operator-vite imports its live page bodies via the `@` alias (→ `apps/operator/`). See the `operator-next-is-retired` insight.

## Two repos, two stages

[Section titled “Two repos, two stages”](#two-repos-two-stages)

```plaintext
~/papercupai-workspace/
├── papercup/                 ← the operator (Vite SPA + Hono host + libs)
│   ├── apps/operator-vite/   ← @papercusp/operator-vite — the TanStack-Router SPA UI (:3055 dev)
│   └── apps/operator/        ← @papercusp/web — the Hono host (bin/hono-host.ts, :3070), serve entry (bin/serve.ts), + lib/app page bodies
└── papercusp-desktop/        ← the Tauri shell (Rust)
    └── src-tauri/            ← main.rs + tauri.conf.json — produces the .deb/.dmg/.msi
```

`papercusp-desktop` is the wrapper. It bundles the operator as a single esbuild-bundled `serve.mjs` **sidecar** (built by `bin/build-desktop-sidecar.sh` into `src-tauri/sidecar/`) and ships the Rust binary + sidecar in one installer. Per plan `operator-core-headless-serve-2026-06-04`, the desktop is an **embedder of `papercusp serve`**: `serve.mjs` owns the whole operator lifecycle (embedded Postgres, migrations, the Hono host, the discovery files); Rust just spawns it and points the webview at it.

## What a Tauri production build does at startup

[Section titled “What a Tauri production build does at startup”](#what-a-tauri-production-build-does-at-startup)

`papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs` `setup()` (production branch):

1. **Pick a free port hint** (e.g. `19210`) and a separate PG port hint — these are cold-start *hints*; the real ports are resolved later from discovery.
2. **Spawn `code-server`** (the bundled VS Code for the web) on a free port, and surface its URL to the sidecar via `PAPERCUSP_CODE_SERVER_URL`. (Debug builds also start an MCP bridge plugin bound to `127.0.0.1`.)
3. **Spawn the `serve.mjs --ensure` sidecar** as one child process. `serve` then owns everything PG/operator: it starts real embedded PostgreSQL (`wal_level=logical`) on its own free port, runs migrations, writes `~/.papercusp/embedded-pg.json`, runs `runBootstrap()` (which starts the endpoint-IPC server + writes `~/.papercusp/endpoint-ipc.json`), and starts the Hono host bound to `127.0.0.1:<port>`. `--ensure` reuses an already-healthy operator under the same HOME instead of double-booting.
4. **Poll `~/.papercusp/operator.json`** (`wait_for_operator`, up to 120s for a first boot that pays `initdb` + full migration replay) until the pid is alive **and** the port accepts TCP. The **real** port comes from this file — `--ensure` reuse may land on a different port than the cold-start hint.
5. **`eval()` an init script into the webview** setting `window.__papercuspBase` / `window.__papercuspAppBase` / `window.__PAPERCUSP_TAURI__` and dispatching a `papercusp:base` event.

The webview opens on the bootstrap page (`papercusp-desktop/web/index.html`, `frontendDist: "../web"`) that:

1. Waits for `window.__papercuspBase` (re-applied if the page-load drops it)
2. Polls `<base>/api/desktop/preflight` until ready
3. Navigates to the real operator UI

With the `papercusp://` **custom protocol** on (default, shipped 2026-06-01), the real app loads from `papercusp://localhost/…` (forwarded to the loopback sidecar), so the webview opens **zero** HTTP connections. With `PAPERCUSP_DESKTOP_CUSTOM_PROTOCOL=0` it falls back to the HTTP `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` origin. Either way, `/api` fetches + EventSource ride **endpoint-IPC** (resolved from `endpoint-ipc.json`) to escape libsoup’s 6-socket pool, falling back to HTTP if the socket isn’t up. Tauri’s IPC (`invoke()`) works alongside because the page is in a Tauri webview.

## What dev mode does instead

[Section titled “What dev mode does instead”](#what-dev-mode-does-instead)

A debug build (`cfg!(debug_assertions) == true`) makes `main.rs` `setup()`:

1. **Skip the `serve.mjs` spawn entirely** — the developer is expected to run the operator dev stack separately (the Vite SPA on `:3055` + the Hono host on `:3070`)
2. **Start the tauri-agent-tools dev bridge** (debug-only, localhost-only, token-authenticated) and, on Linux, auto-grant `getUserMedia`
3. **Open devtools automatically** (WebKitGTK doesn’t reliably wire Ctrl+Shift+I)
4. Webview loads `http://localhost:3055` (`devUrl` in `tauri.conf.json`); `/api` fetches ride endpoint-IPC re-read from `~/.papercusp/endpoint-ipc.json` (written by the externally-run operator), with graceful HTTP fallback while it’s down

So a dev Tauri window IS just a Tauri webview pointed at the live Vite dev server on `:3055` (with the Hono host on `:3070`). Production is the same UI code but served from the bundled sidecar on a private port. (`papercusp-desktop`’s `beforeDevCommand` runs `bin/dev-operator-ifneeded.sh` to bring the dev stack up if it isn’t already.)

## Where the operator code lives in a prod bundle

[Section titled “Where the operator code lives in a prod bundle”](#where-the-operator-code-lives-in-a-prod-bundle)

After `bin/build-desktop-sidecar.sh` (which esbuild-bundles the operator into `src-tauri/sidecar/`) followed by `tauri build` (`= npm run build` in `papercusp-desktop/` — note `beforeBuildCommand` is empty, so the sidecar build is a **separate** step):

```plaintext
/usr/lib/Papercusp/                          # Linux .deb install root
├── papercusp-desktop                        # main Tauri binary
└── sidecar/                                 # bundled as a Tauri resource (sidecar/**/*)
    ├── serve.mjs                            # one esbuild-bundled ESM operator entry — main.rs spawns `node serve.mjs --ensure`
    ├── db-sql/                              # bundled SQL migration files
    ├── node_modules/                        # externalized native deps only (node-pty, @papercusp/embedded-postgres-server + its @embedded-postgres/<plat> binary, …)
    ├── code-server/                         # the bundled code-server
    └── bin/
        ├── node                             # bundled Node v24 runtime (Tauri prepends bin/ to the sidecar's PATH)
        ├── omp
        └── gh
```

Embedded Postgres is no longer a separate sidecar directory — `serve.mjs` resolves the `@papercusp/embedded-postgres-server` package (with its platform binary) out of `sidecar/node_modules/` and runs PG in-process. `zero-cache` is **not** shipped (the desktop sidecar serves SSE itself; the opt-in `zero-cache-server` was removed 2026-05-07). Mac is the same shape inside `Papercusp.app/Contents/Resources/`. Windows under `C:\Program Files\Papercusp\` (where the sidecar is routed through WSL).

## The bundled Node binary (`bundled_path_env`)

[Section titled “The bundled Node binary (bundled\_path\_env)”](#the-bundled-node-binary-bundled_path_env)

`main.rs` has a `bundled_path_env()` helper that builds a `PATH` with the shipped `sidecar/bin/` directory (containing `node`, `omp`, `gh`) prepended. **Every node-based spawn runs through it** rather than relying on `which node`, because GUI-launched apps inherit `$PATH = /usr/bin:/bin` on macOS — Homebrew’s `node`, `nvm` Node, etc. won’t be visible. Without this, the packaged process can’t find `node` at all (the Linux clean-room test VM caught exactly this — see [VMs](/internal/docs/build-system/vms)), and `pg_dump`/`libpq` discovery would break on Mac.

## The embedded-PG discovery file

[Section titled “The embedded-PG discovery file”](#the-embedded-pg-discovery-file)

On boot, **`serve.mjs`** (not `main.rs` anymore) writes `~/.papercusp/embedded-pg.json` containing roughly:

```json
{
  "pid": 877130,
  "adminUrl": "postgresql://harness_admin:...@127.0.0.1:20721/papercusp",
  "appUrl":   "postgresql://harness_app:...@127.0.0.1:20721/papercusp",
  "port": 20721,
  "startedAt": "2026-05-13T12:56:00Z"
}
```

It also writes `~/.papercusp/operator.json` (the Hono host pid + port that `main.rs` polls) and `~/.papercusp/endpoint-ipc.json` (the IPC socket path).

Three rules:

* The operator reads PG discovery via `getHarnessAdminUrl()` in `packages/operator-core/lib/embedded-pg-discovery.ts`. **Never hard-code `:5432` or `:16534` anywhere** — always resolve through this helper. The central connection resolver in `libs/papercusp/libs/db/src/connection.ts` already does this; new code should call the helper.
* The discovery files are **owned by `serve`**: it writes them atomically on boot and removes `operator.json`/`embedded-pg.json` on the way down. `serve --ensure` also makes same-HOME double-launches converge on one operator rather than fighting over the file.
* Native PG (`:5432`) is for Restart / paperclip / marketplace **and** is what this dev box’s operator runs against (`apps/operator/.env.local` pins a `:5432/papercusp` `DATABASE_URL`). The **ship** target is embedded-pg, but on the standing dev box there is **no** `papercusp_legacy`/`papercusp_native_backup` rename — `papercusp` on `:5432` is alive and in use. Code must keep working under embedded-pg regardless, so resolve through `getHarnessAdminUrl()` rather than assuming either topology.

## What gets *built* vs. what gets *shipped*

[Section titled “What gets built vs. what gets shipped”](#what-gets-built-vs-what-gets-shipped)

* **Built** but **not shipped**: the Vite SPA’s intermediate output, `target/debug/`, `node_modules/.cache/`. The auditor (`papercusp-desktop/bin/audit-bundle.sh`) scans the *installer* contents, not the build directory.
* **Built and shipped** but **not loaded at runtime in prod**: `web/index.html` only runs during the brief bootstrap; `tauri.conf.json`’s `devUrl` is dev-only and never read in a release binary.
* **Built and shipped and active**: everything under `sidecar/`. `serve.mjs` is spawned at boot (and owns embedded PG in-process); `code-server` is spawned alongside it; both run for the lifetime of the Tauri window.

## A note on Linux WebKit quirks

[Section titled “A note on Linux WebKit quirks”](#a-note-on-linux-webkit-quirks)

WebKitGTK is what wry uses on Linux, and it has a few recurring quirks the desktop works around:

* **`localhost` vs `127.0.0.1`** — WebKitGTK may resolve `localhost` to `::1` while the sidecar binds IPv4 loopback, which fails the bootstrap’s preflight fetch. `main.rs` deliberately hands the webview a `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` base, not `localhost`.
* **libsoup’s 6-socket pool** — the webview’s `/api` fetch + EventSource are routed over endpoint-IPC (Unix socket) instead of HTTP precisely to escape this limit. See the discovery-file handoff above.
* **getUserMedia denied by default** — `main.rs` auto-grants media permission on Linux so the operator’s voice / wake-word / ElevenLabs paths work without a `NotAllowedError`.

> Historical note: the old “duplicate dashboard” + “access control checks CORS spam” bugs were Next.js-era artifacts (a Next error overlay double-mounting the layout, and wildcard CORS headers in `next.config.js`). Both that machinery and `next.config.js` are gone now that the operator is a Vite SPA served by the Hono host, so those specific fixes no longer apply.

# TypeScript Layers

> The four-layer model the operator is migrating toward — core / host / routes / client — and the empty tsconfig scaffold under apps/operator/layers/ that names them.

## What this is

[Section titled “What this is”](#what-this-is)

`apps/operator/` will eventually be partitioned into four compile units. Each one is a tsconfig with its own `include` glob, and the layers reference each other in a one-directional dependency graph. The build invariant is: nothing in `core` can import from `host`, `routes`, or `client`; nothing in `host` can import from `routes` or `client`; etc.

Today the partition is **scaffolded but empty**. The four layer tsconfigs exist under `apps/operator/layers/` with `include: []`. `tsc --build apps/operator/layers/tsconfig.layers.json` resolves cleanly but checks no files. Files migrate into a layer’s `include` glob as the route-migration work (Phase 4) and the layering-enforcement work (Phase 6b) progress.

This is by design — the alternative was to globs-up the existing tree and lie about which files belong where. The layers describe the **target**, not the current state.

## The four layers

[Section titled “The four layers”](#the-four-layers)

```plaintext
                  ┌─────────┐
                  │  core   │
                  └────┬────┘
                       │
        ┌──────────────┼─────────────┐
        ▼              ▼             ▼
   ┌─────────┐   ┌──────────┐   ┌─────────┐
   │  host   │   │  client  │   │ routes  │
   └────┬────┘   └──────────┘   └────┬────┘
        │                            │
        └────────► routes ◄──────────┘
                  (via host)
```

### core

[Section titled “core”](#core)

**What lives here:** typed business logic with no host coupling. `define_tool` handlers (the host-clean ones), the endpoint system’s pipeline + dispatch stack, schemas, pure helpers, type definitions.

**What may be imported:** anything from `libs/*`, `packages/*`, and host-clean third-party packages (`zod`, `date-fns`, `postgres`, `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, etc.).

**What may NOT be imported:**

* `next/*`
* `node:fs`, `node:child_process` directly (use `@papercusp/host-platform` instead)
* DOM types implicitly
* React

If you find yourself wanting to reach for `node:fs` in core code, the answer is to take a `HostPlatform` parameter (or call `getHostPlatform()`) — see [host-platform](/internal/docs/build-system/architecture) coverage in the host-platform package source.

### host

[Section titled “host”](#host)

**What lives here:** host-specific glue that the desktop needs but a future web host might not. `desktopHostPlatform`’s body, IPC bridge code (`packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-ipc/`), embedded-PG discovery, plugin runtime (`packages/operator-core/lib/plugin-host-runtime.ts`), FS watchers, background sweepers, socket lifecycle.

**What may be imported:** `core`, anything in `libs/*` and `packages/*`, Node stdlib (`node:fs`, `node:child_process`, `node:net`, etc.).

**What may NOT be imported:** `next/*` (Next-specific request/response shapes); React.

### routes

[Section titled “routes”](#routes)

**What lives here:** transport-shaped code — Next route handlers (`app/api/.../route.ts`) and Hono routers (`app/api/_hono/*.ts`). Thin shims that map an HTTP request into a `core` or `host` function call.

**What may be imported:** `core`, `host`, `next/*` (`NextRequest`, `cookies()`, etc.), Hono types.

**What may NOT be imported:** React; client-only browser APIs.

A handler that holds non-transport state (cookies, cost caps, feature locks, transcript persistence) is A1-class — it stays as a substantive shim and doesn’t migrate to a `define_tool` projection. See [agent-policies §endpoint-system migration](/internal/docs/agent-policies) for the audit axes.

### client

[Section titled “client”](#client)

**What lives here:** React components, hooks, transport-adapter polyfills (`packages/operator-core/lib/transport-adapters/`), Zero client wiring, client-side state.

**What may be imported:** `core`, `react`, `next/link`, `next/navigation` (client APIs), DOM types, browser-only third-party packages.

**What may NOT be imported:**

* `node:fs`, `node:child_process` (server-only)
* `next/headers`, `cookies()` (server-only)
* Database clients (`postgres`, drizzle)
* Anything in `host` (the client doesn’t run on the host)

## How to run the layered build

[Section titled “How to run the layered build”](#how-to-run-the-layered-build)

```bash
npx tsc --build apps/operator/layers/tsconfig.layers.json
```

Exit code 0 with no output means all four layers’ include globs resolved + every cross-layer reference is satisfied. Today this trivially succeeds because every `include` is empty.

When files start moving in (Phase 4, Phase 6b), the build will start checking them and a violation — say, a file in `client/include` importing `host/some-thing` — will surface as a `tsc --build` error.

## What this scaffold doesn’t do (yet)

[Section titled “What this scaffold doesn’t do (yet)”](#what-this-scaffold-doesnt-do-yet)

* **No enforcement.** Phase 6a (this) ships the structural slots. Phase 6b adds ESLint `no-restricted-imports` rules + dependency-cruiser; that lands once Phase 4 has disentangled routes from `core` enough that the rules wouldn’t be a wall of red.
* **No code moves.** The four `include` arrays are `[]`. Files migrate in by per-handler audit, not en masse.
* **No replacement of Next’s tsconfig.** `apps/operator/tsconfig.json` is what Next + the IDE consume; it’s untouched. The layered build is a parallel surface that runs independently.

## How a file gets added to a layer

[Section titled “How a file gets added to a layer”](#how-a-file-gets-added-to-a-layer)

When a route migration (Phase 4) determines that a handler is host-clean and projectable, the worker:

1. Moves the handler file to its target location (often `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/<feature>/<name>.ts`).
2. Adds the file’s path to the appropriate layer’s `include` glob in `apps/operator/layers/tsconfig.core.json` (or `host.json`, etc.).
3. Runs `tsc --build apps/operator/layers/tsconfig.layers.json` locally; addresses any reported violations before committing.

The first few migrations will likely uncover edge cases (DOM types leaking into core via a stale .d.ts, a tsbuildinfo path that needs gitignoring, etc.). Those get fixed as found; the scaffold’s job is to make the violation visible early instead of letting it ship.

## When to revisit

[Section titled “When to revisit”](#when-to-revisit)

When ≥75% of `app/api/*/route.ts` files have been audited (Phase 4 milestone), or when an enforcement violation appears that the scaffold should have caught — whichever comes first. At that point Phase 6b adds the ESLint rules + builds fail on cross-layer imports.

Sister doc: the [host-platform](https://github.com/papercusp/papercusp/tree/main/libs/host-platform) interface that `core` and `host` share, and [agent-policies §endpoint-system migration](/internal/docs/agent-policies) for the per-route audit rules.

# Privacy audit (PostHog leak scanner)

> The V1 ship contract, how bin/audit-bundle.sh enforces it, and how to extend it for future leak categories.

## The V1 contract

[Section titled “The V1 contract”](#the-v1-contract)

A freshly installed production binary must:

1. Make **zero network requests** to `flags.papercuspai.com` under any usage.
2. Resolve every feature flag to its `FLAG_DEFAULTS` ship value with `source: "defaults"` — i.e. PostHog must not be configured. (The defaults are the V1 ship state: `papercusp-snapshots` is `true` by design; cloudflare-publish / oracle / harness-phases / design / rust-port-ui / testing / the-hive / video / voice / improvement-auto-implement / inbox-durable-escalations are all `false`.)

Both must hold without anyone configuring anything post-install.

## How the system already enforces it

[Section titled “How the system already enforces it”](#how-the-system-already-enforces-it)

`packages/operator-core/lib/posthog-config.ts` resolves the active PostHog configuration in this priority order:

1. **Env vars** — `PAPERCUSP_POSTHOG_HOST`, `PAPERCUSP_POSTHOG_KEY`, `PAPERCUSP_POSTHOG_PERSONAL_KEY`, `PAPERCUSP_POSTHOG_TESTING_FEATURES`
2. **Discovery file** — `~/.papercusp/posthog.json` (and `~/.papercusp/posthog-personal.json` for the personal API key)
3. **Default** — testing-features disabled → the `/api/flags/bootstrap` layer returns `source: "defaults"`

`packages/operator-core/lib/flag-bus.ts` only initializes the PostHog client when `isTestingFeaturesEnabled() === true`. So on a clean install (no env vars, no discovery files), the PostHog SDK never starts. **Zero network requests by construction.**

`libs/flags/src/types.ts` exports `FLAG_DEFAULTS` with every flag defaulting `false`. These are baked into the bundle. On a clean install they are the values returned.

## What the auditor scans for

[Section titled “What the auditor scans for”](#what-the-auditor-scans-for)

`papercusp-desktop/bin/audit-bundle.sh` **FAILs** an artifact only if it contains a real PostHog secret — a `phx_` or `phc_` key followed by 30+ alphanumeric/underscore chars:

```plaintext
phx_[A-Za-z0-9_]{30,}
phc_[A-Za-z0-9_]{30,}
```

These are `REGEX_NEEDLES`. Placeholders like `phx_xxx` or path/prose references (`posthog.json`, `PAPERCUSP_POSTHOG_KEY`) deliberately do **not** match — earlier versions used those literal strings as needles and false-positived on source/docs/code, so the literal `NEEDLES` array is now empty.

It also has **soft `WARN_NEEDLES`** that surface (but do *not* fail) when the browser SDK is in the bundle:

```plaintext
node_modules/posthog-js/
posthog-js@
```

`posthog-js` is dynamic-imported only when the user opts into telemetry (default off), so its presence isn’t a leak per se — but a hostile fork could strip the opt-in gate, so it’s worth flagging. WARN, not FAIL.

Documentation paths (`content/docs`, `*.mdx`, `*.md`, `*.rsc`, prerendered `app/docs/*.html`) are excluded from the FAIL scan via an `exclude_re` so legitimate prose mentions of the needles don’t trip it.

## Supported artifact formats

[Section titled “Supported artifact formats”](#supported-artifact-formats)

```plaintext
.deb         → dpkg-deb -x
.rpm         → rpm2cpio | cpio -idm  (falls back to 7z)
.dmg         → hdiutil attach  (on Linux: 7z)
.msi         → 7z x
.exe (NSIS)  → 7z x
.AppImage    → ./Artifact --appimage-extract
directory    → copied + scanned in place (useful for an unpacked Papercusp.app or the sidecar/ dir)
```

If `7z` (or `hdiutil`/`rpm2cpio`) isn’t available for a given format, the script WARNs and scans the artifact as a raw binary blob instead. Extraction goes into a `mktemp -d` and is `rm -rf`’d on exit.

## Usage

[Section titled “Usage”](#usage)

```sh
bin/audit-bundle.sh path/to/Papercusp_0.0.1_amd64.deb
bin/audit-bundle.sh /home/marsh-office/Papercusp_0.0.1_x86_64.dmg \
                    /home/marsh-office/Papercusp_0.0.1_x64_en-US.msi \
                    /home/marsh-office/Papercusp_0.0.1_x64-setup.exe
```

Exit codes:

* `0` — all clean (`OK: N/N artifacts clean`)
* `1` — at least one artifact had a match
* `2` — usage error

## /admin integration

[Section titled “/admin integration”](#admin-integration)

Three integration points:

1. **Inside each prod-build command** (Linux, Mac, Windows): the build script runs the auditor on its own output before declaring success. A bundled leak fails the build.
2. **Standalone “Audit prod bundles for PostHog leaks” card** — re-runs against the local `papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/{deb,rpm}` artifacts plus any `.dmg`/`.msi`/`.exe` in `/home/marsh-office/`.
3. **CI-equivalent local check** — `papercusp-desktop/bin/audit-bundle.sh` can be called from any context; consider adding it to a pre-release script if/when one exists.

## Verified-clean status (2026-05-13)

[Section titled “Verified-clean status (2026-05-13)”](#verified-clean-status-2026-05-13)

All four currently-built artifacts pass:

```plaintext
Papercusp_0.0.1_amd64.deb       (700 MB)  OK
Papercusp_0.0.1_x86_64.dmg      (460 MB)  OK
Papercusp_0.0.1_x64_en-US.msi   (375 MB)  OK
Papercusp_0.0.1_x64-setup.exe   (268 MB)  OK
```

## Extending the scanner

[Section titled “Extending the scanner”](#extending-the-scanner)

If a new “must not ship in prod” secret pattern is identified, edit `papercusp-desktop/bin/audit-bundle.sh`. Prefer a **regex** that matches only the real secret (long random suffix), not a placeholder or path reference:

```sh
REGEX_NEEDLES=(
  'phx_[A-Za-z0-9_]{30,}'
  'phc_[A-Za-z0-9_]{30,}'
  # add new secret-shaped patterns here
)
```

For a literal-string match, add to the (currently empty) `NEEDLES` array — but be careful: literal needles like `posthog.json` false-positive on source/docs/code, which is exactly why they were removed. For a “this code is present but gated” signal that should surface without failing the build, add to `WARN_NEEDLES`. Then run the standalone audit card to verify existing artifacts before declaring the new policy enforced.

## Why this isn’t an AST / behavioral scan

[Section titled “Why this isn’t an AST / behavioral scan”](#why-this-isnt-an-ast--behavioral-scan)

The bundles are gigabytes of compiled JS, minified output, native binaries, postgres data files, etc. A `grep -rlF`/`grep -rlE` over the extracted tree is fast (\~5–10s per artifact). The auditor uses **regex** needles tuned to match only real secrets (a `phx_`/`phc_` key with a long random suffix) so it doesn’t false-positive on placeholders or prose — rather than parsing the JS, which would be slow and brittle against minification.

## What the auditor does NOT catch

[Section titled “What the auditor does NOT catch”](#what-the-auditor-does-not-catch)

* **Behavioral leaks**: code that hardcodes `flags.papercuspai.com` and calls `fetch()` regardless of `isTestingFeaturesEnabled()`. The auditor scans for embedded *secrets*, not for the SDK’s runtime behavior. Defense: the build chain validates `flag-bus.ts`’s gating discipline; no code outside that file should touch PostHog endpoints.
* **Same-host PostHog instance accidentally pointing prod traffic somewhere it shouldn’t**. Defense: see the V1 contract — even with a wrong host, the client must not start.
* **Telemetry from other sources** (Tauri’s auto-update, OS crash reporters). These are separate trust decisions documented elsewhere.

If you need to validate behavioral guarantees, see [verification](/internal/docs/build-system/verification) — that page covers the live-run smoke test (`curl /api/flags/bootstrap`, `ss -tnp | grep flags.papercuspai`) that catches behavioral leaks.

# Verifying a build

> How to smoke-test each platform end-to-end before declaring the artifact good to ship.

## Pre-flight check (any platform)

[Section titled “Pre-flight check (any platform)”](#pre-flight-check-any-platform)

Re-run the auditor on every artifact:

```sh
papercusp-desktop/bin/audit-bundle.sh \
  papercupai-workspace/papercup/papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/deb/Papercusp_0.0.1_amd64.deb \
  /home/marsh-office/Papercusp_0.0.1_x86_64.dmg \
  /home/marsh-office/Papercusp_0.0.1_x64_en-US.msi \
  /home/marsh-office/Papercusp_0.0.1_x64-setup.exe
```

Or click **Audit prod bundles for PostHog leaks** in `/admin`. Should print `OK: 4/4`. If any FAIL, **stop** — the artifact must not ship.

***

## Linux .deb verification

[Section titled “Linux .deb verification”](#linux-deb-verification)

### 1. Install + launch

[Section titled “1. Install + launch”](#1-install--launch)

```sh
sudo dpkg -i papercupai-workspace/papercup/papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/deb/Papercusp_0.0.1_amd64.deb
papercusp
```

Or click **Install + launch Linux .deb** in `/admin`.

Expected: a brief bootstrap page, then the window navigates to the operator UI within \~5–15s (a first boot pays `initdb` + migrations inside `serve.mjs`, so allow longer). Title bar “Papercusp”. If it stays stuck on the bootstrap page, the sidecar never reached the preflight-ready state → check the serve logs.

### 2. Verify no discovery files leaked

[Section titled “2. Verify no discovery files leaked”](#2-verify-no-discovery-files-leaked)

```sh
sudo useradd -m papercusp-verify
sudo -u papercusp-verify ls -la ~papercusp-verify/.papercusp/ 2>&1
```

Expected: `No such file or directory`. The bundle never created the file.

### 3. Flag bootstrap silent

[Section titled “3. Flag bootstrap silent”](#3-flag-bootstrap-silent)

```sh
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3055/api/flags/bootstrap | jq
```

Wait — the prod binary doesn’t serve on `:3055`. The sidecar (`node serve.mjs`) picks a free port, which it records in `~/.papercusp/operator.json` (the authoritative source). Read it from there, or grep the listener.

```sh
PROD_PORT=$(jq -r .port ~/.papercusp/operator.json)
# Fallback if operator.json isn't present:
# PROD_PORT=$(ss -tnlp | awk '/serve\.mjs|node/{split($4,a,":"); print a[2]}' | sort -u | grep -v 3055 | head -1)
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:${PROD_PORT}/api/flags/bootstrap | jq
```

Expected (the V1 ship defaults — `papercusp-snapshots` is `true` by design, every other flag `false`):

```json
{
  "flags": {
    "papercusp-snapshots": true,
    "papercusp-cloudflare-publish": false,
    "papercusp-oracle": false,
    "papercusp-rust-port-ui": false,
    "papercusp-harness-phases": false,
    "papercusp-design": false,
    "papercusp-testing": false,
    "papercusp-inbox-durable-escalations": false,
    "papercusp-improvement-auto-implement": false,
    "papercusp-video-channels": false,
    "papercusp-voice-channels": false,
    "papercusp-the-hive": false
  },
  "evaluatedAt": 1234567890,
  "source": "defaults"
}
```

`source` must be `"defaults"` (the only other values are `"posthog"` and `"override"`). A `"posthog"` source on a clean install means PostHog config leaked in. The flag *values* must match `FLAG_DEFAULTS` in `libs/flags/src/types.ts` (snapshots on; everything else off). (`papercusp-templates` / `papercusp-marketplace` were retired — distribution lives in the ungated Cupboard.)

### 4. No outbound PostHog traffic

[Section titled “4. No outbound PostHog traffic”](#4-no-outbound-posthog-traffic)

```sh
sudo ss -tnp | grep -E "flags.papercuspai|posthog"
```

Expected: empty.

### 5. Embedded PG discovery

[Section titled “5. Embedded PG discovery”](#5-embedded-pg-discovery)

```sh
cat ~/.papercusp/embedded-pg.json
cat ~/.papercusp/operator.json
```

Expected: JSON with a non-5432 port (both files written by `serve.mjs`). **Confirms the desktop spawned its own embedded PG, didn’t talk to native `:5432`.**

### 6. Feature data loads

[Section titled “6. Feature data loads”](#6-feature-data-loads)

In the app, navigate to **Harness → sheets**. The Feature Queue panel should populate with features (not empty). No errors in the DevTools console.

### 7. Closed-flag routes really 404

[Section titled “7. Closed-flag routes really 404”](#7-closed-flag-routes-really-404)

```sh
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:${PROD_PORT}/design
```

Expected: `404`. The V1 contract requires `notFound()` to return real HTTP 404, not a 200-page-with-404-content.

### 8. Cleanup

[Section titled “8. Cleanup”](#8-cleanup)

```sh
sudo dpkg -r papercusp
sudo userdel -r papercusp-verify
```

## FAIL criteria (any platform)

[Section titled “FAIL criteria (any platform)”](#fail-criteria-any-platform)

| Symptom                                                                              | Means                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| A real PostHog key (`phx_…` / `phc_…`) found by `audit-bundle.sh` inside the install | Secret leaked into bundle — **must** rebuild                                   |
| `/api/flags/bootstrap` returns `source: "posthog"` on a clean install                | PostHog config (env var or discovery file) made it through — leak              |
| Any flag other than `papercusp-snapshots` returns `true`                             | Default ship-state violated — leak                                             |
| `ss -tnp` shows connection to `flags.papercuspai.com`                                | App phoning home in clean-install state — leak                                 |
| Window stuck on the bootstrap page (never navigates off `web/index.html`)            | The sidecar never became ready — check the preflight handshake / serve logs    |
| `embedded-pg.json` / `operator.json` missing, or app connects to `:5432`             | Embedded PG didn’t bootstrap (`serve.mjs` owns this)                           |
| Sheets harness shows 0 features when the API returns features                        | Feature loading broken                                                         |
| Window shows the **dev** server’s app (URL has `:3055`)                              | The webview pointed at the dev server instead of the bundled sidecar — rebuild |

## A self-contained checklist

[Section titled “A self-contained checklist”](#a-self-contained-checklist)

Copy this and run top to bottom:

```sh
# 1. Auditor pass
papercusp-desktop/bin/audit-bundle.sh \
  papercupai-workspace/papercup/papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/deb/Papercusp_0.0.1_amd64.deb \
  /home/marsh-office/Papercusp_0.0.1_x86_64.dmg \
  /home/marsh-office/Papercusp_0.0.1_x64_en-US.msi \
  /home/marsh-office/Papercusp_0.0.1_x64-setup.exe


# 2. Linux install + launch + smoke
sudo dpkg -i papercupai-workspace/papercup/papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/deb/Papercusp_0.0.1_amd64.deb
setsid /usr/bin/papercusp >/dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null &
sleep 15
PORT=$(jq -r .port ~/.papercusp/operator.json)
echo "operator port: $PORT"
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/api/flags/bootstrap" | jq .source       # → "defaults"
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" "http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/design"  # → 404
sudo ss -tnp | grep -E "flags.papercuspai|posthog" || echo "no posthog traffic ✓"


# 3. Cleanup
pkill -KILL papercusp
sudo dpkg -r papercusp
```

When every line is green, the artifact is ship-ready for that platform.

## Inventory

[Section titled “Inventory”](#inventory)

| VM                                           | Host process                                                                        | SSH port      | Display                                       | Inside-VM repo path                              |
| -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| **macOS Sonoma** (x86\_64)                   | `qemu-system-x86_64 ... mac_hdd_ng.img`                                             | `2222`        | SPICE on `127.0.0.1:5930`                     | `~/papercupai/papercusp-desktop`                 |
| **Windows 10**                               | `qemu-system-x86_64 ... win10.img`                                                  | `2223`        | (no SPICE configured; consider RDP if needed) | `C:\Users\User\papercupai\papercusp-desktop`     |
| **Linux test** `clean` (Ubuntu 24.04)        | `qemu-system-x86_64 … run/<name>/overlay.qcow2` (via `scripts/linux-test-vm/vmctl`) | `2224`        | SPICE on `127.0.0.1:5932`                     | n/a — installs the packaged `.deb` (no checkout) |
| **Linux fed** `fed-a`/`fed-b` (Ubuntu 24.04) | same golden image, +2nd NIC on `papercusp-fedbr0` (via `bin/vm-federation.sh`)      | `2225`/`2226` | SPICE `127.0.0.1:5933`/`5934`                 | n/a — two-machine federation testing             |

The **Mac** and **Windows** VMs exist only to *produce* their platform’s Tauri bundle. The **Linux test** VM is different in kind — it *consumes* the built `.deb`, fresh-installing it on a pristine Ubuntu to validate the shipped artifact (and to act as a separate machine for federation testing). Day-to-day operator dev (`:3055`) and Linux builds still run entirely on the host.

## Linux test VM (clean-room: fresh-install + federation)

[Section titled “Linux test VM (clean-room: fresh-install + federation)”](#linux-test-vm-clean-room-fresh-install--federation)

Unlike the build VMs, this is a **disposable Ubuntu 24.04 clean-room** for testing the packaged `.deb` in true isolation — driven by **`papercusp-desktop/scripts/linux-test-vm/vmctl`**, not a hand-rolled boot script. It exists for (1) **fresh-install testing** the real `.deb` on a pristine machine, and (2) acting as a **separate machine** for shared-harness / federation testing. Plan: `linux-test-vm-and-federation-2026-06-04`.

* **Scripts (versioned):** `papercusp-desktop/scripts/linux-test-vm/` — `vmctl`, `boot-vm.sh`, `cloud-init/`, `lib/common.sh`.
* **Images (outside the repo, never committed):** `~/papercup-linux-test-vm/` — `images/golden.qcow2` + per-instance `run/<name>/overlay.qcow2`. SSH key `~/.ssh/papercup-vm-linux` (auto-generated on first `provision`).
* **Base:** Ubuntu 24.04 cloud image + a *minimal X stack* (openbox via getty-autologin + `startx`) — deliberately **not** GNOME (which fails to register its session on the qxl GPU) and with **no** preinstalled webkit, so `apt install ./Papercusp.deb` pulls the WebKitGTK runtime from scratch (a truer fresh install).

```sh
cd papercusp-desktop/scripts/linux-test-vm
./vmctl provision            # one-time: build the golden image (~10–15 min)
./vmctl up clean             # boot a pristine overlay
./vmctl install clean        # scp newest .deb in + apt install (the fresh-install test)
./vmctl verify clean         # assert deps/PG/operator/window + screenshot → PASS/FAIL
./vmctl gui clean            # (run yourself) open a SPICE viewer to click around
./vmctl reset clean          # wipe back to a pristine overlay
./vmctl down clean           # power off
```

`install` defaults to the newest `src-tauri/target/release/bundle/deb/Papercusp_*_amd64.deb` (pass a path to override). `verify` checks: package installs, binary `ldd`-resolves, app process up, embedded Postgres running, operator responds **on its dynamic port** (parsed from the app log — *not* a fixed `:3070`), and captures a window screenshot via the qemu monitor (`screendump`). Artifacts land in `run/<name>/verify/`. Tunables: `PAPERCUSP_TESTVM_RAM_MB`, `PAPERCUSP_TESTVM_CPUS`, `PAPERCUSP_TESTVM_DISK`, `PAPERCUSP_TESTVM_HOME`.

**It earns its keep.** The first fresh-install run caught that the shipped `.deb` had **no database** on a clean machine: `spawn_embedded_postgres_server` / `spawn_zero_cache_server` (`src-tauri/src/main.rs`) used a bare `Command::new("node")` while the packaged process PATH has no `node` — fixed by routing them through the bundled-node PATH like `spawn_sidecar` does. The dev box hides this because it always has `node` on PATH, which is exactly why a clean VM is necessary. (Plan decision D-009.)

### Two-machine federation (Phase 2)

[Section titled “Two-machine federation (Phase 2)”](#two-machine-federation-phase-2)

The same VMs double as **separate machines** for cross-machine federation testing — proving the packaged `.deb` federates (a write on one machine lands in the other’s PG) over a real OS + real network hop, not just loopback. Driven by **`papercusp-desktop/bin/vm-federation.sh`**, which reuses the one-box smokes’ assertion core (`bin/lib/federation-asserts.sh`, D-003) over an SSH driver.

```sh
cd papercusp-desktop
bin/vm-federation.sh --vms=2 --dht=testnet --net=bridge   # primary: fed-a ↔ fed-b
bin/vm-federation.sh --vms=1                               # host instance ↔ fed-a VM
bin/vm-federation.sh --vms=2 --net=socket                 # rootless (no sudo) fallback
bin/vm-federation.sh --vms=2 --no-reset --skip-install    # fast iteration (reuse overlays)
```

* **Network (D-016):** every fed VM keeps its slirp NIC (internet/SSH/SPICE) and gets a **second** NIC on host bridge `papercusp-fedbr0` (`10.77.0.0/24`, host `10.77.0.1`) with a static guest IP — no dnsmasq/NAT. The host runs a `hyperdht/testnet` advertised on the bridge IP; both VMs set `PAPERCUSP_DHT_BOOTSTRAP` to it → deterministic discovery over a real hop. `--net=socket` is a rootless dual-NIC fallback (qemu socket L2, exactly two VMs).
* **Identities:** `papercupai` / `aviynw` via per-instance `GH_TOKEN` (resolved by `gh-token.ts`); `gh` + `postgresql-client` are apt-installed in each VM as driver prereqs.
* **Up-front `.deb` gate (P-011):** a static grep of the packaged `serve.mjs` (the sidecar boot entry; `host.mjs` is retired) asserts it carries `PAPERCUSP_DHT_BOOTSTRAP` support + `[swarm]` logs (landed 2026-06-02), failing fast on an older `.deb` that would silently use the public DHT.

**Status (verified 2026-06-07, unattended runs on a current `.deb`):** the harness proves everything up to the holepunch boundary in **both modes** — `--vms=2` *and* `--vms=1` reach fresh-install, clean embedded-PG boot on a fresh `initdb`, write-free share (`state:"booted"` both sides), and **cross-machine swarm-join** (both identities announcing on the same topic + DHT). Neither reaches the bidirectional merge, and the boundary is now fully classified: hyperdht **holepunch does not complete between any two endpoints on ONE physical host** — VM↔VM *and* host↔VM both sit at `conns=0` in raw-hyperswarm tests (same topic, same bridge-advertised bootstrap, working UDP both directions), so neither the single-NIC+NAT candidate nor the host’s no-NAT network position rescues it (plan D-017/D-018). `--dht=public` (P-012) is **INCONCLUSIVE** by same-host NAT hairpin, per the plan’s D-004 best-effort caveat — though both peers do announce on the real public DHT through slirp.

The full bidirectional-merge acceptance needs **truly separate machines** — and that gate was **discharged on Hetzner (2026-06-08, plan D-019)**: the Tier-3 p2p-perf suite on two separate Hetzner cpx31 VMs over the public DHT got `peer_connected` on both peers, cross-region append→visible p95 = 950.5 ms, and a real NAT holepunch (`punches=1 relaySuccess=0`) — positively confirming the single-host `conns=0` wall is a topology artifact (no second physical box needed; the cloud-deployment layer provides the separate machines on-demand). It was further confirmed **cross-region** (ash↔hil, D-020: append→visible p95 = 1115.5 ms over real transcontinental WAN) and — via `bin/deb-hetzner-federation.sh` — for the **shipped `.deb` itself** (D-021: two Hetzner VMs, the `.deb`’s headless sidecar, `peer_connected` + bidirectional `origin=remote` merge over the public DHT). The finding, the clean-machine traps the harness flushed out (slirp-subnet, embedded-PG boot race, the sidecar port-grep race, embedded-pg-refuses-root, and the bundled `pgvector` needing the 24.04 toolchain), and the Hetzner discharge are in the agent-insight [VM federation harness](/internal/docs/agent-insights/vm-federation-separate-machine-proof).
