## Disk discipline

[Section titled “Disk discipline”](#disk-discipline)

Tauri builds are huge. A clean Mac build typically consumes:

* \~5 GB Rust target dir (`papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/target/release/`)
* \~3 GB npm cache (`~/Library/Caches/`)
* \~1.5 GB built node\_modules
* \~500 MB intermediate `.dmg` staging
* \~10 GB Xcode CoreSimulator runtimes (if you build iOS at all)

**Pre-build check** the user reflexively runs: `df -h /` on each VM. If `<10 GB` free, clean up before kicking off a build — mid-build ENOSPC is a hard failure and leaves a broken-half state.

The macOS VM has been on the verge of full multiple times. Safe deletes when desperate:

```sh
# iOS simulator runtimes (recreatable in Xcode → Settings → Platforms)
rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Devices/*    # device instances only
# spm cache
rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/SourcePackages/
# Rust target (forces clean rebuild but reclaims ~3-5 GB)
rm -rf ~/papercupai/papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/target
```

The Linux host (\~40-50 GB free typical) doesn’t hit ENOSPC during builds but the Rust target dir there does grow to \~5 GB.

## Node version pinning

[Section titled “Node version pinning”](#node-version-pinning)

Both VMs run **nvm + Node 22** for the build-time `npm install` + `tauri build`. (This is separate from the *bundled* runtime that ships inside the artifact — `bin/build-desktop-sidecar.sh` vendors Node **v24** into `sidecar/bin/node`.) Node 20 hangs / errors during `npm install`.

```sh
# In either VM:
nvm install 22       # one-time
nvm use 22           # every shell
```

The `build-mac-prod` and `build-windows-prod` `/admin` commands source `nvm` and pin Node 22 explicitly. If you SSH in manually, don’t forget `nvm use 22`.

## npm `--legacy-peer-deps` is required

[Section titled “npm --legacy-peer-deps is required”](#npm---legacy-peer-deps-is-required)

The workspace’s peer-dep tree has unresolvable conflicts that make `npm install` hang **silently with 0% CPU** in modern npm. **Always pass `--legacy-peer-deps`** for installs done in the build context. The /admin scripts do this; if you do manual installs in either VM, you must too.

## Mac VM environment quirks

[Section titled “Mac VM environment quirks”](#mac-vm-environment-quirks)

* **Bundled-Node PATH**: GUI-launched apps on macOS inherit `$PATH = /usr/bin:/bin` — Homebrew Node, nvm Node, brew-installed `pg_dump` / `libpq` are all invisible. `main.rs:bundled_path_env()` builds a `PATH` with the shipped `sidecar/bin/` (node/omp/gh) prepended, and every node-based spawn (the `serve.mjs` sidecar + `code-server`) runs through it. **If you add a new spawn**, route it through the same helper.
* **Gatekeeper**: the DMG is unsigned. First launch will be blocked. The install-mac-dmg `/admin` command strips quarantine via `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Papercusp.app`. If launching by hand, you’ll need to do this too.

## Windows VM crashes routinely

[Section titled “Windows VM crashes routinely”](#windows-vm-crashes-routinely)

The Windows VM crashed **6+ times during a single build session** (2026-05-13). Symptoms: SSH hangs indefinitely, `qemu-system-x86_64` process disappears, `/tmp/win-boot.log` last line is a kernel power error.

**Recovery procedure** (this happens often enough it’s worth automating; for now do it manually):

```sh
# Verify dead
ps -ef | grep -v grep | grep "qemu.*win10\|qemu.*windows"   # → should be empty


# Restart
cd ~/win10-vm && nohup bash boot.sh > /tmp/win-boot.log 2>&1 &


# Wait ~90s
sleep 90 && ssh -i ~/.ssh/papercup-vm-win -p 2223 User@127.0.0.1 'echo ok'


# Re-run the build (it'll resume from incremental Rust cache if not corrupted)
```

The Rust target dir in the Windows VM survives crashes — it’s qcow2 + AHCI writeback so a few seconds of write-back data may be lost, but cargo’s atomic incremental graph handles this gracefully.

If a build was mid-`tauri build` when the VM crashed, you may need to delete and recreate `C:\Users\User\papercusp-desktop\src-tauri\binaries\embedded-postgres-server-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe` — `tauri-bundler` doesn’t always recover cleanly from in-place sidecar binary writes when the process disappears mid-write. Symptom: `failed to remove symlink ... os error 5`.

## Why builds don’t run in containers

[Section titled “Why builds don’t run in containers”](#why-builds-dont-run-in-containers)

The Tauri team’s MSI tooling (`wix`) requires Windows, and Apple’s code-signing tooling requires macOS. We don’t currently sign builds (the audit pipeline assumes unsigned binaries) but the Mac build does need to be a Darwin host for `cargo` to cross-compile to `x86_64-apple-darwin`. So the VMs aren’t replaceable by Linux containers without a substantial cross-compile setup.

## Build cancellation

[Section titled “Build cancellation”](#build-cancellation)

The `/admin` build commands run via `bash -lic`. Closing the SSE stream (Stop button or browser close) sends `SIGTERM` to the whole process group — which cleanly terminates the local `npm` and `tauri build` invocations on the host, but the SSH-driven Mac/Windows builds **continue running inside the VM** even after SIGTERM kills the SSH client. To actually cancel a Mac/Windows build mid-flight, SSH in separately and `pkill -f "tauri build\|cargo"`.

# Data Sync overview

> How harness UI panels read from Postgres in real time via Zero + RichGrid.

Zero is being retired — historical reference

Zero / zero-cache / ZQL named-queries / WebSocket push is **on the retirement path**. The shipping desktop app uses **SSE-primary** sync (the `:3070` Hono host pushes invalidate/update over Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY`); zero-cache is **not run** on desktop. Treat this page as historical reference. Source of truth: `apps/operator/providers/HarnessZeroProvider.tsx` (transport-selection doc-comment) + the root `CLAUDE.md` deployment-model section.

Default to the data-sync library, not a fresh poll

**For any new component that reads server state, default to `useSyncQuery({queryName, args})` from `@papercusp/sync`.** Don’t roll a new `fetch + setInterval` poll. Don’t open a raw `EventSource` for query data.

The library is the single audited path: SSE/WS push, payload-on- invalidate, REST refetch fallback, observability shim (`window.__sync_metrics__`), reconnect resilience. Each parallel poll or ad-hoc EventSource forks all of that and accumulates as drift.

**Genuine exceptions** (you may roll your own integration):

* **Streaming-by-nature payloads** — log tails, terminal output, command-runner progress, LLM token streams. These are byte streams, not query data; raw `EventSource` is the right tool. See the existing uses in `OperatorPanel`, `BranchActionRunner`, `ProvisionStream`, `HarnessDashboard`’s log stream, `PiPanel` (pty).
* **Pure UI timers** — `setNow(Date.now())` for relative-time refresh, `setInterval` for animation steps. No fetch, not data sync.
* **Mobile (`apps/operator-mobile/`)** — uses its own pure-HTTP + EventSource path with `usePolledList` and `sync-stream.ts` for per-device JWT scoping and battery-aware visibility pause. New mobile consumers stay on that pattern.

If you think you have another reason to bypass the library, **surface it as a question first** instead of forking quietly. Drift here costs real CPU, battery, and latency that the user only sees as “the app feels sluggish.”

**The migration template** (3-line summary):

1. **Read** — add a resolver entry in `packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/index.ts` (the **Zero-free** dispatcher): `'queryName.variant': { argsSchema, resolve }` returning a flat row array. Prefer the structured DB projection if one exists (e.g. read `harness_plans.items` jsonb rather than re-parsing markdown). The legacy `libs/zero-harness/src/queries.ts` ZQL path is **retired** — do not add there.
2. **Write** — at the write site (the REST route / `defineTool` handler, or a watcher), fire `notifySyncInvalidate('queryName.variant', args)` from `packages/operator-core/lib/sync-sse.ts` after the write commits. For an optimistic write surface use `useSyncMutate('group.verb', restFallback)`; with Zero retired it takes the REST fallback, and the invalidate above is what pushes the new state back to subscribers.
3. **Component** — `const { data } = useSyncQuery({queryName, args})`. Done.

Full recipe in the [Cookbook](/internal/docs/data-sync/cookbook); the Zero-free dispatcher’s per-entry recipe is in the [adding-a-sync-query](/internal/docs/agent-insights/adding-a-sync-query) insight.

## What this section covers

[Section titled “What this section covers”](#what-this-section-covers)

This is a reference for agents and humans building UI panels in the harness operator (`apps/operator/app/harness/`) and the Papercup demo (`apps/papercup/`). Read this **before** you wire a new panel to data.

The stack is two layered conventions, not a single library:

1. **Zero** ([rocicorp.dev/zero](https://rocicorp.dev/zero)) — the reactive sync layer. Postgres is the source of truth. A `zero-cache` process tails logical replication and broadcasts changes to every connected client. Clients call `useQuery(...)` and re-render when the underlying row changes — no polling, no manual refetch.
2. **RichGrid** (`@restart/grid-core`, mirrored at `papercupai/papergrid`) — the column-driven grid renderer every tabular panel uses. It accepts plain rows + a `ColumnDef[]`, handles sorting, row click, row styling, and (optionally) virtual rendering. It does **not** know about Zero — the panel passes Zero query results as the `rows` prop.

These two are intentionally orthogonal:

* A panel can use **Zero without RichGrid** (e.g. card or feed UX — `ArchitectInbox`).
* A panel can use **RichGrid without Zero** (e.g. data that comes from a one-shot REST call — `ProjectsList`, the harness `[slug]/projects` page).
* The default for a new tabular panel that displays Postgres-backed data is **both**.

## Why this exists

[Section titled “Why this exists”](#why-this-exists)

Before this stack was in place, every panel had its own list-rendering code (a `<table>` or a `.map()` over `<div>`s), its own polling loop, its own optimistic-update logic, and its own bug about “stale data after a mutation.” Migrating to RichGrid + Zero collapses all of that into:

```tsx
const [results] = useQuery(queries.snapshots(slug));
return <RichGrid rows={results.map(rowToSnapshot)} columns={columns} getRowId={s => s.id} inline />;
```

Mutations write directly to Postgres (via a normal `POST /api/...` route); Zero notices the change and pushes it to every connected client within \~50ms.

## Where each piece lives

[Section titled “Where each piece lives”](#where-each-piece-lives)

| Concern                                | Package                   | Path                                                |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| RichGrid component + `ColumnDef` types | `@papercusp/grid-core`    | `libs/generic/papergrid/grid-core/src/RichGrid.tsx` |
| Zero schema definitions                | `@papercusp/zero-harness` | `libs/zero-harness/src/schema.ts`                   |
| Named-query catalog                    | `@papercusp/zero-harness` | `libs/zero-harness/src/queries.ts`                  |
| Sync hooks (`useSyncQuery`, …)         | `@papercusp/sync`         | `libs/generic/sync/src/SyncContext.ts`              |
| Sync provider for harness app          | local                     | `apps/operator/providers/HarnessZeroProvider.tsx`   |
| `zero-cache` process (retired)         | systemd unit              | `zero-cache-harness.service`                        |
| Postgres database                      | server                    | `papercusp` DB on `:5432`                           |

## Reading order for new contributors

[Section titled “Reading order for new contributors”](#reading-order-for-new-contributors)

1. [RichGrid](/internal/docs/data-sync/richgrid) — the renderer; learn this first because it’s the smaller, self-contained surface.
2. [Zero](/internal/docs/data-sync/zero) — how a row in Postgres becomes a row in your component.
3. [Named queries](/internal/docs/data-sync/named-queries) — how to add a new query to the shared catalog.
4. [Schema conventions](/internal/docs/data-sync/schema) — per-harness Postgres schemas, `harness_shared` cross-harness views, publications.
5. [Pitfalls](/internal/docs/data-sync/pitfalls) — non-obvious issues that have silently broken every panel in a schema. Read this before debugging.
6. [Cookbook](/internal/docs/data-sync/cookbook) — copy-paste recipes for the most common panel-building tasks.

## Source-of-truth files

[Section titled “Source-of-truth files”](#source-of-truth-files)

When the docs and the code disagree, the code wins. The docs are kept in sync best-effort, but the canonical references are:

* `libs/generic/papergrid/grid-core/src/RichGrid.tsx` — props, `ColumnDef` shape
* `libs/zero-harness/src/queries.ts` — every query name and its args
* `libs/zero-harness/src/schema.ts` — every published table and its Zero-side type
* `apps/operator/app/adv/harnesses/useHarnessData.ts` — a live consumer reading the consolidated queries via `useSyncQuery` (`featuresConsolidated.bySlug`, `issuesConsolidated.bySlug`, `agentRunsConsolidated.bySlug`)

# Cookbook

> Copy-paste recipes for the most common panel-building tasks.

Zero is being retired — historical reference

Zero / zero-cache / ZQL named-queries / WebSocket push is **on the retirement path**. The shipping desktop app uses **SSE-primary** sync (the `:3070` Hono host pushes invalidate/update over Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY`); zero-cache is **not run** on desktop. Treat this page as historical reference. Source of truth: `apps/operator/providers/HarnessZeroProvider.tsx` (transport-selection doc-comment) + the root `CLAUDE.md` deployment-model section.

## Recipe 1: New panel reading from an existing Zero table

[Section titled “Recipe 1: New panel reading from an existing Zero table”](#recipe-1-new-panel-reading-from-an-existing-zero-table)

The 80% case. You want to render an existing per-harness table as a new panel.

```tsx
'use client';


import { useMemo } from 'react';
import { RichGrid, type ColumnDef } from '@papercusp/grid-core';
import type { SnapshotConsolidatedRow } from '@papercusp/zero-harness';
import { useSyncQuery } from '@papercusp/sync';


interface Props {
  slug: string;
  onSelect?: (id: string) => void;
}


export default function MySnapshotsPanel({ slug, onSelect }: Props) {
  // `useSyncQuery<T>` types T as the ROW element; `.data` is `T[]`.
  // `args` is a named object, not a positional array.
  const { data: rows } = useSyncQuery<SnapshotConsolidatedRow>({
    queryName: 'snapshotsConsolidated.bySlug',
    args: { slug },
  });


  const columns = useMemo<ColumnDef<SnapshotConsolidatedRow>[]>(() => [
    {
      key: 'when', header: 'When', width: 1.3,
      sortKey: 'ts', defaultSortDir: 'desc',
      render: ({ row }) => new Date(Number(row.ts)).toLocaleString(),
    },
    {
      key: 'iter', header: 'Iter', width: 0.4, align: 'right',
      sortKey: 'iterNum',
      render: ({ row }) => row.iterNum,
    },
  ], []);


  return (
    <RichGrid<SnapshotConsolidatedRow>
      rows={rows}
      columns={columns}
      getRowId={(r) => r.snapshotId}
      onRowClick={(r) => onSelect?.(r.snapshotId)}
      inline
    />
  );
}
```

## Recipe 2: Migrating an existing `.map()` list to RichGrid

[Section titled “Recipe 2: Migrating an existing .map() list to RichGrid”](#recipe-2-migrating-an-existing-map-list-to-richgrid)

Source pattern (anti-pattern in this codebase):

```tsx
{items.map((item) => (
  <div key={item.id} className="row">
    <span>{item.id}</span>
    <span>{item.name}</span>
    <span>{item.status}</span>
  </div>
))}
```

Migration:

```tsx
import { useMemo } from 'react';
import { RichGrid, type ColumnDef } from '@papercusp/grid-core';


const columns = useMemo<ColumnDef<Item>[]>(() => [
  { key: 'id', header: 'ID', width: 1, sortKey: 'id',
    render: ({ row }) => row.id },
  { key: 'name', header: 'Name', width: 3, sortKey: 'name',
    render: ({ row }) => row.name },
  { key: 'status', header: 'Status', width: 1, sortKey: 'status',
    render: ({ row }) => row.status },
], []);


return (
  <RichGrid<Item>
    rows={items}
    columns={columns}
    getRowId={(i) => i.id}
    inline
  />
);
```

Steps in order:

1. Add `import { RichGrid, type ColumnDef } from '@papercusp/grid-core'`.
2. Build a `columns` array, one entry per visible field. Wrap in `useMemo`.
3. Replace the `.map()` block with `<RichGrid …>`.
4. Move per-row click handler from each row to `onRowClick`.
5. Drop the manual loading + error CSS (RichGrid renders its own header even when rows is empty; provide a sibling empty-state component if you need a friendlier message).

## Recipe 3: Adding a new column to an existing Zero-synced table

[Section titled “Recipe 3: Adding a new column to an existing Zero-synced table”](#recipe-3-adding-a-new-column-to-an-existing-zero-synced-table)

```sql
ALTER TABLE harness_<slug>.harness_<table>
  ADD COLUMN new_col text;
```

For each existing harness, repeat. Then:

1. Update `bin/scaffold-harness-schema.sh` so future harnesses get it.
2. Update `libs/zero-harness/src/schema.ts` — add `new_col: string()` (or the right type — beware TIMESTAMPTZ).
3. The publication already includes the table; the new column flows automatically.
4. Restart `zero-cache-harness`.
5. Update consumers (`useSyncQuery` results now include `new_col`).

## Recipe 4: Adding a new table to all harnesses

[Section titled “Recipe 4: Adding a new table to all harnesses”](#recipe-4-adding-a-new-table-to-all-harnesses)

Bigger lift. Steps:

1. Add `CREATE TABLE` DDL to `bin/scaffold-harness-schema.sh`.

2. Run scaffold against every existing harness:

   ```bash
   for slug in $(psql -tAc "SELECT nspname FROM pg_namespace WHERE nspname LIKE 'harness\_%'" | sed 's/^harness_//'); do
     bin/scaffold-harness-schema.sh "$slug"
   done
   ```

3. Add the table to `libs/zero-harness/src/schema.ts` (register it in the `createSchema({ tables: [...] })` list).

4. Add a query factory to `queries.ts`.

5. Add a `slugToXxxKey` helper to `queries.ts`.

6. Restart `zero-cache-harness`.

## Recipe 5: Cross-harness consolidated table

[Section titled “Recipe 5: Cross-harness consolidated table”](#recipe-5-cross-harness-consolidated-table)

When you need to render data across all harnesses (e.g. global feature list).

1. Create a new base table in `harness_shared`:

   ```sql
   CREATE TABLE harness_shared.harness_<name>_consolidated (
     harness_slug text,
     <column>     <type>,
     -- …
     PRIMARY KEY (harness_slug, <pk>)
   );
   ```

2. For each per-harness source table, add an `AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE` trigger that maintains the consolidated table.

3. Add the consolidated table to the `zero_harness` publication.

4. Register a no-arg named query:

   ```ts
   <name>Consolidated: () => z.query.<name>Consolidated,
   ```

5. Register the table in `schema.ts` and restart zero-cache.

`harness_features_consolidated` is the working example to copy.

## Recipe 6: Mutations that update Zero panels

[Section titled “Recipe 6: Mutations that update Zero panels”](#recipe-6-mutations-that-update-zero-panels)

You want a button that inserts a row and have every connected client see it appear.

```tsx
async function addNote() {
  const res = await fetch('/api/harness/<slug>/notes', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ text: 'hello' }),
    headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
  });
  if (!res.ok) {
    toast.error('add note failed');
    return;
  }
  // No reload, no refetch. Zero will broadcast the new row in <100ms.
}
```

The API route writes to PG. Zero broadcasts. `useSyncQuery` re-renders. Done.

If you want optimistic UI before the round-trip, hold the new row in component state and clear it when the Zero query result reflects the real one. Don’t try to write through Zero — that’s not how this stack works.

## Recipe 7: Per-row action buttons

[Section titled “Recipe 7: Per-row action buttons”](#recipe-7-per-row-action-buttons)

Buttons inside a column cell that need to **not** trigger the row’s `onRowClick`:

```tsx
{
  key: 'action',
  header: '',
  width: 0.6,
  align: 'right',
  render: ({ row }) => (
    <button
      onClick={(e) => {
        e.stopPropagation();
        handleDelete(row.id);
      }}
    >
      delete
    </button>
  ),
}
```

The `e.stopPropagation()` is required.

## Recipe 8: Selected-row highlight

[Section titled “Recipe 8: Selected-row highlight”](#recipe-8-selected-row-highlight)

```tsx
const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState<string | null>(null);


const getRowBg = (row: Row) =>
  row.id === selectedId ? '#1f2937' : 'transparent';


<RichGrid
  rows={rows}
  columns={columns}
  getRowId={(r) => r.id}
  onRowClick={(r) => setSelectedId(r.id)}
  getRowBg={getRowBg}
  inline
/>
```

The live `DepartmentHarnessDashboard.tsx` → `MemoryEntriesGrid` (`apps/operator/app/harness/`) is a current example of RichGrid with selection/striping; the retired `SnapshotsPanel.tsx` shows the same selected-row pattern.

## Recipe 9: PG-mirrored filesystem store

[Section titled “Recipe 9: PG-mirrored filesystem store”](#recipe-9-pg-mirrored-filesystem-store)

Use this when a filesystem JSON file must remain authoritative — e.g. an external CLI writes it, or a runtime loader reads it by path — but you also want cross-harness queries and Zero subscriptions over the same data.

The pattern in three parts:

**1. The PG table** is a derived index of the JSON. Same schema, plus `updated_at`. Add to the `zero_harness` publication.

```sql
CREATE TABLE harness_shared.plugin_enables (
  harness_slug   text NOT NULL,
  plugin_slug    text NOT NULL,
  version        text NOT NULL,
  config_hash    text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  enabled_at     timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at     timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  PRIMARY KEY (harness_slug, plugin_slug)
);
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON harness_shared.plugin_enables TO harness_app;
GRANT SELECT ON harness_shared.plugin_enables TO harness_zero;
ALTER PUBLICATION zero_harness ADD TABLE harness_shared.plugin_enables;
```

**2. A mirror helper.** Reads the JSON for one harness/scope, upserts matching rows, deletes orphans. This is the function every writer calls.

packages/operator-core/lib/plugin-enables-pg.ts

```ts
import { getOrgPg } from '@papercusp/db-org';


export async function mirrorHarness(harness: string): Promise<void> {
  const file = await readEnabled(harness);                  // read JSON
  const enabled = file?.enabled ?? {};
  const { sql } = getOrgPg();
  for (const [pluginSlug, meta] of Object.entries(enabled)) {
    await sql`
      INSERT INTO harness_shared.plugin_enables
        (harness_slug, plugin_slug, version, config_hash, enabled_at, updated_at)
      VALUES (${harness}, ${pluginSlug}, ${meta.version}, ${meta.configHash},
              ${meta.enabledAt}, now())
      ON CONFLICT (harness_slug, plugin_slug) DO UPDATE
        SET version = EXCLUDED.version,
            config_hash = EXCLUDED.config_hash,
            updated_at = now()
    `;
  }
  // Delete rows for plugins removed from the JSON
  const slugs = Object.keys(enabled);
  if (slugs.length === 0) {
    await sql`DELETE FROM harness_shared.plugin_enables WHERE harness_slug = ${harness}`;
  } else {
    await sql`
      DELETE FROM harness_shared.plugin_enables
      WHERE harness_slug = ${harness} AND plugin_slug NOT IN ${sql(slugs)}
    `;
  }
}
```

**3. Hook every writer.** After each successful JSON write — direct or via subprocess — call the mirror. Best-effort: a mirror failure logs but does not fail the API call.

```ts
// in the API route that calls the CLI
const r = await spawn(PAPERCUSP_BIN, ['plugin', 'enable', slug, '--harness', h]);
if (r.code === 0) {
  try { await mirrorHarness(h); } catch (e) {
    console.warn('[plugins/enable] PG mirror failed for', h, e);
  }
}
```

**4. Backfill + drift recovery.** Provide a script that reads ALL JSONs and re-syncs PG. It runs on a fresh checkout, after a direct CLI run that bypassed the operator API, or whenever you suspect drift.

scripts/backfill-plugin-enables.mjs

```js
// Same logic as mirrorHarness, run for every harness directory.
// Idempotent: re-running on already-synced data is a no-op.
```

### When to pick this pattern over PG-canonical

[Section titled “When to pick this pattern over PG-canonical”](#when-to-pick-this-pattern-over-pg-canonical)

| Pick PG-canonical (Recipe 1-2) when | Pick PG-mirror (this) when                                                    |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| You own every writer                | A third-party process or runtime path writes the JSON and you can’t change it |
| The data has no on-disk consumer    | A loader reads the JSON file at runtime by path                               |
| Atomicity of write matters          | The JSON is the operational source of truth and PG is a query-side index      |

Reference implementations:

* `packages/operator-core/lib/plugin-enables-pg.ts` (papercusp CLI is the writer)
* `packages/operator-core/lib/plugin-configs-pg.ts` (substrate plugin loader reads JSON at runtime)

## Recipe 10: Where to put a new panel

[Section titled “Recipe 10: Where to put a new panel”](#recipe-10-where-to-put-a-new-panel)

| Panel scope                                                  | Location                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tabular data for one harness, shown in the harness dashboard | `apps/operator/app/harness/<Name>Panel.tsx`                                                                          |
| Department-level dashboard panel                             | `apps/operator/app/harness/DepartmentHarnessDashboard.tsx` (extend the existing file rather than creating a new one) |
| Cross-harness panel (global view)                            | `apps/operator/app/<route>/<Name>Panel.tsx`                                                                          |

The live `apps/operator` harness UI is dock-based (`apps/operator/app/harness/[slug]/HarnessDockShell.tsx`); wire a new panel in as a dock panel rather than into a monolithic tab switcher.

When in doubt, copy the structure from one of these. The live example is `DepartmentHarnessDashboard`; the others now live in the **retired** `@papercusp/web` surface (`libs/papercusp/apps/web/app/harness/`) but still show the canonical RichGrid + sync wiring:
