# Pi (oh-my-pi) integration

> Two-track integration — pi as worker-role CLI (Option

[`oh-my-pi`](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi) (binary `omp`) is a 3.5k★ open-source AI coding agent for the terminal — strong tool harness (read / bash / edit / write / grep / find / lsp / python / browser / subagents / hooks / plugins), `--mode=rpc/json` structured output, multi-model fuzzy matching, session resume, and a TUI.

It complements Papercusp at a different layer: **pi has strong in-loop autonomy; Papercusp has strong mission orchestration**. Together: pi as the worker, Papercusp as the conductor.

This page covers two integration tracks.

## Track A — Pi as the worker-role CLI

[Section titled “Track A — Pi as the worker-role CLI”](#track-a--pi-as-the-worker-role-cli)

Track A is a proposal — not yet implemented

Track B (the embedded pi pane) shipped; **Track A has not**. There is no per-role `cliBin` field in the harness role config today — the TS orchestrator’s `invoke.ts` resolves a single agent binary globally (`$AGENT_CMD ?? $CLAUDE`, default `omp -p`), not per-role. The config below is the proposed schema, not the current one.

The smallest valuable integration. Papercusp’s per-role config already supports overrides; add `cliBin` to the schema so individual roles can specify a non-default CLI.

```json
// config.json (in any harness)
{
  "primaryRole": "orchestrator",
  "roles": {
    "worker": { "cliBin": "pi", "model": "opus" },
    "validator": { "cliBin": "claude" },
    "orchestrator": { "cliBin": "claude" }
  }
}
```

**What lands:** pi runs the worker pipeline (where tool breadth matters); claude stays on plan / validate / orchestrate (where structured-decision reliability matters). Each invocation is `pi -p --no-session --append-system-prompt=<file>` so the fresh-context contract holds.

**Effort:** \~½ day. The bash run.sh’s `invoke()` and the TS orchestrator’s `invoke.ts` both already shell out to a configurable CLI binary; this is wiring per-role config through to that spawn.

**Output parsing.** Pi’s `--mode=json` emits a JSONL event stream with the same shape papercusp already parses for claude (session header, then events). Empirically verified: first event is `{"type":"session","version":3,"id":"…","cwd":"…"}` followed by tool/message events. The adapter to map pi’s event names to papercusp’s audit schema is \~30 lines, not a deal-breaker.

**Auth.** Pi inherits the sidecar’s environment, including `ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN`. Users logged into Claude Code see no auth prompt when papercusp invokes pi — the same Claude Max subscription that drives `claude -p` drives `pi -p`. Other providers (OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock, Vertex, OpenRouter, …) flow the same way via their respective env vars.

### Cost-mixing example

[Section titled “Cost-mixing example”](#cost-mixing-example)

The interesting payoff is fine-grained cost control across roles. Pi’s four model slots ([see §16.4 in the spec](/spec/cli-pluggability/#two-layer-pluggability-a-worked-example)) let a single config dial each role independently:

```json
// config.json — opinionated mid-budget setup
{
  "roles": {
    "scoper":       { "cliBin": "pi", "extraArgs": ["--plan=opus"] },
    "planner":      { "cliBin": "pi", "extraArgs": ["--plan=opus"] },
    "worker":       { "cliBin": "pi", "extraArgs": ["--model=sonnet", "--smol=haiku"] },
    "validator":    { "cliBin": "pi", "extraArgs": ["--model=gemini-2-flash"] },
    "orchestrator": { "cliBin": "claude" }
  }
}
```

Reasoning: opus on the rare planning calls, sonnet on hot-path worker calls (with haiku for tool-plan subtasks via pi’s `--smol`), gemini flash on cheap validator passes, claude on the orchestrator for stable decision-verb output. Pairs naturally with papercusp’s [hard-stop budget enforcement](/spec/state/#53-hard-stop-budget-enforcement) — the substrate enforces the hard cap; this config tunes the per-call cost.

See [§16 CLI pluggability](/internal/docs/spec/cli-pluggability) for the substrate concept this builds on.

## Track B — Embedded pi TUI as a peer pane

[Section titled “Track B — Embedded pi TUI as a peer pane”](#track-b--embedded-pi-tui-as-a-peer-pane)

A new `pi` tab in the harness dashboard that hosts an interactive `omp` process inside the desktop app. The autonomous loop continues in the background; the human can drop into pi mid-mission for surgical override.

### Goal

[Section titled “Goal”](#goal)

Surface an interactive pi TUI inside the Papercusp Desktop harness UI alongside the existing `vscode` / `git` / `brainstorm` panels. (Phase 3b adds a “open in pi” button per feature that scopes pi to that feature’s worktree.)

### Design decisions

[Section titled “Design decisions”](#design-decisions)

1. **PTY runs in the Node sidecar, not the Tauri Rust process.** The same sidecar code runs in desktop (Tauri) and cloud (container) modes. A Rust-side PTY would fork the codebase. Use `node-pty` from inside the sidecar.

2. **I/O transport: Server-Sent Events + POST, not WebSockets.** Next.js’s standalone server (`node server.js`) does not natively support raw WS-upgrade on arbitrary routes; SSE + POST works out-of-the-box in Next.js / Hono and is plenty for terminal I/O. WS is a future optimization.

3. **`pi` is a user-installed prerequisite, not bundled.** Matches the existing `claude` pattern. The desktop preflight UI already surfaces missing-prereq state — extend with a `pi` check.

4. **No session persistence in v1.** Pi has `--no-session` for ephemeral runs; persistent resume across pane reopen is v2 polish.

5. **Slot into the existing `MainPanel` union.** `HarnessDashboard.tsx` lists every embedded-tool tab (`brainstorm`, `proposals`, `git`, `dashboard`, `vscode`, `insights`, etc.) — adding `'pi'` follows the established pattern. The `vscode` tab (which embeds `code-server` in an iframe) is the direct precedent: same shape, different embedded tool.

### Rejected alternatives

[Section titled “Rejected alternatives”](#rejected-alternatives)

* **Rust-side PTY (`portable-pty` crate)** — forks desktop/cloud paths, more native build pain on Windows, couples a UI feature to the platform shell.
* **SSH/wetty-style HTTP terminal services** — another process, another auth surface, another port. The `node-pty + xterm.js + SSE` stack runs entirely inside the existing sidecar.

### Pi command surface used by Track B

[Section titled “Pi command surface used by Track B”](#pi-command-surface-used-by-track-b)

The pane spawns one of:

* `omp` — pi’s interactive default mode. Best for general use.
* `omp shell` — pi’s “interactive shell console” subcommand. Slightly different surface; useful for shell-flavored workflows.

Useful flags to pass:

* `--no-pty` — disable pi’s *internal* PTY-based bash execution. We already have a PTY (the one we bridge to xterm.js); pi nesting another inside it can confuse signal handling and resize semantics. Set this in the embedded pane.
* `--session-dir=$STATE_DIR/.pi-sessions/` (or env `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`) — point pi’s session store at the harness state dir so sessions are scoped to the harness, not the user’s home. Falls back to `~/.omp/agent` if unset.
* `--append-system-prompt=<file>` — for Phase 3b feature-scoped opens, inject the feature’s spec/lineage as additional system prompt.
* `--export=<session-file>` — Phase 3d candidate. After a session ends, exporting it to HTML and storing under the harness audit dir makes the in-pane work part of the durable record.

### Phasing

[Section titled “Phasing”](#phasing)

Phases 3a–3c are shipped

The status table on [/implementation/status/#pi-oh-my-pi-integration—tracks-a—b-phase-3abc-shipped](/internal/docs/implementation/status) tracks landed phases. Live in the harness dashboard (open a harness in the desktop shell) — click the `pi` tab.

**Phase 3a — MVP terminal pane (\~1 day).** ✅ shipped. A new `pi` tab in the harness dashboard. Click → opens xterm.js connected to a fresh `pi` process in the harness’s project directory. Keystrokes in, output out. Close tab → kill pi.

**Phase 3b — peer pane layout + feature-scoped launch (\~1 day).** ✅ shipped (tab-scoped, not split-pane). Each feature’s `FeaturePeekPanel` gets an “open in pi” button → pi spawns in `<stateDir>/worktrees/<fid>` (falls back to project root if no worktree). SSE `onAbort` kills the pty immediately so navigation doesn’t orphan `omp`. The plan called for a split-pane layout; we shipped tab-pattern instead (matches the existing `vscode` tab; no layout-shift, full pane width). True split-pane is a future affordance if needed.

**Phase 3c — desktop polish (\~½ day).** ✅ shipped. `pi` added to preflight checks (PATH + well-known-paths probe). Install-hint UI surfaces missing-pi with `brew install can1357/oh-my-pi/oh-my-pi`. README documents pi as an optional prereq. Pi missing does NOT block the app from booting — only the pi tab degrades.

**Phase 3d — partially shipped.**

* **Feature-scoped system-prompt injection** ✅ shipped. When the user clicks “open in pi” on a feature, the spawn endpoint reads `harness_features` for that `(slug, featureId)`, formats the title / spec / status / lineage as markdown, writes to `<stateDir>/pi-prompts/<feature-id>.md`, and adds `--append-system-prompt=<path>` to the omp args. Pi launches already aware of the feature it’s working on. Falls back silently when the feature lookup fails — no error surface, just no injection.
* **Per-harness session persistence** ✅ shipped via `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=<stateDir>/pi-sessions/`. Each harness has its own pi history under its state dir; sessions persist across pane reopens automatically. Future polish: explicit “resume last session” button using `omp -c` / `omp -r <id>`.
* **Audit export** — deferred. `--export <session>.html` after each pane close, dropped into `<stateDir>/audit/pi-sessions/`. Sessions are persisted today; export is a presentation layer that can run later from the persisted jsonl.
* **Pi plugin** via `--plugin-dir <path>` — deferred. A `papercusp` plugin shipped at `~/.papercusp/global-plugins/pi/` that registers tools like `papercusp.feature_status`, `papercusp.list_features`, `papercusp.lineage`, `papercusp.post_comment`. Pi loads it on startup; the plugin reads/writes papercusp state through the existing Hono API (so no extra trust boundary). Bidirectional from the dashboard side: papercusp learns of pi-emitted events via plugin hooks.
* **Subagent cross-pollination** — deferred. `omp agents unpack` ships curated subagent personas. Wrap each as a papercusp plugin so they appear in the marketplace catalog. Cross-pollinate the ecosystems.
* **Multi-pane** — deferred. Multiple concurrent pi panes scoped to different features (capped per the 4-pane limit in §Risks).

### I/O protocol (HTTP/SSE)

[Section titled “I/O protocol (HTTP/SSE)”](#io-protocol-httpsse)

```plaintext
POST /api/harness/:slug/pty/spawn
  body: { laneId?: string, cols: number, rows: number,
          ctxPrompt?: string, cwd?: 'project'|'worktree' }
  → { id: string }   // uuid


GET /api/harness/:slug/pty/:id/stream    (text/event-stream)
  ← event: data\ndata: <base64-bytes>\n\n
  ← event: exit\ndata: {"code": 0}\n\n


POST /api/harness/:slug/pty/:id/input    { data: <base64-bytes> }
POST /api/harness/:slug/pty/:id/resize   { cols, rows }
POST /api/harness/:slug/pty/:id/kill
```

Bytes are base64-encoded over JSON to keep the SSE stream uniform regardless of encoding (xterm.js handles arbitrary byte streams; pi may emit non-UTF-8 in edge cases like binary file contents). Idle PTYs (no input, no SSE consumer) auto-kill after 5 minutes.

### Critical files to read first

[Section titled “Critical files to read first”](#critical-files-to-read-first)

| `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/index.ts`             | Hono route-table assembly. The pty router registers the same way the harness/plugins routers do.                                                                   |

| `papercusp-desktop/web/index.html`                                      | `renderHint()` switch — the pi case.                                                                                                                               |

### Verification

[Section titled “Verification”](#verification)

**Phase 3a:**

1. Launch the desktop shell: `cd papercusp-desktop && npm run dev` (the only supported run path; it boots the operator sidecar + webview).
2. In the Tauri window, open a harness (`/harness/<some-slug>`).
3. Click the new pi tab.
4. Pi prompt appears; type `pwd` + Enter; output shows the harness’s project directory.
5. Type `exit`; pane shows “(pi exited 0)” and the spawn lifecycle cleans up (verify `pgrep -af omp` returns nothing).
6. Resize the window; xterm-fit addon resizes; pi sees the new width (`tput cols`).

**Phase 3b:** 7. Two-pane layout works: dashboard left, pi right; resizable divider; both visible. 8. On a feature row, “Open in pi” puts pi inside that feature’s worktree directory (verify with `pwd`). 9. Pi’s first prompt includes the feature spec + lineage (visible when asked “what are you working on?”).

**Phase 3c:** 10. `pi` shows as `missing` in the bootstrap UI when uninstalled; install hint card appears with a brew/install command. 11. Once installed, `pi` flips to `ok` on next preflight tick; pi tab works. 12. README quick-start mentions pi as optional.

**Cross-cutting:**

* No native-binary load errors at sidecar boot on macOS, Linux, Windows.
* The desktop bundle still ships within size budget (no inadvertent +100MB from xterm assets).
* No stray pty processes survive sidecar shutdown.

### Risks

[Section titled “Risks”](#risks)

| Risk                                                                                                                   | Mitigation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `node-pty` native binding fails under Next.js `output: 'standalone'` (Next traces deps and may miss the `.node` file). | Verify on day 1. If `next.config.js` `outputFileTracingIncludes` doesn’t capture `node_modules/node-pty/build/Release/*.node`, add an explicit include. Fallback: ship pty-bridge as a separate child process the Next handler shells out to. |
| `node-pty` Windows ConPTY initialization fails on older Win10.                                                         | Document min Windows version (10 1809+) in README. Surface a clear inline error in the pane.                                                                                                                                                  |
| Pi binary not on `PATH` despite being installed (Mac homebrew + Tauri-Cocoa launches without a login shell).           | Probe `/usr/local/bin/omp`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/omp`, `~/.cargo/bin/omp` in addition to `which`. Fall back to user-configurable `pi.binPath` in `config.json`.                                                                                 |
| Concurrent pi panes spawn many processes / use lots of memory.                                                         | Cap to 4 concurrent ptys per harness; show “pty limit reached” inline instead of opening a 5th.                                                                                                                                               |
| Pi’s nested PTY (its `bash` tool) conflicts with the outer xterm.js PTY — terminal corruption or signal loss.          | Spawn with `--no-pty`. Pi degrades gracefully (loses interactive bash but keeps every other tool).                                                                                                                                            |
| Auth state drifts: user logged into Claude Code in their normal shell, but the desktop app launches without that env.  | Surface `ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` presence in the preflight UI; document the GUI-app-no-login-shell gotcha in the README.                                                                                                 |

## What is explicitly NOT in scope

[Section titled “What is explicitly NOT in scope”](#what-is-explicitly-not-in-scope)

* Pi plugin exposing papercusp tools (deferred to Phase 3d).
* Session persistence / resume across pane reopen (deferred).
* Replacing the `vscode` tab — pi sits alongside it, not instead of it.
* Web (non-desktop) deployment of the pi pane — works the same way (sidecar is identical), but rollout is separate.

Note

Track A and Track B are independent — implement either or both. Track A alone is the smaller, less-visible change. Track B alone gives users the interactive override without changing how the autonomous loop runs. Together they make pi a first-class citizen in the desktop runtime.

# Plugin + marketplace pipeline — state as of 2026-05-11

> One-page reference for the TS plugin/template/snapshot/marketplace system as it stands today. Where the code is, what's covered by tests, what's deferred, and where to look first.

Note

Snapshot of the system as `tsplugin` agent left it (2026-05-11). For the roadmap of new runtimes built on top of this (WASM, daemon, iframe), see `papercup-native/docs/ts-plugin-system-v1-plan.md` — owned by `@plugin` agent (Rust runtime).

Dated snapshot — paths and the marketplace surface have moved

Preserved as the 2026-05-11 milestone. Reading it today, note:

* The operator is now **`apps/operator/`** and its `app/api/**` routes were ported to **Hono routers under `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/**`**; `apps/operator/lib/*` (e.g. `plugin-host-runtime.ts`, `plugin-grants.ts`) now lives under **`packages/operator-core/lib/`**. The Next route paths in the tables below are stale.
* The `localhost:3057` / `papercuspai.com` marketplace-api was superseded by the in-app **Cupboard** (`apps/operator-public`, CF Workers + Hono + D1).
* The “use git worktrees for non-main work” hard rule is **reversed** under the current model: the shared tree stays on `staging` and you do **not** branch/worktree — concurrency is serialized by the `locks:*` + `coord:*` systems. See the repo `CLAUDE.md` “Branch discipline” section.

## TL;DR

[Section titled “TL;DR”](#tldr)

Three publishable kinds (`plugin`, `template`, `snapshot`) share one marketplace pipeline. Operator at `localhost:3055` serves the install/discover surface; marketplace-api at `localhost:3057` is the registry. Plugins run in-process under a two-tier capability check (manifest ∩ user-granted). Tests cover every helper and DB-backed function shipped in this session.

## What runs end-to-end today

[Section titled “What runs end-to-end today”](#what-runs-end-to-end-today)

### Plugin lifecycle

[Section titled “Plugin lifecycle”](#plugin-lifecycle)

1. **Install** — `POST /api/marketplace/install-plugin { slug, version? }` shells out to `papercusp install <slug>@<version>`. **Atomic since PR #6**: downloads + extracts + validates manifest in a sibling staging dir, then renames into place. Failed download / bad tarball / manifest mismatch preserves the existing install.
2. **Enable** — `POST /api/plugins/enable { slug, harnesses[], disable? }` adds to `enabled-plugins.json` for each harness and writes the boot-time silent grant backfill.
3. **Consent** — `/installed/plugins/<slug>/permissions` renders a harnesses × capabilities grid; toggling `POST /api/plugins/grants { plugin, version, harness, capabilities, action }` mutates `harness_shared.plugin_capability_grants`. Two-tier check: every `hasCapability(ctx, cap)` ANDs manifest with the granted set.
4. **Run** — Lifecycle hooks fire from operator (`beforeMissionStart`, `mission.start`, `onFeaturePassed`, `task.passed`, `feature.completed`, `proposal.accepted`) and from `run.sh` (`beforeMissionStart`, `onPostOrchestrator`, `onPostWorker`, `onPostValidator`, `afterDone`).
5. **Action invocation** — `POST /api/plugins/[...path]` proxies through `ctx.actions.register(...)`’d handlers. Every invocation produces an audit row via `PgAuditWriter` (fail-closed — action fails if audit write fails).
6. **Update** — `GET /api/plugins/updates` diffs installed vs catalog; `/installed/plugins` shows “Update → vX.Y.Z” with new-cap re-consent prompt before bumping.
7. **Uninstall** — `POST /api/plugins/uninstall { slug }` removes the global plugin dir + disables from every harness it was enabled in.

### Template lifecycle

[Section titled “Template lifecycle”](#template-lifecycle)

1. **Save** — “Save template” button on harness dashboard → `POST /api/harness/<slug>/save-as-template { slug, version, description?, author? }` forks the recipe (SPEC.md, AGENTS.md, `.papercusp/config.json`, `.papercusp/validation-contract.md` + plugin recommendations from `enabled-plugins.json`) into `~/.papercusp/templates/<slug>/<version>/`.
2. **Publish** — `POST /api/templates/<slug>/<version>/publish` tars + signs + uploads to marketplace-api.
3. **Install** — `POST /api/marketplace/install { slug, projectName, targetPath? }` scaffolds a new project. **Slug-collision recovery (PR #5)**: returns `{ code: 'project_name_taken', suggestedName: '<base>-2' }` on conflict; UI auto-offers via `confirm()`. Partial-init cleanup wipes half-scaffolded dirs on `papercusp init` failure.

### Snapshot lifecycle

[Section titled “Snapshot lifecycle”](#snapshot-lifecycle)

1. **Capture** — `POST /api/snapshots/create` writes a tarball under `<harness>/.papercusp/snapshots/`.
2. **Publish** — `POST /api/snapshots/<id>/publish` uploads to marketplace.
3. **Fork** — `POST /api/snapshots/<id>/instantiate` (or `papercusp snapshot fork`) creates a new harness with schema rename. **Grants carry over (PR #2)**: `copyGrantsToNewHarness` copies every `(plugin, version, capability)` grant on the source harness to the new fork via `INSERT … SELECT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`.
4. **Republish** — *pending*. PR-B paused per `@plugin`’s reply on coord, awaiting v1 plan greenlight (Batch G+1 bumps `SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA_VERSION` to 2).

## Hard rules in this code (don’t break)

[Section titled “Hard rules in this code (don’t break)”](#hard-rules-in-this-code-dont-break)

* **No TS deletion** anywhere in `apps/operator/` or `libs/papercusp/`. Set by `shared.jsonl` 2026-05-10T05:50.
* **Rust port is opt-in** via `?backend=rust`; default routes always go to TS.
* **Paperclip stomps** `apps/operator/app/harness/*` periodically. `pgrep -af paperclip` before editing harness UI; race-and-recommit if it stomps you.
* **Schema ownership**: `packages/plugin-sdk/papercusp-plugin.schema.json` is `@plugin`’s territory going forward (per their handoff on coord 2026-05-11T15:30). Transitional additions get a `kind: contract` post first.
* **Use git worktrees** for any non-main feature work — never branch-switch the canonical `papercup/` checkout while other agents may be writing.

## Test coverage

[Section titled “Test coverage”](#test-coverage)

Plugin-loader tests (vitest, `packages/plugin-loader/`):

* 91 cases covering manifest validation, capability matching (incl. two-tier), hookbus isolation, action registry, semver, audit, api-factory, tools.

Operator unit tests (vitest, `apps/operator/`):

* 67 cases on pure helpers from PRs #2-#5: `isNewerVersion`, `computeCapChange`, `suggestNextFreeName`, `SLUG_RE`, `SEMVER_RE`, `explainCapability`, `tierBadgeColor`.

Operator integration tests (vitest + testcontainers PG, `apps/operator/test/`):

* 25 cases covering every public function in `lib/plugin-grants.ts`: `copyGrantsToNewHarness` (8), `grantCapabilities/revokeCapabilities/getGrantsForPluginInHarness` (11), `backfillGrantsFromEnabledPluginsAndLegacyFile` (6).

Total: **183 tests** specifically on the plugin/marketplace surface.

## Key APIs at a glance

[Section titled “Key APIs at a glance”](#key-apis-at-a-glance)

```plaintext
GET   /api/marketplace/catalog                  — proxies marketplace-api with hide-filter
POST  /api/marketplace/install                  — template/snapshot install (slug-collision aware)
POST  /api/marketplace/install-plugin           — plugin install via papercusp CLI
DELETE /api/marketplace/uninstall               — template uninstall
GET   /api/plugins/global                       — installed plugins
GET   /api/plugins/manifest?slug=<id>           — declared capabilities for consent UI
GET   /api/plugins/updates                      — installed-vs-catalog diff with capChange
GET   /api/plugins/grants?plugin=&version=&harness=
POST  /api/plugins/grants                       — toggle a (plugin, harness, cap) grant
POST  /api/plugins/enable                       — enable/disable a plugin in harness(es)
POST  /api/plugins/uninstall
POST  /api/snapshots/create
POST  /api/snapshots/<id>/publish
POST  /api/snapshots/<id>/instantiate           — fork (carries grants)
POST  /api/snapshots/<id>/retract
POST  /api/harness/<slug>/save-as-template
POST  /api/templates/<slug>/<version>/publish
```

## First places to look

[Section titled “First places to look”](#first-places-to-look)

* New plugin author: `/docs/spec/plugin-quickstart` — five-command flow from blank dir to published plugin.
* Plugin runtime contract: `packages/plugin-sdk/src/index.ts` — capability strings + lifecycle hook signatures.
* Capability semantics: `packages/plugin-loader/src/capabilities.ts` — wildcard matching, two-tier AND.
* Manifest schema: `packages/plugin-sdk/papercusp-plugin.schema.json` — `additionalProperties: false`.
* Lifecycle wire-up: `apps/operator/lib/plugin-host-runtime.ts` — fire-points + audit + grants integration.
* Marketplace registry: `../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-api/src/server.ts` — catalog, signing, retraction, SBOM.

# Implementation status

> Phase-by-phase ship state of the Papercusp reference runtime.

Dated phase-status snapshot — paths have since moved

This is a historical implementation-status record (Phase 1–§MHS work, through mid-2026). It’s preserved as a dated milestone log; **the file paths and a few component names below are stale** after later refactors. The big renames to keep in mind when reading:

* `apps/papercup/**` and `apps/papercusp/**` → the operator now lives at **`apps/operator/`**; its Next.js `app/api/**` routes were ported to **Hono routers under `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/**`**.
* Operator-side `lib/*` (e.g. `lib/plugin-host-runtime.ts`, `lib/plugin-runtime.ts`) now lives under **`packages/operator-core/lib/`**.
* The `run.sh` → TS orchestrator port shipped and its ported run-loop was later **retired** (see [orchestrator-port](/internal/docs/implementation/orchestrator-port)); the live pipeline is the DBOS runner in `packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/`.
* The `papercuspai.com` marketplace described in the “After all of the above” table was superseded by the in-app **Cupboard** (`apps/operator-public`).

The reference runtime lives in this monorepo (`papercupai/papercup`). Phase numbering matches the spec sections; some phases were split into a/b for separable shipping.

## What’s gating v1.0

[Section titled “What’s gating v1.0”](#whats-gating-v10)

All 5 of the 6b sub-tasks have landed:

1. ✅ Lifecycle hooks — `beforeMissionStart` / `onLoad` / `onFeaturePassed` / `onProposalAccepted` fire from the operator (Hono routes); `beforeMissionStart` / `afterDone` / `onPostOrchestrator` / `onPostValidator` fire from `run.sh` via the `papercusp-fire-hook` CLI.
2. ✅ Mount plugin `apiRoutes` — `mountPluginApiRoutes` runs at `/api/[[...route]]/route.ts` startup.
3. ✅ Typed-service DI container — `createPapercuspApi` in `@papercusp/plugin-loader/api-factory.ts`.
4. ✅ Construct gated `PapercuspContext` — `buildPapercuspContext` + per-(plugin, harness) `ServerActionRegistry` attached as `ctx.actions`. Plugins like `@papercupai/cloudflare-pages` that `ctx.actions.register('publish', handler)` from `init()` now succeed.
5. ✅ `componentId` → lazy React registry — `lib/plugin-runtime.ts` resolver, `lib/PluginTabs.tsx` strip, `lib/PluginReactTab.tsx` single-tab render. Wired into `HarnessDashboard.tsx` (the dashboard’s tab strip includes React-mode plugin tabs alongside iframe ones).

Residual cleanups (none gate v1.0):

* v2 iframe-CSP loader (deferred per spec §8.6).

### After 6b (plugin architecture)

[Section titled “After 6b (plugin architecture)”](#after-6b-plugin-architecture)

| Item                                            | Scope                                              | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ~~Plugin schema auto-apply at install~~         | ✅ Already wired + types unified 2026-04-29         | The branch in `papercusp install` (libs/papercusp/packages/cli/src/papercusp.ts) already runs DDL via `psql ON_ERROR_STOP=1` when `manifest.schema` is set. The SDK type was `PluginSchemaDef = {schemaName, ddlPath}` while the install code expected `string[]`. Unified: SDK now exports `PluginSchemaField = PluginSchemaDef \| PluginSchemaDef[] \| string[]`; install normalizes via a new `normalizeSchemaField` helper. 6 unit tests cover all three shapes + malformed input. No existing plugin uses the field yet, but the type/runtime mismatch is gone and the path is exercisable.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ~~Marketplace → auto-install drop-in~~          | ✅ Already wired + cache-busting added 2026-04-29   | The UI flow already existed end-to-end: `<InstallPluginButton>` (in `MarketplaceList.tsx`) POSTs to `/api/marketplace/install-plugin`, which shells out to `papercusp install <slug> --accept-capabilities`. The CLI extracts the tarball into `~/.papercusp/global-plugins/<name>/` and (post-2026-04-29) auto-applies any `manifest.schema` DDL via psql. **What was missing:** the in-process runtime cache (`globalThis`-pinned for HMR robustness) didn’t know about the just-installed plugin. Now both the install and uninstall endpoints call `_resetPluginHostForTests()` + `_resetPluginApiRoutesForTests()` after a successful CLI run, so the next request re-discovers and the new plugin’s `init` / `onLoad` fire on first slug contact. Verified end-to-end against `@papercupai/docs-viewer`: `initializedPairs` goes from 6 → 0 after the install POST. |
| ~~Plugin hot-reload in dev mode~~               | ✅ Shipped 2026-04-29                               | `watchPluginsForReload({dir})` in `lib/plugin-host-runtime.ts` — opt-in via `PAPERCUSP_DEV_PLUGIN_WATCH=1` env var. Recursive `fs.watch` on `~/.papercusp/global-plugins/` with a 250ms debounce; only resets on `papercusp.json` / `index.{js,mjs,ts}` / `dist/index.js` changes (ignores editor swap files + `node_modules` churn). Watcher handle pinned on `globalThis` so HMR doesn’t double-arm it. Production hosts leave it off.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ~~Wildcard `secrets:read:PREFIX_*` capability~~ | ✅ Shipped 2026-04-29                               | Both flavors land together: subdomain (`http:fetch:*.foo.com`) and prefix (`secrets:read:YT_*`). Implemented in `hasCapability` via a shared `matchWildcardCap` helper — also reused by `actions.ts` for action-cap subset validation. Strict semantics: `*.foo.com` does NOT match the bare suffix `foo.com`; `head*` requires a non-empty head and a non-empty tail (degenerate `secrets:read:*` is rejected). 5 new tests in `capabilities.test.ts`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ~~`compute:exec:<binary>` capability~~          | ✅ Shipped 2026-04-29                               | Added `compute:exec:<basename>` to the SDK Capability union; existing wildcard helper handles `compute:exec:py-*` style prefix grants. New `PapercuspContext.spawn?: PluginSpawn` typed surface — async returns `{stdout, stderr, code, killed}`. Host implementation in `lib/plugin-host-runtime.ts` (`makePluginSpawn`): rejects path-bearing bins (basename only), gates on `compute:exec:<basename>`, ensures the plugin’s data dir exists before spawn, captures stdout/stderr to 1 MiB each (truncated marker on overflow), 30 s timeout with SIGTERM→SIGKILL escalation. Verified end-to-end against a probe plugin: declared `compute:exec:echo` succeeds with `code=0 stdout="hello-from-spawn"`; undeclared `ls` rejects with MissingCapability; `/bin/echo` rejects before cap check on the path-separator guard.                                              |
| ~~Plugin runtime versioning + CHANGELOG~~       | ✅ Shipped 2026-04-29                               | `PAPERCUSP_RUNTIME_VERSION = '0.1.0'` constant in the SDK; loader rejects plugins whose `papercusp:` range excludes the runtime version. Minimal in-tree semver matcher in `packages/plugin-loader/src/semver.ts` covers `X.Y.Z` / `^X.Y.Z` (incl. caret-leading-zero) / `~X.Y.Z` / `>=X.Y.Z` / `*`. 9 semver tests + 1 negative-path loader test. CHANGELOG authored at `packages/plugin-sdk/CHANGELOG.md` — covers the lifecycle hooks, free-form bus, action registry, capability strings (incl. wildcards), manifest schema, loader contract, host runtime APIs, and the recent shape changes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ~~Reference plugins (slack-notify, jira-sync)~~ | ✅ Already authored — symlinks repointed 2026-04-29 | Both `@papercupai/slack-notifier` (1 action: `notify`) and `@papercupai/jira-sync` (3 actions: `create-issue`, `list-issues`, `post-comment`) lived at `papercupai-workspace/papercusp/plugins/` but their global-plugins symlinks still pointed at the retired `Restart/libs/papercusp/plugins/` location, so the runtime was silently skipping them. Repointed; both load cleanly, register all their declared actions, and the slack `notify` invoke probe returns the expected “SLACK\_WEBHOOK\_URL not configured” envelope.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

| Tag `desktop-v0.0.2`                                           | \~½ day                                    | Run `bin/release-local.sh 0.0.2 alpha` in the desktop checkout. Local Linux x86\_64 build → signed → GitHub Release. No CI involved.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

| Auto-updater wiring (Tauri)                                    | ✅ shipped                                  | Runtime endpoint resolution + channel-aware manifest (`/api/updates/manifest`) + signed releases via local builds (see desktop `SHIPPING.md`).                                                                                                                                                                                               |
