## 15.19 Open questions

[Section titled “15.19 Open questions”](#1519-open-questions)

1. **License field default**: should snapshots default to `MIT` (permissive) or `none` (no rights granted)? Argument for MIT: encourages community reuse. Argument for none: protects users who didn’t think about licensing. Likely answer: explicit license picker at publish time; no default; refuse to publish without user-selected license.

2. **Cost-to-continue estimation accuracy**: should the marketplace UI show “this snapshot has 12 todo features ≈ $8 to drive to passed” based on `expected_cost_cents`? Pro: helps users decide. Con: estimates may be wildly inaccurate. Proposed: show with explicit “estimate, actuals will vary” caveat.

3. **Retention for free tier**: should free-tier snapshots have a shorter shelf life (e.g., 30 days unless paid)? Pro: cost control. Con: undermines the “permanent artifact” property. Proposed: free tier limits *count* (e.g., 10 active snapshots) but not lifespan.

4. **Binary distribution: bundle vs postinstall download**: §15.20 commits to postinstall download from upstream releases. Open: should we mirror these binaries on R2 to avoid GitHub release-API rate-limiting during high-publish windows? \~50 MB × N platforms = \~250 MB R2 storage. Probably yes for production reliability.

5. **Stored-procedure conventions for harness schemas**: §15.22 commits to a CI-enforced “no hardcoded `harness_<slug>` in function bodies” rule. Open: do we ever actually need stored procedures in per-harness schemas, or should we ban them entirely? Banning is simpler; allowing requires careful schema-aware procedure authoring.

## 15.20 Binary dependencies

[Section titled “15.20 Binary dependencies”](#1520-binary-dependencies)

The substrate ships with a postinstall hook that downloads pinned binary dependencies into `~/.papercusp/bin/`. Same pattern as esbuild, sharp, ripgrep, swc, biome — well-trodden in the Node ecosystem.

**Why not system installers (apt, brew, winget)**:

* Most distros require sudo for system installs. The substrate doesn’t run as root. Asking the user to retry under sudo breaks the “user just installs papercusp” promise.
* Package-manager fragmentation on Linux. `apt` vs `dnf` vs `zypper` vs `pacman` vs `apk` — each needs its own command. Detecting which one’s available is real code, and any non-listed distro fails.
* macOS without Homebrew. Real users; sudo-less install isn’t possible.
* Versions drift. Whatever ships in `apt-get install trufflehog` is whatever Debian/Ubuntu pinned, possibly years stale. We’d need to validate version compatibility on every install.

**Postinstall download model**:

```text
On `npm install -g papercusp`, postinstall script:
  1. Detect platform (darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-arm64, linux-x64,
     win32-x64).
  2. Download pinned binaries from upstream GitHub releases:
     - trufflehog (https://github.com/trufflesecurity/trufflehog/releases/...)
     - gitleaks (https://github.com/zricethezav/gitleaks/releases/...)
     - cosign (https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/releases/...)
     - oras (https://github.com/oras-project/oras/releases/...)
  3. Verify sha256 against substrate-pinned manifest in
     `apps/papercusp/lib/snapshot/binary-versions.ts`.
  4. Write to ~/.papercusp/bin/.
  5. Add to PATH for substrate's child processes (NOT user shell).
```

`papercusp doctor` verifies binary integrity (sha256 against pinned manifest) and re-downloads if missing/corrupt. `papercusp upgrade` pulls a new pinned manifest, re-downloads.

**Storage**: \~50 MB total across all 4 binaries × 5 platforms. Acceptable; node\_modules already adds 200+ MB. Pinned versions guarantee consistent behavior across substrate installs.

**Failure modes**:

* Network failure during postinstall: substrate proceeds; first attempt to use `papercusp snapshot create` runs the download lazily with same logic.
* Sha256 mismatch: refuse to use, log loudly. Could indicate compromise or upstream tampering.
* Platform unsupported: refuse with clear “your platform isn’t supported for snapshots; supported: darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-arm64, linux-x64, win32-x64”.

**v1.1 enhancement (under consideration)**: mirror binaries on R2 so GitHub release-API rate-limiting can’t block users during high-publish windows. See §15.19 question 4.

## 15.21 Library factoring

[Section titled “15.21 Library factoring”](#1521-library-factoring)

The substrate ships **three** libraries for the publish/snapshot work, not one library with a `kind` parameter (which is a smell of two libraries pretending to be one):

### `papercusp-publish-auth` — genuinely shared (\~300 LOC)

[Section titled “papercusp-publish-auth — genuinely shared (\~300 LOC)”](#papercusp-publish-auth--genuinely-shared-300-loc)

Used by both publishing and snapshots. Ships:

* JWT minting + validation (HS256, `jti`/`sha256`/`exp` claims)
* Replay-protection D1 unique-key constraint
* Canonical-form sha256 hashing (RFC 8785 JCS)
* Audit log writer (D1)
* Rate-limit client (KV burst + daily counters)

Located at `libs/papercusp-publish-auth/`.

### `papercusp-export-build` — publishing-specific (\~400 LOC)

[Section titled “papercusp-export-build — publishing-specific (\~400 LOC)”](#papercusp-export-build--publishing-specific-400-loc)

Used by §16 Publishing only. Ships:

* File selection from `<exportDir>/` (built site output)
* Light redaction policy (build artifacts rarely leak secrets; source maps are the main concern)
* Tarball composition optimized for 5-25 MB sites
* Cloudflare Pages deployment client

Located at `libs/papercusp-export-build/`.

### `papercusp-export-state` — snapshot-specific (\~600 LOC)

[Section titled “papercusp-export-state — snapshot-specific (\~600 LOC)”](#papercusp-export-state--snapshot-specific-600-loc)

Used by §15 Snapshots only (this spec). Ships:

* Whole-harness file selection with denylist
* Heavy redaction policy (source + .papercusp/ + agent transcripts)
* pg\_dump + filter-registry-driven shared-table CSV exports
* Tarball composition for 50-500 MB snapshots
* ALTER SCHEMA-based restore flow
* Slug rewrite over text artifacts

Located at `libs/papercusp-export-state/`.

### Why three libraries instead of one

[Section titled “Why three libraries instead of one”](#why-three-libraries-instead-of-one)

Looking at the divergence:

| Concern              | Publishing                                  | Snapshot                                 |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| File selection       | `<exportDir>/` only                         | Whole harness, sans denylist             |
| Redaction aggression | Light (build artifacts rarely leak secrets) | Heavy (source + .papercusp/)             |
| Artifact format      | Tarball of files                            | Tarball of files + DB dump + shared CSVs |
| Size target          | 5-25 MB                                     | 50-500 MB                                |
| Auth                 | JWT against `publish.papercuspai.com`       | JWT against `papercuspai.com/snapshots`  |

Five of six concerns diverge. The shared concern (auth) extracts cleanly. A single library with a `kind: 'for-publish' | 'for-snapshot'` parameter forces every read to branch on `kind`, which adds complexity without saving code. Three libraries is the cleaner factoring.

## 15.22 CI enforcement

[Section titled “15.22 CI enforcement”](#1522-ci-enforcement)

Two correctness-critical conventions need *enforcement*, not just documentation. Without enforcement, both rules will rot within 6 months of shipping.

### Shared-table-filter-registry check

[Section titled “Shared-table-filter-registry check”](#shared-table-filter-registry-check)

When a developer adds a new `harness_shared.<table>` in `libs/db/sql/*.sql`, the corresponding entry must also exist in `apps/papercusp/lib/snapshot/shared-table-filters.ts`. Otherwise snapshots from harnesses that have rows in that table would silently omit them on capture, or include all rows globally on capture (cross- harness leak).

CI check: parse all `CREATE TABLE harness_shared.X` statements from SQL migrations; assert each has a corresponding `SHARED_TABLE_FILTERS.X` entry. Fails the build if missing.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml (excerpt)
- name: Check shared-table-filter-registry
  run: |
    npx tsx scripts/check-shared-table-filters.ts
```

### Stored-procedure-no-hardcoded-slug check

[Section titled “Stored-procedure-no-hardcoded-slug check”](#stored-procedure-no-hardcoded-slug-check)

Function bodies containing hardcoded `harness_<slug>` references survive ALTER SCHEMA RENAME with the wrong name (Postgres treats function bodies as opaque text; renaming the schema doesn’t update the body).

CI check: grep for `CREATE FUNCTION` blocks in SQL migrations; within each block, check for `harness_<` patterns. Any match fails the build with: “function bodies must use `current_schema()` or accept schema as parameter; no hardcoded `harness_<slug>` references.”

```yaml
- name: Check no hardcoded harness slug in stored procedures
  run: |
    npx tsx scripts/check-no-hardcoded-slug-in-functions.ts
```

Both checks add \~30 minutes of one-time work. They prevent regression classes that would otherwise surface as silent data corruption.

### Cross-version restore CI matrix

[Section titled “Cross-version restore CI matrix”](#cross-version-restore-ci-matrix)

Beyond the two checks above, snapshot tests run a matrix:

* For each supported substrate version `vN, vN-1, vN-2, ...`:

  * Capture snapshot on substrate version `vN`
  * Restore on substrate version `vN+1` (and verify)
  * Restore on substrate version current

* Matrix runs nightly + on each release-candidate PR.

This is the substrate’s equivalent of Discourse’s 10-year-mature “backups across versions” testing. Catches schema-migration incompatibilities before they ship.

### Destructive-migration `Snapshot compat:` rule

[Section titled “Destructive-migration Snapshot compat: rule”](#destructive-migration-snapshot-compat-rule)

Forward-only migrations don’t make destructive operations safe. A `DROP COLUMN`, `RENAME TABLE`, or `DROP TABLE` applied to old snapshot data loses information silently. The cross-version CI matrix catches the gross failures, but a destructive migration that “successfully” drops data on restore passes the matrix while losing the user’s work.

CI check: any migration matching the destructive pattern must contain a `-- Snapshot compat:` comment block explaining the preservation strategy. Linter fails the PR otherwise.

```sql
-- migrations/v25__rename_features_table.sql
-- Snapshot compat: snapshots from v <= 24 carry harness_features rows;
-- this migration MUST preserve them. Renaming is non-destructive
-- (data preserved); but if we ever drop columns or merge tables,
-- a CONVERTING-migration must run the data-preservation logic.


ALTER TABLE harness_features RENAME TO harness_features_v2;
```

```sql
-- migrations/v27__drop_unused_legacy_metadata.sql
-- Snapshot compat: this column was added in v18 and never read after v22.
-- Snapshots from v18-v22 will lose this column's data on restore.
-- Acceptable because: column was an experimental field never surfaced
-- in UI; no users relied on it; verified by grep of substrate codebase.


ALTER TABLE harness_features DROP COLUMN legacy_metadata;
```

The reviewer assesses whether the preservation strategy is honest. The linter just checks the comment exists.

### Forbidden-deserializer CI grep

[Section titled “Forbidden-deserializer CI grep”](#forbidden-deserializer-ci-grep)

A snapshot is untrusted code AND untrusted data (see §15.24). Substrate code that touches captured artifacts must use safe deserializers only. CI greps the substrate codebase for forbidden calls anywhere a captured-artifact path is involved:

* `pickle.load`, `pickle.loads`, `dill.load`, `cloudpickle.load`
* `yaml.load` (PyYAML default — unsafe; use `yaml.safe_load`)
* `eval(`, `Function(`, `vm.runInNewContext(`, `Reflect.apply(`
* SQLite open without `SQLITE_DBCONFIG_NO_LOAD_EXTENSION=1`
* Direct shell-out to anything in `<projectDir>/.git/hooks/`

Any match in code paths that touch the snapshot staging dir, restore artifacts, or `<projectDir>/.papercusp/` fails the build with a clear “deserialize captured data through safe path only — see §15.24.”

```yaml
- name: Check forbidden deserializers in snapshot code paths
  run: |
    npx tsx scripts/check-forbidden-deserializers.ts \
      --paths apps/papercusp/lib/snapshot/ libs/papercusp-export-state/
```

## 15.23 Trust model

[Section titled “15.23 Trust model”](#1523-trust-model)

A snapshot is an artifact installed on a consumer’s machine that restores DB rows, source code, plugin enablement, and capability grants. The integrity guarantees the consumer needs:

1. **Authenticity**: this snapshot was published by the identity it claims (not a marketplace impersonator)
2. **Integrity**: the bytes received match what the publisher signed (not tampered in transit or at rest)
3. **Auditability**: the publication event is recorded somewhere the publisher can’t unilaterally erase
4. **Revocability**: the publisher can take down a snapshot they regret publishing; a compromised secret can be rotated

The signing chain delivers all four:

```text
                  Tenant (publisher)
                       │
                       │  authenticates via OIDC
                       ▼
   ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │  Sigstore Fulcio (CA)                  │
   │  Accepts: GitHub, Google, Microsoft,   │
   │  GitLab, Buildkite, ... (any           │
   │  Fulcio-trusted OIDC issuer)           │
   └─────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                 │  short-lived signing cert
                 │  (10-min validity)
                 ▼
   ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │  Cosign signs manifest.sha256          │
   │  Signature includes:                   │
   │    - identity (verified OIDC)          │
   │    - cert chain                        │
   │    - manifest sha256                   │
   └─────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                 │  signature event
                 ▼
   ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │  Sigstore Rekor (transparency log)     │
   │  Append-only, public, Merkle-proof'd   │
   └─────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
   ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │  manifest.json includes:               │
   │    - manifestSha256                    │  binds
   │    - filesNdjson.sha256 OR files[]     ├─►  to
   │    - file[].sha256 (per-file content)  │  bytes
   └────────────────────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
            Tarball blobs
```

**Consumer’s verification path** (run automatically by `papercusp install`):

1. Download manifest + signature from Gitea OCI registry
2. Verify signature against Rekor (the signature must have been logged)
3. Verify the OIDC identity in the cert chain matches the publishing tenant’s known identity (marketplace records the binding at first publish)
4. Verify `manifest.manifestSha256` matches the downloaded manifest
5. For each file in `files[]` (or via `filesNdjson`), verify the downloaded content’s sha256 matches
6. If any check fails, refuse install with a clear diagnostic

**What this guarantees**:

* Authenticity: ✓ via OIDC + Fulcio cert chain
* Integrity: ✓ via per-file sha256 + manifest sha256 + Cosign signature
* Auditability: ✓ via Rekor (anyone can independently verify a snapshot was logged at publish time, even if marketplace later becomes compromised)
* Revocability: ✓ via marketplace’s withdrawn-snapshot flow + tenant secret rotation (compromised secret invalidates future signatures)

**What this does NOT guarantee**:

* That the snapshot’s *content* is benign (signing != safety; see §15.24 abuse + moderation)
* That the publisher’s identity is who they claim to *humans* (Sigstore verifies the OIDC identity; humans on the marketplace may still be impersonators of well-known names — display the OIDC email/handle prominently in the UI)

**HMAC against tenantSecret is NOT a signature**. HMAC is symmetric: the marketplace knows the secret (to validate); anyone with the secret can forge a “signed” manifest. That’s authentication, not third-party- verifiable provenance. v1.0/v1.1 mentioned HMAC as an alternative to Cosign; v1.2 drops that — Cosign-keyless is required from day one.

**OIDC provider breadth**. Sigstore Fulcio accepts (as of writing) GitHub, Google, Microsoft, GitLab, Buildkite, and others. Tenants authenticate via whichever they prefer; identity is preserved in the cert chain. Saying “GitHub OAuth” would lock out non-GitHub users; the marketplace doesn’t.

## 15.24 Abuse + moderation

[Section titled “15.24 Abuse + moderation”](#1524-abuse--moderation)

A public marketplace for installable snapshots is a public-distribution problem. The spec covers secret leakage thoroughly (§15.9); this section covers the rest of the abuse surface.

### Code execution warning at install

[Section titled “Code execution warning at install”](#code-execution-warning-at-install)

Restoring a snapshot installs untrusted code AND untrusted data on the consumer’s machine. The pre-restore consent screen (§15.6 step 10) includes a prominent warning:

```text
This snapshot contains executable code from <tenant-display-name>.


  Source code:    <N> files, <M> MB
  Database state: <K> rows
  Plugins:        <P> plugin(s) requiring <C> capabilities


After restore, the source code is on your machine. Reviewing it before
running `papercusp run` is recommended:


    cd <projectDir> && less docs/features/F-001.md  (etc.)


The substrate will NOT auto-run `npm install`, `pip install`, or
`papercusp run` — you do that explicitly after reviewing.


Reviewing the code: this snapshot's source/ contains <N> files;
inspect for unfamiliar dependencies, post-install scripts, etc.


  [ Cancel install ]   [ Review source first ]   [ Continue install ]
```

### Deserialization safety

[Section titled “Deserialization safety”](#deserialization-safety)

A snapshot is untrusted code AND untrusted data. Every common unsafe-deserializer pattern is a confirmed RCE vector:

* `pickle.load` on Python state — Python pickles execute arbitrary code by design
* `yaml.load` (PyYAML default) instead of `yaml.safe_load` — YAML’s `!!python/object` tag is RCE
* `eval` / `Function()` / `vm.runInNewContext` on captured strings — including substrate-internal “we’ll just eval this cached query” paths
* SQLite database with `SQLITE_LOAD_EXTENSION` enabled at open — extension load runs arbitrary binary code
* Shell-out to `.git/hooks/*` if `.git/` is included — hooks are shell scripts the substrate’s git operations would invoke

The substrate’s deserialization posture is a hard rule: use **only safe deserializers** on captured artifacts.

**Safe list (allowed)**:

* `JSON.parse` (with reasonable size limits)
* CSV via `csv-parse` (well-trodden, no eval semantics)
* `pg_restore` (constrained by Postgres semantics; SQL injection pre-mitigated via `--single-transaction --variable=ON_ERROR_STOP=1`)
* Plain markdown via standard parser (no embedded script execution; HTML in markdown is rendered through a sanitizing parser)
* Plain text

**Forbidden on captured artifacts**:

* `pickle`, `dill`, `cloudpickle`, any Python serializer with code-execution semantics
* `yaml.load` — use `yaml.safe_load`
* `eval`, `Function`, `vm.runInNewContext`, `Reflect.apply` on captured strings
* SQLite open without `SQLITE_DBCONFIG_NO_LOAD_EXTENSION=1`
* `.git/hooks/*` execution — hooks are stripped at capture time (§15.4)

CI enforces (§15.22) — any forbidden deserializer call in code paths that touch snapshot staging or restored artifacts fails the build.

### Takedown process

[Section titled “Takedown process”](#takedown-process)

* **Public <abuse@papercuspai.com> mailbox**, monitored. 48-hour SLA for initial response on legal-content takedowns; 1-week SLA for terms-of- service complaints.
* **Marketplace UI report button** on every public snapshot detail page: “Report this snapshot” → category picker (illegal content / malware / impersonation / copyright / other) → free-text → emailed to abuse\@.
* **Soft-delete on first plausible report** within 72-hour cooldown. Bytes physically removed from R2 after the cooldown if the report is upheld.
* **Provenance chain auto-flagging**: if a snapshot is removed for illegal content, all snapshots with `derivedFrom.snapshotId` matching it (or in its derivative chain) are auto-flagged for review. The reviewer decides whether each derivative also requires takedown.
* **Audit log**: every takedown decision (date, reporter, reviewer, outcome, original tenant) recorded in an audit table that even the marketplace operator cannot delete.

### Illegal content reporting

[Section titled “Illegal content reporting”](#illegal-content-reporting)

If hosted snapshots contain CSAM, the marketplace operator is required under US law (18 U.S.C. § 2258A) to report to NCMEC’s CyberTipline. The marketplace ships with the NCMEC reporting flow built in:

* abuse@ inbox monitored for CSAM-flagged reports
* Verified CSAM → CyberTipline report within 24 hours (legally mandated; faster if possible)
* Snapshot bytes preserved for law-enforcement subpoena (90 days minimum), separate from the public R2 retention policy

For other illegal content (US-DMCA copyright, jurisdiction-specific hate speech, malware), the takedown process above applies; specific legal-counsel review required for jurisdiction-specific issues.

### ToS gate at first publish

[Section titled “ToS gate at first publish”](#tos-gate-at-first-publish)

Tenants must accept the marketplace ToS before first publish. The ToS commits the tenant to:

* “I won’t publish malware, illegal content, or content I don’t have the right to distribute”
* “I understand my snapshots may be reviewed and removed”
* “I understand my OIDC-verified identity is recorded with each publish for abuse-response purposes”
* “I agree to NCMEC reporting flows for CSAM”
* DMCA-style “I agree the marketplace is a safe-harbor host; I am responsible for content I publish”

Standard terms; specific drafting requires legal review pre-launch.

### First-run sandbox option (v1.1+)

[Section titled “First-run sandbox option (v1.1+)”](#first-run-sandbox-option-v11)

Per §15.14 future work: “Try this snapshot in an E2B sandbox before installing locally” — limits blast radius for evaluating untrusted snapshots. v1 ships without this; v1.1 adds it as a button on the marketplace detail page.

## 15.25 Plugin snapshot manifest registry

[Section titled “15.25 Plugin snapshot manifest registry”](#1525-plugin-snapshot-manifest-registry)

Plugins that persist state outside per-harness Postgres schemas (e.g., binary tool caches, vector embeddings) need an explicit declaration of what to capture and restore. Without it, snapshots silently drop the plugin’s state across fork boundaries.

The substrate’s `papercusp.json` plugin manifest gains a `snapshot:` block (mirroring the shared-table-filter registry pattern from §15.5):

```json
{
  "id": "@papercupai/vscode-server",
  "version": "0.4.2",
  "snapshot": {
    "include": [
      {
        "kind": "pg-schema",
        "name": "harness_<slug>.plugin_vscode_settings",
        "comment": "Per-harness vscode preferences"
      },
      {
        "kind": "file-glob",
        "pattern": "<projectDir>/.papercusp/plugins/vscode/config.json",
        "comment": "Per-harness vscode config; small, JSON, safe"
      }
    ],
    "exclude": [
      {
        "kind": "file-glob",
        "pattern": "<projectDir>/.papercusp/plugins/vscode/cache/",
        "comment": "Re-derivable on first run"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Capture pass behavior

[Section titled “Capture pass behavior”](#capture-pass-behavior)

For each enabled plugin in `manifest.plugins[]`:

* If plugin has a `snapshot:` block:

  * Walk `include[]` paths, copy into `<staging>/state/plugin-<slug>/`
  * Skip everything matching `exclude[]` patterns
  * Plugin’s pg schemas captured as part of the per-harness pg\_dump (already done in §15.5 step 3)

* If plugin has no `snapshot:` block:

  * Print warning: `plugin <id> has no snapshot block; per-plugin state may not be captured (consult plugin author)`
  * Continue capture (don’t block; warning is the deterrent)

### Restore pass behavior

[Section titled “Restore pass behavior”](#restore-pass-behavior)

For each plugin in `manifest.plugins[]`:

* Verify plugin is installed locally (§15.6 step 10a)
* Verify cap declarations match actual installed (§15.6 step 10b)
* For plugins with a `snapshot:` block: copy `state/plugin-<slug>/` contents back to the declared `include[]` paths
* For plugins without one: warn, don’t restore plugin state, continue

### Cross-reference to §10 (Capabilities)

[Section titled “Cross-reference to §10 (Capabilities)”](#cross-reference-to-10-capabilities)

The broader question — “should the substrate force plugins to live only in per-harness Postgres schemas, or allow opt-out filesystem state via the snapshot block?” — is a §10 architectural conversation, not a snapshot-spec decision. The §15.25 registry pattern is the v1 mechanism for the practical need; whether to harden it via capability denials (`filesystem:write:outside-projectdir = false` for all plugins forever) is a §10 owner decision separate from this spec.

For v1: registry as documented above. For v2+: §10 owner decides.

### CI enforcement

[Section titled “CI enforcement”](#ci-enforcement)

Plugin manifests without a `snapshot:` block produce an install-time warning. Plugin authors who want to declare “we have no per-plugin state to snapshot” do so explicitly via:

```json
{
  "snapshot": { "kind": "stateless" }
}
```

This silences the warning. Plugins with neither a real `snapshot:` block nor `stateless` declaration get the warning every install, which incentivizes plugin authors to make the explicit declaration.

# 16. Publishing — hosted Cloudflare publishing (v3)

Status: code complete, awaiting Cloudflare bootstrap

**Publishing** — one-click public publishing from coding harnesses. Worker (`apps/papercusp-publish/`), shared auth lib (`libs/papercusp-publish-auth/`), substrate plugin (`@papercupai/cloudflare-pages-hosted`), and Settings UI all landed 2026-04-28. Live deployment waits on \`wrangler d1/kv create + secret put

* deploy`and a wildcard cert on`\*.preview\.papercuspai.com\`.

Three rounds of architectural review have been incorporated (v1 → v2 → v3). Once a real user publishes their first project this page folds into §7 (Plugin extension points) and §11 (Distribution).

## 15.0 Why this exists

[Section titled “15.0 Why this exists”](#150-why-this-exists)

A non-technical user runs a coding harness, describes what they want in plain English, watches the harness build it, and clicks **Publish**. Within \~30 seconds they get a public URL they can share. **They never touch a Cloudflare credential, never create an API token, never pre-create a project.**

Without this, “ship the app” is a half-day of Cloudflare onboarding for the user — a step where the AI-built-an-app value proposition crashes into “log into Cloudflare, generate a Pages:Edit token with these exact permissions, copy your account UUID from the right sidebar…” and the user gives up.

The mechanism is a hosted publish service we run, fronting our own Cloudflare account. Users borrow our infra; we hold the master token; the content’s served on a vanity subdomain we control.

## 15.1 Goals + non-goals

[Section titled “15.1 Goals + non-goals”](#151-goals--non-goals)

**Goals**

* One click from harness header → live public URL within \~30 seconds.
* Zero credentials handled by the user, ever.
* Coding harness only — `papercup-org` parents and other non-coding templates do not get a Publish button.
* Bounded blast radius if our master Cloudflare account is suspended: every user can recover their projects without our infra.

**Non-goals (v1)**

* Custom user-owned domains. v1 deploys to `*.preview.papercuspai.com`.
* Private/access-gated deployments. v1 is fully public; private mode is spec’d here but built later.
* Build pipelines. v1 publishes static files from `<project>/<exportDir>`; the harness already produced the output.
* Paid-tier billing. Schema supports `tenants.tier` from day one; enforcement of paid limits comes later.

## 15.2 Architecture

[Section titled “15.2 Architecture”](#152-architecture)

```text
┌────────────────────────────┐         ┌───────────────────────────────────┐         ┌─────────────────┐
│  user's coding harness     │         │  publish.papercuspai.com           │         │   Cloudflare    │
│  (substrate at :3055)      │         │  (Worker + D1 + KV + R2)          │         │   Pages API     │
│                            │         │                                   │         │                 │
│  click Publish             │         │  POST /publish/start              │         │                 │
│   ↓                        │         │  ├─ JWT validate (HS256+jti+sha)  │         │                 │
│  walks out/, computes      │  jwt+   │  ├─ replay check (D1 unique-key)  │         │                 │
│  per-file sha256 +         ├────────►│  ├─ rate-limit (KV burst+daily+IP)│         │                 │
│  canonical manifest        │ manifest│  ├─ ensure CF project (D1 cache)  │         │                 │
│  POSTs                     │         │  └─ returns deploymentId +        │         │                 │
│   ↓                        │         │      missing-files upload URLs    │         │                 │
│  PUT each file             ├ stream ►│  proxy stream (no buffer)         ├ master ►│  /files         │
│  (only the missing ones)   │         │  ┌─ verify per-file sha256        │  token  │                 │
│   ↓                        │         │                                   │         │                 │
│  POST /publish/finalize    ├────────►│  ├─ create CF deployment          ├────────►│  deployments    │
│                            │         │  └─ archive manifest+files to R2  │         │                 │
│   ↓                        │         │                                   │  status │                 │
│  poll /status/:depId       ├────────►│  ── returns CF status             │◄────────┤                 │
│   ↓                        │         │                                   │         │                 │
│  toast: live at <vanity>   │         │  *.preview.papercuspai.com via     │         │                 │
└────────────────────────────┘         │  Worker route → CF Pages auto     │         │                 │
                                       │  subdomain                        │         │                 │
                                       └───────────────────────────────────┘         └─────────────────┘
```

## 15.3 Data model

[Section titled “15.3 Data model”](#153-data-model)

### D1 — durable state

[Section titled “D1 — durable state”](#d1--durable-state)

```sql
CREATE TABLE tenants (
  id              text primary key,           -- tnt_<10-base32>
  secret_hash     text not null,              -- HMAC-SHA256(secret, HASH_PEPPER)
  secret_hash_v   int  not null default 1,    -- KDF version, for rotation
  rotated_from    text,                       -- previous tenant id, audit
  created_at      int  not null,              -- epoch ms
  last_used_at    int,
  last_ip         text,
  status          text default 'active',      -- active | revoked | banned
  tier            text default 'free',        -- free | paid | self-host-byo
  notes           text                        -- admin notes
);


CREATE TABLE projects (
  tenant_id        text not null references tenants(id),
  harness_slug     text not null,
  cf_project_name  text not null,             -- sha256(secret||harness)[:16] + "-" + sanitize(harness)
  cf_subdomain     text,
  vanity_subdomain text,                       -- "<harness>-<rand>" on preview.papercuspai.com
  created_at       int not null,
  primary key (tenant_id, harness_slug)
);


CREATE TABLE deployments (
  id               text primary key,           -- dep_<8-base32>
  tenant_id        text not null references tenants(id),
  harness_slug     text not null,
  cf_deployment_id text not null,              -- NOT NULL: row only inserted after CF returns
  vanity_url       text,
  manifest_sha     text,                       -- canonical manifest sha256, audit + dedup
  archive_path     text,                       -- R2 key: "<tenant>/<deployment>/" prefix
  bytes_total      int,
  files_count      int,
  status           text default 'building',    -- pending_create | uploading | building | live | failed
  failure_reason   text,
  created_at       int not null,
  completed_at     int
);


-- Replay protection — atomic via PRIMARY KEY (D1's serializable per-DB transactions)
CREATE TABLE jti_used (
  jti  text primary key,
  exp  int not null
);


-- Audit log — kept indefinitely for CF abuse responses
CREATE TABLE audit_publishes (
  id              integer primary key autoincrement,
  tenant_id       text not null,
  harness_slug    text not null,
  deployment_id   text,
  ip              text,
  ua              text,
  manifest_sha    text,
  bytes_total     int,
  outcome         text,                       -- ok | rate_limited | invalid_jwt | banned | upload_failed | cf_error
  ts              int not null
);
CREATE INDEX idx_audit_ts             ON audit_publishes(ts);
CREATE INDEX idx_audit_tenant_ts      ON audit_publishes(tenant_id, ts);
CREATE INDEX idx_audit_harness_ts     ON audit_publishes(harness_slug, ts);
CREATE INDEX idx_audit_ip_ts          ON audit_publishes(ip, ts);
```

### KV — counters + ephemeral state

[Section titled “KV — counters + ephemeral state”](#kv--counters--ephemeral-state)

| Key                                 | Purpose                                                                             | TTL    |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| `ratelimit:burst:<tenantId>`        | per-tenant 5/min                                                                    | 60s    |
| `ratelimit:daily:<tenantId>`        | per-tenant 50/day free, 500/day paid                                                | 86400s |
| `ratelimit:ip-publish-daily:<ip>`   | 50/day per IP, **independent of tenant** (closes the wipe-and-re-register loophole) | 86400s |
| `ratelimit:ip-register-hourly:<ip>` | 10/hour per IP on `/register-tenant`                                                | 3600s  |
| `upload:<deploymentId>:<sha256>`    | per-file upload token state                                                         | 900s   |

### R2 — artifact retention (the eject path’s fire exit)

[Section titled “R2 — artifact retention (the eject path’s fire exit)”](#r2--artifact-retention-the-eject-paths-fire-exit)

Bucket `papercusp-publish-archive`. At `/publish/finalize` *after* CF deployment succeeds, write:

```plaintext
<bucket>/<tenantId>/<deploymentId>/manifest.json
<bucket>/<tenantId>/<deploymentId>/files/<sha256>.bin    ← per file
```

Lifecycle: **30 days for free tier, 1 year for paid**. Cron deletes expired prefixes.

The eject script reads from R2, *not* CF Pages API. R2 is a separate product on the same account; suspension scopes can differ. If both R2 and Pages are nuked, the substrate still has the source on the user’s local machine (`<project>/<exportDir>`) and can re-upload to BYO-CF — two independent recovery paths.

R2 cost: \~$0.015/GB-month. Typical site is \~5 MB; 1k tenants ≈ 5 GB ≈ $0.07/mo. Pennies.

## 15.4 Authentication + replay protection

[Section titled “15.4 Authentication + replay protection”](#154-authentication--replay-protection)

### Per-substrate handshake — one time

[Section titled “Per-substrate handshake — one time”](#per-substrate-handshake--one-time)

`POST publish.papercuspai.com/register-tenant` with `Content-Type: application/json`, body `{}` (anonymous v1 — when OAuth ships, auth header binds the tenant to a user account). Returns:

```json
{ "tenantId": "tnt_a3kf9xe2pq", "tenantSecret": "<32-byte base64url>" }
```

Stored in `~/.papercusp/publish-credentials.json` (chmod 600). The `tenantSecret` is high-entropy machine-generated — argon2’s slow-hash advantage doesn’t apply here, so we use HMAC-SHA256 with a server-side `HASH_PEPPER` for \~µs verification.

### Per-publish JWT

[Section titled “Per-publish JWT”](#per-publish-jwt)

```plaintext
header  { alg: "HS256", typ: "JWT" }
claims  {
  sub:    "<tenantId>",
  iat:    <epoch-sec>,
  exp:    iat + 60,
  jti:    <16-byte random base64url>,
  sha256: <hex of canonical-manifest-sha256>     // binds JWT to upload body
}
sig     HMAC-SHA256(header.claims, tenantSecret)
```

Worker validation order:

1. Verify HMAC signature against tenant’s `secret_hash` (lookup by `sub`).
2. Reject if `now > exp` or `now < iat - 5s` (clock skew tolerance).
3. `INSERT INTO jti_used (jti, exp) VALUES (?, ?)` — duplicate primary key throws → 401. **D1 PRIMARY KEY constraint is the atomic replay guard, not KV `put`.**
4. On `/publish/start`, recompute canonical manifest sha256 from the request body; reject if `!== claims.sha256`.

### Canonical manifest (RFC 8785 / JCS)

[Section titled “Canonical manifest (RFC 8785 / JCS)”](#canonical-manifest-rfc-8785--jcs)

```json
{
  "files": [
    { "path": "index.html", "sha256": "abc...", "bytes": 1024 }
  ],
  "deployment_slug": "sheets2"
}
```

Substrate and Worker both run the same JCS library. Files pre-sorted by NFC-normalized path; numbers in canonical form; no whitespace. Without this, path-encoding mismatches (NFC vs NFD on macOS, key-order differences across JSON serializers) silently break JWT signature validation and burn debug hours.

### Tenant lifecycle

[Section titled “Tenant lifecycle”](#tenant-lifecycle)

* **Rotate:** `POST /rotate-secret` with old secret → returns new secret. Old secret invalidated immediately (`secret_hash` updated atomically; `rotated_from` records the previous tenant id for audit).
* **Revoke:** admin sets `tenants.status = 'revoked'`; every subsequent publish returns 401. User must re-register from a fresh substrate install.
* **Last-used audit:** every successful publish updates `last_used_at` + `last_ip`. Surfaces “this tenant published from a new IP” via the Settings UI for the operator to notice.

## 15.5 Rate-limit tiers (final ordering)

[Section titled “15.5 Rate-limit tiers (final ordering)”](#155-rate-limit-tiers-final-ordering)

1. **Per-tenant daily** — 50/day free, 500/day paid. KV `ratelimit:daily:<tid>`.
2. **Per-tenant burst** — 5/min. KV `ratelimit:burst:<tid>`.
3. **Per-IP publish-daily** — 50/day, **independent of tenant**. KV `ratelimit:ip-publish-daily:<ip>`. Closes the wipe-`~/.papercusp` and re-register loophole that per-IP-on-registration alone doesn’t.
4. **Per-IP register-hourly** — 10/hour on `/register-tenant`. KV `ratelimit:ip-register-hourly:<ip>`.
5. **Per-file size cap** — 25 MB (CF Pages hard limit per file).
6. **Per-deployment file count cap** — 20,000 (CF hard limit).
7. **Per-deployment total size cap** — 1 GB (our policy; CF doesn’t enforce — saves us bandwidth abuse).

## 15.6 Endpoint reference

[Section titled “15.6 Endpoint reference”](#156-endpoint-reference)

### `POST /register-tenant`

[Section titled “POST /register-tenant”](#post-register-tenant)

* **Auth:** none (v1) / GitHub OAuth (v1.1).
* **Body:** `{}` for v1.
* **Returns:** `{ tenantId, tenantSecret }`. Substrate writes to `~/.papercusp/publish-credentials.json`.
* **Rate limit:** 10/hour per IP.

### `POST /publish/start`

[Section titled “POST /publish/start”](#post-publishstart)

* **Auth:** JWT.

* **Body:** canonical manifest (see §15.4).

* **Returns:**

  ```json
  {
    "deploymentId": "dep_<8>",
    "missing": [
      { "path": "index.html", "sha256": "...", "uploadUrl": "https://publish.papercuspai.com/publish/file/<id>?token=..." }
    ],
    "vanityUrl": "https://sheets2-a4f9c.preview.papercuspai.com",
    "createdProject": false
  }
  ```

* **Idempotency:** re-POSTing the same manifest with the same JWT-sha256 within 30 minutes returns the same `deploymentId` with `missing[]` filtered to still-not-uploaded files. **Resumable uploads.**

### `PUT /publish/file/<deploymentId>?token=<signedUrlToken>`

[Section titled “PUT /publish/file/\<deploymentId>?token=\<signedUrlToken>”](#put-publishfiledeploymentidtokensignedurltoken)

* **Auth:** signed-URL HMAC token (`HMAC(JWT_SECRET, deploymentId+sha256+exp)`).
* **Body:** raw file bytes.
* **Worker behavior:** streams body to CF `/pages/projects/<n>/files` using the master token, *without buffering* (Workers Streams API). No bandwidth cost on the Worker; no subrequest budget cost beyond 1 per file. **Verifies sha256(body) === claimed sha256** before forwarding; rejects on mismatch.
* **Workers Paid prerequisite:** $5/mo plan provides 1,000 subrequests per Worker invocation, vs 50 on Free. Required for ≥40-file deployments.

### `POST /publish/finalize`

[Section titled “POST /publish/finalize”](#post-publishfinalize)

* **Auth:** JWT.

* **Body:** `{ deploymentId }`.

* **Worker behavior:**

  1. Verify all `missing[]` files have been uploaded.
  2. Call CF `/pages/projects/<name>/deployments` to publish.
  3. Insert `deployments` row with `status='building', cf_deployment_id=<...>`.
  4. Asynchronously archive `manifest.json` + each `<sha256>.bin` to R2.
  5. Return `{ vanityUrl, status: 'building' }`.

### `GET /publish/status/<deploymentId>`

[Section titled “GET /publish/status/\<deploymentId>”](#get-publishstatusdeploymentid)

* **Auth:** JWT.
* **Returns:** `{ status: 'building' | 'live' | 'failed', vanityUrl, failureReason? }`.
* **Substrate polling:** 1s for first 10s, 5s thereafter, total cap 5 min, jittered ±20%.

### `POST /rotate-secret`

[Section titled “POST /rotate-secret”](#post-rotate-secret)

* **Auth:** JWT (signed by old secret).
* **Returns:** `{ tenantSecret: <new> }`. Old secret invalidated atomic with new secret install (UPDATE in single transaction).

### `DELETE /publish/<harness>` *(v1.1)*

[Section titled “DELETE /publish/\<harness> (v1.1)”](#delete-publishharness-v11)

* **Auth:** JWT.
* **Effect:** removes the deployment, frees the project, GCs R2 archive. Plugin gets an Unpublish row in config→Plugins.

### `GET /admin/gc` *(cron, internal)*

[Section titled “GET /admin/gc (cron, internal)”](#get-admingc-cron-internal)

* Deletes `deployments` rows in `status='uploading' AND created_at < now-1h`. Calls CF `DELETE /deployments/<id>` for each abandoned half- upload to free the CF project. Deletes R2 prefixes past retention TTL.

## 15.7 Eject-to-own-CF (data model v1, button v1.1)

[Section titled “15.7 Eject-to-own-CF (data model v1, button v1.1)”](#157-eject-to-own-cf-data-model-v1-button-v11)

The fire exit. Designed v1 because designing it later is too late; the button ships v1.1.

### Plugin config schema additions

[Section titled “Plugin config schema additions”](#plugin-config-schema-additions)

```json
{
  "byoCloudflareToken":     "<user's Pages:Edit token, optional>",
  "byoCloudflareAccountId": "<user's CF account UUID, optional>"
}
```

When both are present, the plugin **bypasses** `publish.papercuspai.com` entirely and calls CF Pages directly with the user’s own token. Same plugin, two configurations. Free forever for self-hosters who bring their own credentials.

### Eject migration script

[Section titled “Eject migration script”](#eject-migration-script)

`apps/papercusp-publish/scripts/eject.ts` — admin-runnable. For each tenant’s projects:

1. Read manifest + per-file content from **R2**, not CF Pages API. (R2 is the fire exit’s load-bearing component. CF Pages API is unavailable when the master account is suspended; that’s the entire problem.)
2. Re-upload to user’s BYO CF account using their token.
3. Rewrite plugin config: set `byoCloudflareToken` + `byoCloudflareAccountId`.
4. Delete the now-orphaned R2 prefix.

**Tertiary fallback:** if R2 retention has expired, the substrate’s local `<project>/<exportDir>` still has the source — re-publish from local. Two independent recovery paths.

### Why this matters

[Section titled “Why this matters”](#why-this-matters)

WordPress.com → WordPress.org structurally has the same bad-actor blast radius problem in miniature. One user publishing illegal content suspends the master account; *every* user’s site goes down. The eject path means “every user’s site goes down for \~hours, not forever” — because their site rebuilds from R2 (and worst case: from local source). That’s a tolerable degradation; permanent loss is not.

## 15.8 Plugin scoping — `requiresTemplateKinds`

[Section titled “15.8 Plugin scoping — requiresTemplateKinds”](#158-plugin-scoping--requirestemplatekinds)

The hosted-publish plugin is coding-harness-only by design. Other templates don’t show the Publish button. Three places enforce this:

### Plugin manifest gains a new field

[Section titled “Plugin manifest gains a new field”](#plugin-manifest-gains-a-new-field)

```json
{
  "name": "@papercupai/cloudflare-pages-hosted",
  "kind": "plugin",
  "requiresTemplateKinds": ["coding"]
}
```

Plural — `["coding", "department"]` is supported; a plugin that works on multiple template kinds declares them all. Singular form was rejected because it’d need to grow to plural day two.

### Enforcement points

[Section titled “Enforcement points”](#enforcement-points)

| Where                            | Behavior                                                                                                                                |
| -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `papercusp plugin enable <slug>` | Refuses with: `error: plugin "@papercupai/cloudflare-pages-hosted" requires templateKinds=[coding]; harness "papercup-org" is kind=org` |
| Substrate UI plugin cards        | Disabled “Enable” button + tooltip: “Requires a coding harness.”                                                                        |
| Marketplace listings             | Constraint pill: `🪧 coding harnesses only` next to the plugin name.                                                                    |

Templates declare their kind via `papercusp.json`:

```json
{ "kind": "template", "templateKind": "coding" }
```

Existing templates (papercup-coding, papercup-org, …) get this field in a back-compat update. Templates without `templateKind` are treated as `'coding'` by default for back-compat; templates that opt-in explicitly are exact.

## 15.9 Project name + URL

[Section titled “15.9 Project name + URL”](#159-project-name--url)

### CF project name (account-internal)

[Section titled “CF project name (account-internal)”](#cf-project-name-account-internal)

```plaintext
sha256(tenantSecret || "/" || harnessSlug).slice(0, 16) + "-" + sanitize(harnessSlug)
```

Per-(tenant, harness) hash. Two tenants both creating `sheets` get different prefixes; one tenant’s projects don’t cluster in CF’s account-internal listings. Hides cross-project tenant correlation even from CF support engineers reading abuse reports.

### Vanity URL (user-visible)

[Section titled “Vanity URL (user-visible)”](#vanity-url-user-visible)

```plaintext
<sanitized-harness-slug>-<8-base32-random>.preview.papercuspai.com
```

The 8-base32-random is per-deployment; same harness republished gets a different URL. Prevents URL enumeration of one user’s project history.

User can override the user-facing slug at publish time (defaults to harness slug, sanitized). Helps when the harness was named “tax-deduction-calculator-2026” but you want the public URL to say “calculator”.

### Wildcard subdomain routing

[Section titled “Wildcard subdomain routing”](#wildcard-subdomain-routing)

`*.preview.papercuspai.com` → Worker route → looks up `projects.vanity_subdomain` → proxies to the auto-generated CF `<prefix>.pages.dev` for that project. CF’s Pages.dev URL never leaks to the user.

## 15.10 What gets built

[Section titled “15.10 What gets built”](#1510-what-gets-built)

| # | Component                                                                                                    | LOC         |
| - | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------- |
| 1 | `apps/papercusp-publish/` Worker — D1 + KV + JCS canonicalizer + JWT + signed-URL helpers + R2 archive write | 1,000-1,400 |
| 2 | `@papercupai/cloudflare-pages-hosted` plugin — JCS manifest, retry/resume on partial upload, BYO-CF fallback | \~500       |
| 3 | Substrate “Publishing” settings page — mode selector, tenant info, rotate-secret button                      | \~250       |
| 4 | `papercup-coding` template — adds `recommendedPlugins`                                                       | 5 lines     |
| 5 | DNS — wildcard cert + Worker route on `*.preview.papercuspai.com` + `publish.papercuspai.com`                | \~3 hours   |
| 6 | Eject script reading from R2                                                                                 | \~200       |
| 7 | `requiresTemplateKinds` field — spec + CLI loader + UI gating + marketplace pill                             | \~300       |
| 8 | R2 bucket setup + lifecycle rules + cleanup cron                                                             | \~150       |

**Total: \~2.5 days.**

## 15.11 Admin one-time setup

[Section titled “15.11 Admin one-time setup”](#1511-admin-one-time-setup)

1. **Cloudflare master account:** scope a `Pages:Edit` token (verify no DNS/Workers/R2 perms). Save as `CF_MASTER_TOKEN`.
2. **Cloudflare R2:** create bucket `papercusp-publish-archive`, generate scoped R2 token. Save as `R2_ACCESS_KEY` / `R2_SECRET_KEY`.
3. **Generate `JWT_SECRET`** — 32 random bytes, base64.
4. **Generate `HASH_PEPPER`** — 32 random bytes, base64. Separate from `JWT_SECRET`.
5. `wrangler kv:namespace create papercusp-publish-counters`.
6. `wrangler d1 create papercusp-publish` + apply migration.
7. **Workers Paid plan** ($5/mo) — confirmed prerequisite.
8. `wrangler deploy` Worker.
9. DNS: `*.preview.papercuspai.com` and `publish.papercuspai.com` → Worker route. Wildcard cert via CF managed cert (1-click in dashboard).
10. Cron: daily `/admin/gc` for stale uploads + R2 archive expiry.
11. Smoke test from a clean machine.

## 15.12 What’s NOT in v1

[Section titled “15.12 What’s NOT in v1”](#1512-whats-not-in-v1)

* **Multi-master-account sharding.** Useful at scale; R2 retention provides a real recovery path, so a single master account is acceptable for v1. Worth revisiting at 1k+ paying users.
* **Machine fingerprinting** for tenant binding. Privacy-invasive; per-IP daily cap (§15.5 #3) closes the abuse loop without it.
* **Custom user-owned domains.** v1 deploys to `*.preview.papercuspai.com` only; user-supplied domains in v1.1.
* **Private mode** via Cloudflare Access. Schema field `projects.access_policy: 'public' | 'private'` reserved; Worker enforcement v1.1.
* **Paid-tier billing.** `tenants.tier` column exists; defer billing until we have users.

## 15.13 Risk register

[Section titled “15.13 Risk register”](#1513-risk-register)

| Risk                                                  | Likelihood                         | Impact                                                | Mitigation                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| CF master account suspended for one user’s content    | Real-mode (not tail)               | Every user’s site offline                             | R2 archive retention + eject script (§15.7); reduces to “outage during eject”                    |
| `CF_MASTER_TOKEN` leaks                               | Low (Workers secret)               | Every project republishable by attacker               | Token scoped Pages-only (no DNS/R2), rotate quarterly, CF analytics alerting on call-rate spikes |
| Workers subrequest cap (50 free / 1k paid)            | Real on Workers Paid for monorepos | 1k+ file deployments fail                             | `/publish/upload-batch` endpoint as fallback, defer to v1.1                                      |
| User publishes 10 GB of static MP4s                   | Possible                           | Bandwidth costs balloon                               | Per-deployment 1 GB cap (§15.5 #7); per-tenant daily limit                                       |
| First-publish cold-start (\~+3s for project creation) | Every new harness                  | Slightly slower initial Publish                       | Pre-warm `ensureProject` at plugin enable time so first publish is warm                          |
| Half-completed upload (network drop, browser close)   | Real, common                       | Project in `status=uploading` forever, KV tokens leak | Resumable upload via `/publish/start` idempotency (§15.6); cron GC at 1h (§15.6)                 |

## 15.14 Open questions (decide before code)

[Section titled “15.14 Open questions (decide before code)”](#1514-open-questions-decide-before-code)

1. **R2 retention period** — proposal: 30 days free / 1 year paid. Alternatives: 90 days for everyone (simpler), 7 days free / 90 days paid (cheaper).
2. **Workers Paid commitment** — $5/mo locked in from day one. Confirm.
3. **OAuth for `/register-tenant`** — v1 is anonymous (tenant-per-machine). v1.1 binds tenants to GitHub user via OAuth. If the marketplace already has a GitHub OAuth app, reuse it; otherwise spec scopes (`Pages:Edit` only, no `repo`).

## 15.15 Implementation order

[Section titled “15.15 Implementation order”](#1515-implementation-order)

**Day 1**

* Worker scaffold + D1 schema (tenants, projects, deployments, jti\_used, audit\_publishes) + KV bindings + R2 binding (\~5h)
* JWT (HS256+jti+sha256) + JCS canonicalizer + HMAC-pepper secret hashing (\~3h)
* `/register-tenant` + `/publish/start` + per-IP & per-tenant rate limits (\~3h)

**Day 2**

* File-PUT proxy (Worker streams body to CF without buffering) (\~3h)
* `/publish/finalize` + R2 archive write + status polling endpoint (\~4h)
* `/publish/start` resume semantics + GC cron (\~2h)

**Day 2.5**

* DNS + URL-rewrite Worker route on `*.preview.papercuspai.com` (\~3h)
* Plugin (JCS manifest, resume on partial upload, polling, BYO-CF fallback) (\~4h)
* Settings UI + eject script + smoke test + docs (\~3h)
