## 14. What “PASS” means

[Section titled “14. What “PASS” means”](#14-what-pass-means)

PASS only if **all of**:

1. The action was performed via verdict (clicks/fills, not curl).
2. The DOM after the action matches the documented expectation.
3. Backend state (where applicable) is corroborated via `curl` or the operator log.
4. No console errors with severity ≥ `error` were emitted by the action (run `verdict console error`).

Anything else → `FAIL` or `INCONCLUSIVE`. Don’t report PASS without positive evidence — silence is not success.

## 15. Common gotchas

[Section titled “15. Common gotchas”](#15-common-gotchas)

* **Verdict shares chromium with the human user.** Long click-and-wait sequences fail when the user is browsing. Run `verdict status` first.
* **Sonner Toasts are lazy.** `[data-sonner-toaster]` only mounts when at least one toast is active. The empty `<section aria-label="Notifications alt+T">` is just the accessibility announcer. To assert a toast appeared, query `[data-sonner-toaster] li` *during* the action, not after the toast has timed out.
* **Add-plugin enable is slow (3–9s).** No spinner. Wait for `curl /api/plugins/enabled` to reflect the change; don’t time out early.
* **`/marketplace` URL behavior changed.** It now renders the Overview tab directly (4 tabs total: Overview, Templates, Plugins, Snapshots) — not a redirect to `/templates`.
* **Stream parser unwrap.** Oracle stream events arrive as `{type:"stream_event", event:{type:"content_block_delta", delta:{...}}}` — parsing top-level `content_block_delta` silently drops every text token. (Already handled server-side; relevant if you’re writing a new SSE consumer.)
* **Stale Vite parse cache.** If a JSX parse error references a line that doesn’t match the on-disk file, the cache is stale. `rm -rf apps/operator-vite/node_modules/.vite` and restart. (Next.js is retired — there is no `.next` cache anymore.)
* **Harness tab nav uses `?panel=`.** `panel=plugin:<id>` selects a plugin-contributed tab. Test these the same way as built-in tabs.
* **`tauri-agent-tools screenshot --selector` is flaky on tiny elements.** A short input (e.g. the operator composer at \~187×42 px) sometimes returns a 1×1 PNG. Workaround: `screenshot --title Papercusp -o full.png` then crop in ImageMagick using the rect from `eval "JSON.stringify($('input').getBoundingClientRect())"`.
* **`ipc-monitor` is silent for the operator chat.** The composer sends via HTTP/SSE to `/api/agent-mcp/operator-converse`, not via Tauri IPC. Use `console-monitor`, `rust-logs`, or `curl /api/operator/conversations/<id>` to corroborate. `ipc-monitor` *is* the right tool for plugin/host wiring, workspace switching, and shell-sidecar calls.
* **Bridge port is per-process.** `tauri-agent-tools probe` reports the live port (e.g. `34875`); restart the dev shell and the port changes. Always `probe` before scripting a sequence.
* **Radix tabs (and other pointerdown-activated Radix widgets) ignore plain `click`.** A programmatic `el.click()` (or the bridge `click` verb) dispatches only a `click` event; Radix `Tabs` activate on *pointerdown*, so the tab looks clicked but selection and the nuqs `?tab=` param never change — and your test silently measures nothing. Dispatch the full sequence: `for (const t of ['pointerdown','mousedown','pointerup','mouseup','click']) el.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent(t,{bubbles:true,cancelable:true,view:window}))`. Plain anchors are fine with `click`. (Found 2026-06-10; cost a full battery round of invalid tab numbers.)
* **Close the Web Inspector before ANY memory or perf measurement.** All Tauri instances share one webview profile (`~/.local/share/com.papercusp.desktop`), and it restores the inspector OPEN from the last session. The inspector’s record buffers (its Network tab logs every SSE/API frame) grew \~1.9 GB across two nav batteries on 2026-06-10 and looked exactly like an app leak — closing it dropped RSS from 2.7 GB to 819 MB instantly. Latency numbers were unaffected; memory numbers with it open are garbage.
* **Don’t measure under `tauri dev` on the shared dev box — launch the bare debug binary.** `tauri dev` watches `src-tauri/**`, and the fleet edits that tree continuously: a peer’s mid-flight Rust edit kills and rebuilds your app mid-test (and a peer’s compile error leaves you appless). Launch `./src-tauri/target/debug/papercusp-desktop` directly (the dev wrapper + bridge are compiled in) and pick the target via the build-switcher rail or a devUrl-restored URL.
* **Wayland trap: a bare `DISPLAY=:9X` launch can land on the owner’s desktop.** GTK prefers Wayland when `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set, so the isolated-Xvfb recipe silently opens the window on the live seat (focus-steal). Always launch with `env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY GDK_BACKEND=x11 DISPLAY=:9X …`.
* **`screenshot` verb may demand sway/grim** (it probes the host platform, not your X11 instance). Fallback that always works on an Xvfb display: `WID=$(DISPLAY=:9X xdotool search --name Papercusp | tail -1); DISPLAY=:9X import -window $WID shot.png`.
* **`operator-converse` trigger enum.** When poking `/api/agent-mcp/operator-converse` directly, `trigger` must be one of `user_message | quiet_wait_resume | open_canvas | user_says_ready | user_welcomed | continue` — anything else streams a single `event: error` frame (`invalid_args`) and closes.

### 15.4 Xvfb / xdotool / OCR fallback cookbook

[Section titled “15.4 Xvfb / xdotool / OCR fallback cookbook”](#154-xvfb--xdotool--ocr-fallback-cookbook)

The bridge covers 99% of cases. Reach for this stack only when:

* You’re on a **release build** (the bridge is `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`).
* You’re on **macOS** and the bridge isn’t compiled in for that target yet.
* You need to verify **visual** behavior the DOM can’t express (animation timing, font rendering, paint-order glitches).
* The Tauri process **crashed** and you need forensics on the dead window (use `tauri-agent-tools diagnose` first; this is a deeper fallback).

Bare `Xvfb` has no GPU/GL — WebKitGTK won’t paint → every screenshot is blank

A plain `Xvfb` is a **software framebuffer with no DRI3/GL** (you’ll see `libEGL warning: DRI3 error: Could not get DRI3 device` in the app log). WebKitGTK’s accelerated compositor then **never paints the webview to that framebuffer, so every screenshot comes back uniformly blank white regardless of what the DOM actually contains** — a render-environment artifact that looks exactly like a broken/blank app. The DOM is fine; the pixels just never render. (This burned \~hours in the desktop-ipc Phase-4 smoke before it was spotted: the “blank window” was the GL-less Xvfb, not the app.)

**Get real GPU GL one of two ways:**

1. **Run on `:0`** (the real GPU X server): `DISPLAY=:0 …`. Simplest, but puts a window on the operator’s actual screen (focus-steal — see §0).

2. **VirtualGL on an isolated Xvfb** (no focus-steal, real GPU) — *recommended.* `vglrun` routes GL to the GPU’s EGL render node while the app displays to the isolated Xvfb. **Always confirm real GL first** — it must report the GPU, not `llvmpipe`/`swrast`:

   ```sh
   DISPLAY=:90 vglrun -d egl0 glxinfo | grep -i "OpenGL renderer"
   # → OpenGL renderer string: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090/...   (good)
   # → ...llvmpipe / swrast                                  (still software — wrong)
   ```

   VirtualGL isn’t in Ubuntu apt; install the GitHub release once:

   ```sh
   curl -sSL -o /tmp/vgl.deb \
     https://github.com/VirtualGL/virtualgl/releases/download/3.1.4/virtualgl_3.1.4_amd64.deb
   sudo dpkg -i /tmp/vgl.deb
   ```

   Use `-d egl0` — the EGL **device index**. Do NOT pass the `/dev/dri/renderD128` path; VGL rejects it (“Invalid EGL device”).

Recipe — isolated **GPU-accelerated** instance via VirtualGL (no focus-steal):

```sh
Xvfb :90 -screen 0 1920x1080x24 -nolisten tcp &  echo $! > /tmp/xvfb90.pid
DISPLAY=:90 openbox &                            echo $! > /tmp/openbox90.pid
# Sanity — must be the real GPU, not llvmpipe:
DISPLAY=:90 vglrun -d egl0 glxinfo | grep -i "OpenGL renderer"
# Launch the app UNDER vglrun so WebKitGTK composites on the GPU:
( cd papercusp-desktop && env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY GDK_BACKEND=x11 DISPLAY=:90 \
    vglrun -d egl0 npm run dev ) > /tmp/tauri-xvfb.log 2>&1 &  echo $! > /tmp/tauri-xvfb.pid
# ⚠ Wayland trap: without `env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY GDK_BACKEND=x11` GTK may pick
# the live Wayland seat and open the window on the OWNER'S desktop, ignoring :90.
# ⚠ On the shared dev box prefer the BARE binary over `npm run dev` — the tauri-dev
# watcher restarts/kills your app whenever the fleet edits src-tauri/** (see §15):
#   env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY GDK_BACKEND=x11 DISPLAY=:90 vglrun -d egl0 \
#     ./src-tauri/target/debug/papercusp-desktop > /tmp/tauri-xvfb.log 2>&1 &
# wait for window
until DISPLAY=:90 xdotool search --name Papercusp > /dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done
# The bridge binds an EPHEMERAL port (Server::http("127.0.0.1:0") in
# src-tauri/src/dev_bridge.rs) — there is NO PAPERCUSP_BRIDGE_PORT env var.
# Read the real port/token from /tmp/tauri-dev-bridge-<pid>.token, or just
# `tauri-agent-tools probe` (pass --pid to disambiguate this instance).
WID=$(DISPLAY=:90 xdotool search --name Papercusp | head -1)
DISPLAY=:90 xdotool type --window $WID "hello"; DISPLAY=:90 xdotool key --window $WID Return
DISPLAY=:90 import -window $WID /tmp/shot.png    # ← now shows REAL content, not blank
convert /tmp/shot.png -crop 1280x80+0+460 /tmp/band.png; tesseract /tmp/band.png - 2>/dev/null
```

Cleanup: `kill $(cat /tmp/tauri-xvfb.pid /tmp/openbox90.pid /tmp/xvfb90.pid) 2>/dev/null`.

For a **release build** (no dev bridge) screenshots are your *only* window introspection — so GPU GL via VirtualGL is **mandatory** there, or the screenshot tells you nothing. On a **debug** build the bridge is still up on the isolated instance — find it with `tauri-agent-tools probe --pid <pid>` or the `/tmp/tauri-dev-bridge-<pid>.token` file (the port is ephemeral; there is **no** `PAPERCUSP_BRIDGE_PORT` env var). Prefer the bridge for DOM/JS (it reads the DOM, not pixels, so it works even GL-less) and use this VirtualGL stack only for the pixels.

# Coordination system — adversarial test coverage matrix

Why this exists

**EI-152** and **EI-153** — two real coordination bugs — shipped *past 27 green wake-executor tests*. Both escaped for the same reason: the existing suite was **single-agent unit tests with the real seams mocked**. They asserted the happy path but never **cross-agent isolation**, the **real socket / resume / config seams**, or **multi-session concurrency**. This matrix is the coverage map for the adversarial suite that closes those classes (plan `coordination-test-suite-2026-06-08`). It lists every failure-mode cell, whether it was covered before, and where it is covered now — **no silent gaps** (a silent gap is exactly what shipped EI-152).

## The four test classes that were missing

[Section titled “The four test classes that were missing”](#the-four-test-classes-that-were-missing)

| Class                                        | What it asserts                                                                                                               | Would have caught |
| -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| **C1 — Cross-agent isolation (adversarial)** | For *every* channel (wake, `coord:send`, inbox, presence, locks, work-item claims): A’s traffic **cannot** reach or affect B. | EI-153            |
| **C2 — Real-seam integration**               | The **real** socket inject, the **real** resume (isolated config dir), the **real** PG — not mocked deps.                     | EI-152 + EI-153   |
| **C3 — Multi-session concurrency**           | N live isolated sessions; concurrent wakes / sends / claims / locks → no **lost / duplicated / misrouted** delivery.          | both              |
| **C4 — Liveness/lifecycle matrix**           | Every (alive / exited / stale / pid-reuse / no-pid / ended) × (handle? / live-socket?) → the **correct** outcome.             | EI-152            |
| **C5 — Identity invariants**                 | `PAPERCUSP_SID` / coord ownerId / config-dir correct across launch **and** resume; zero identity/conversation bleed.          | EI-153            |
| **C6 — Idempotency / coalescing / retry**    | Re-arm idempotency; coalescing windows; retry/backoff; no duplicate deliveries; `once=false` standing semantics.              | —                 |

## The keystone

[Section titled “The keystone”](#the-keystone)

`packages/operator-core/test/_multi-session-testbed.ts` — `MultiSessionTestbed` mints N genuinely-isolated sessions (own coord identity + own `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` / `CODEX_HOME` + on-demand own live control socket in an **isolated discovery dir**) and drives every channel against them. Every C1/C3 cell reuses it. The isolated `psuPtyDir` both protects the live fleet’s `~/.papercusp/psu-pty` and is how a test proves `findLiveHost(A)` never returns B’s socket.

## Closed since first publication

[Section titled “Closed since first publication”](#closed-since-first-publication)

EI-155 — interactive-claude config isolation: CLOSED

**Interactive psu/SU + role claude config isolation (EI-155) is now implemented and tested.** Per-session `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` isolation was previously only on the **orchestrator-spawned bee** path (`spawn-mcp.ts`/`invoke.ts` → `~/.papercusp/session-claude/<spawnId>`, restored on **wake-executor resume**); interactive `psu` claude sessions shared one `~/.claude`. The fix (`bootstrap-su`

* `bootstrap-role` → `writeInteractiveClaudeConfig`, keyed by `sid` via the same `sessionClaudeConfigDir` helper the resume leg reads) materializes a **symlink mirror** of `~/.claude` with exactly one thing isolated — the `projects/` transcript store — and the sibling `~/.claude.json` symlinked in. That is what makes it credential-/onboarding-safe where a creds-only dir is not: the user-level `papercusp-su` MCP (lives in `~/.claude.json`), the file-lock + coord hooks (`settings.json`), plugins/skills, and onboarding/trust all carry through; only the conversation transcripts are private (so `/resume` + wake-by-uuid never reach a peer’s session — the EI-153 root). Verified live on claude-code 2.1.169 (a creds-only dir lost the MCP + hooks; the mirror restores them). Covered by `interactive-claude-config.test.ts` (7) + the `bootstrap-su`/`bootstrap-role` route assertions (CLAUDE\_CONFIG\_DIR present for claude, absent for omp/codex, non-fatal on materialize failure).

Full real claude/codex resume spawn: CLOSED (live-smoke)

**The real-CLI resume rung now has a live-smoke.** The CI test (`wake-resume-isolation.test.ts`) still asserts the wake-executor *builds* the right resume command + hands it to `spawnDetached` (bin/args/env captured via an injected `spawnDetached`). Its complement — does that command, run for real, actually continue the session? — is `apps/operator/scripts/resume-spawn-live.ts`, surfaced as the coordination-suite **C5 real resume spawn (live)** runner. It builds the resume command via the SAME `resumeCommandFor`, runs it against the REAL `claude` / `codex` binary in the EI-155 isolated `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` / `CODEX_HOME`, and asserts the resume CONTINUED the exact session **deterministically** — the session transcript / rollout file GROWS — independent of the model’s output. Gated (needs creds → not CI); each agent leg SKIPS when its CLI is absent/unauthed. Both legs verified green on this box (claude 2.1.169, codex).

## Accepted gaps (logged — not silent)

[Section titled “Accepted gaps (logged — not silent)”](#accepted-gaps-logged--not-silent)

Accepted gaps

* **Production peer ADDRESSING for the authority remote leg.** The HTTP transport is boot-registered and the whole file-lock chain is proven over a real wire, but `shared_presence` carries identity, not a network address — so on a real multi-box deployment no peer address resolves until a topology layer calls `configurePeerAddressResolver` or sets `PAPERCUSP_AUTHORITY_PEER_ADDRESSES`. Until then every remote-authority op fails OPEN with a loud warning (D-004 — git-merge is the data backstop). Tracked in `coord-system-e2e-testing-2026-06-10` (P-006 note; the two-box variant is P-010, owner-gated). Not silent: the fail-open path itself is covered by the cells above.
* **The ts-based watermark’s same-ts boundary.** The watermark cursors are ISO timestamps and the inbox filter is strictly-later, so a consumer that commits the ts of a PARTIALLY-consumed same-ts group will never see that group’s remaining entries. Pinned (not fixed) in `watermark-crash-restart.integration.test.ts` with the safe-commit rule a consumer must follow: when consumption ends mid-group, commit the previous DISTINCT ts (re-see beats skip). A structural fix would key the cursor by `(ts, msg_id)` — a protocol change tracked in `coord-system-e2e-testing-2026-06-10` (P-002 note), not silently absorbed here.
* **Holder→authority heartbeat re-assert as a production op kind.** The D-005 handover protocol (holders re-assert held locks to a new authority; the `LockSetReconstructor` rebuilds within one heartbeat interval) is proven E2E with a rig-local `lock.assert` op. Production wiring — a `lock.assert` kind in `file-lock-authority-ops.ts` fired from the locks heartbeat path on authority change — is not built yet. Until it is, a failover’s rebuild window behaves as pure fail-open (D-004). Tracked in `coord-system-e2e-testing-2026-06-10` (P-007 note).
* The two gaps logged at first publication (interactive-claude config isolation, real resume spawn) are both closed above.

# P-079 runbook — live bidirectional federation acceptance

> **Webapp retired.** Every `localhost:3055`/`localhost:3070` URL here is only reachable while the **Tauri dev shell** is running (`cd papercusp-desktop && npm run dev`). Drive the operator through the Tauri shell, not a browser (see [Agent E2E playbook](/internal/docs/testing/agent-e2e)).

This is the acceptance test for Phase-1b bidirectional federation: two **different** GitHub engineers join/share a harness and sync state **both ways** over the Model B Hyperswarm substrate. It is the gate that closes implementation **Open-Risk R-1** (see below) — the one thing that cannot be asserted offline.

Design: `apps/operator/docs/plans/papercusp-phase1b-bidirectional-federation-2026-06-01.md`. The deterministic offline proof (module + transport, gate stubbed) already exists at `packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/__tests__/two-peer-swarm-bidi.test.ts`; this runbook covers what that test *can’t*: the real GitHub publish→verify loop with two real identities.

Most of P-079 is now an automatable gated test (2026-06-02)

The **whole identity path** — not just the gist crux — now runs **in-process with two real GitHub identities** as a creds-gated acceptance test: `packages/operator-core/lib/identity/p079-live-federation.live.test.ts` (`P079_LIVE=1 npx vitest run p079-live-federation.live`). With both accounts authed on one box, “two machines” collapses to “two distinct GitHub identities”, which IS automatable. The test stubs **nothing** on the identity path: real OAuth `verifyChannel1` (`GET /user`), real attestation gists owned by each account, real device-signed contributor files on `user/<id>` branches of a real shared repo, the **real `verifyChannel2` (no override)** admitting each peer **both ways**, forgery rejection (`oauth_user_id_mismatch` + `github_user_id_mismatch`), and a **real-Hyperswarm bidirectional feature federation gated by the real `verifyChannel2` adapter** (local testnet DHT). It self-cleans its gists + `user/<id>` branches + throwaway keychain entries. The **manual** steps below are now only needed for **Mode B** — two real *machines*, where NAT/firewall/public-DHT reachability is the thing that can’t be faked on one host.

Verified live — gist crux 2026-06-01, full in-process pass 2026-06-02

The **channel-2 publish→verify loop** — the offline-impossible crux — was first run live 2026-06-01 with two genuinely distinct GitHub accounts (`papercupai` + `aviynw`): each created a real attestation **gist** under its own account, and the **real** `verifyAttestation` / `verifyChannel2` accepted each peer for the correct identity **bidirectionally**, while a *forged* identity claim (one account’s gist claimed as the other’s id) was rejected with `github_user_id_mismatch` (D-006 holds live). That run also surfaced + fixed a real bug: the attestation **gist filename** used a raw base64 pubkey prefix, but a gist filename can’t contain `/` (\~11% of device keys) — fixed in `attestationGistFilename` (commit `ae5e25be3`).

On **2026-06-02** this was extended to a **full in-process Mode-A pass** and captured as the gated `p079-live-federation.live.test.ts` (above): the same two real identities published real gists **and** real signed contributor files to a real shared repo, the **real `verifyChannel2` (no override)** admitted each peer both ways, and they **federated a feature bidirectionally over the real Hyperswarm transport with the real channel-2 adapter as the admission gate** — i.e. the swarm/transport half (steps 4–7) is now exercised against the real gate, not just the `two-peer-swarm-bidi` stub. The only thing left for a *true* Mode-B pass is two real **machines** (public-DHT/NAT reachability).

R-1 — RESOLVED: channel-2(c) anchors on gist ownership, not a verified commit

**Historical:** the original design required the contributor-file *commit* to be GitHub-**verified** (`commit.verification.verified === true`). A live probe found Contents-API commits come back **unverified** (`reason: unsigned`) in the real gh-token context, so that check was unsatisfiable and would have blocked **all** admission. **R-1 is resolved** by re-anchoring channel-2 step (c) on **gist ownership**: the contributor file embeds a `device_attestation_gist_id`, and `verifyAttestation` checks that gist is **owned by the claimed `github_user_id`** (GitHub reports `gist.owner.id`), attests the announced `device_pubkey`, and carries a valid device Ed25519 signature. No commit-verification is required anywhere. The 2026-06-01 live run above confirms the gist-ownership anchor works with two real identities.

## Two modes

[Section titled “Two modes”](#two-modes)

* **Mode A — same laptop, two instances (Q-2 surrogate, do this FIRST).** Catches *code* bugs. Two operator instances with fully isolated state + two distinct GitHub accounts. Cheap, fast, repeatable.
* **Mode B — two real machines.** Catches *network* bugs (NAT, firewall, DHT reachability). Run only after Mode A passes.

The **decision rule** (from `papercusp-dogfood-phase11-multi-engineer-dogfood-2026-05-26`): **P-079 PASSES when ≥5 of the 7 walkthrough steps land within 30 s of the user action** — AND the two hard gates hold: (i) both peers’ attestation **gists** are owned by their claimed GitHub id (channel-2(c) holds), (ii) data flows **both** directions.

## Prerequisites (both modes)

[Section titled “Prerequisites (both modes)”](#prerequisites-both-modes)

* Two **distinct** GitHub accounts (call them **Alice** and **Bob**), each with access to a shared test repo (use a throwaway repo, not a production one). Any real GitHub identity is admissible — there is **no** repo-collaborator gate at the substrate; GitHub’s own write/branch-protection rules gate the actual PR merge. So Alice and Bob each just need to be real, `gh`-authenticated GitHub users who can push a `user/<id>` branch to the repo.
* Each side authenticated: `gh auth status` shows the intended account (Alice on her instance, Bob on his). The join/share flow resolves identity **server-side** from this — you do **not** type credentials into the UI.

Why two distinct accounts (not one)

A peer’s device key lives in the OS keychain under `<github_user_id>:<machine-fingerprint>`. Two *different* GitHub accounts get distinct keychain ids → distinct device keys → two genuinely distinct peers, even on one machine. The same account on two machines would currently collide on the login-keyed contributor file (see the [multi-device limitation](/internal/docs/agent-insights/phase1b-federation-limitations)).

### Mode A — isolating two instances on one laptop

[Section titled “Mode A — isolating two instances on one laptop”](#mode-a--isolating-two-instances-on-one-laptop)

Each instance needs its **own**: workspace root (→ its own per-harness corestore), Postgres database, `gh` identity, and Tauri bridge port. Run the second instance under its own Xvfb display so it never steals your focus (see [Agent E2E §15.4](/internal/docs/testing/agent-e2e)):

```sh
# Instance B (Bob) — isolated display, bridge port, and gh config
Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1920x1080x24 -nolisten tcp &
DISPLAY=:99 openbox &
DISPLAY=:99 \
  PAPERCUSP_BRIDGE_PORT=9230 \
  GH_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/gh-bob \
  PAPERCUSP_HOME=/tmp/papercusp-bob \
  bash -lc 'cd papercusp-desktop && npm run dev'
# (gh auth login --hostname github.com  with GH_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/gh-bob, as Bob, beforehand)
```

Instance A (Alice) is your normal `papercusp-desktop && npm run dev` on `:0`. Point each instance’s operator at a **separate** PG database (distinct `DATABASE_URL` / embedded-pg dir) so “Alice’s PG” and “Bob’s PG” are observably different — that is what makes “data crossed the wire” verifiable.

## The 7-step walkthrough

[Section titled “The 7-step walkthrough”](#the-7-step-walkthrough)

1. **Alice shares the harness.** In Alice’s Tauri shell, open the harness’s **Share** wizard (ShareWizard) and finalize. This writes `.papercusp/shared.json`, **publishes Alice’s attestation gist + contributor file** (the file via the Contents API, embedding the gist id), boots Alice’s substrate (joins the swarm topic derived from the repo id) and announces. Note the **join link** the wizard shows (“Send this link to contributors…”).

2. **Confirm Alice’s binding: contributor file + an owned attestation gist (channel-2 gate).** On the shared repo, the `user/<alice_id>` branch should now have `.papercusp/contributors/<alice_login>.json`. That file embeds a `device_attestation_gist_id`; confirm the gist exists and is **owned by Alice’s account** (the channel-2(c) anchor — no commit-verification is involved):

   ```sh
   # gist id from the contributor file
   gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/contents/.papercusp/contributors/<alice_login>.json?ref=user/<alice_id> \
     --jq '.content' | base64 -d | jq -r '.device_attestation_gist_id'
   # confirm that gist's owner id === Alice's github user id
   gh api gists/<gist_id> --jq '.owner.id, .owner.login'
   # expect:  <alice_id>   <alice_login>
   ```

   **If the gist is missing or owned by a different id, channel-2 won’t admit** — see *Troubleshooting*.

3. **Bob joins via the link.** In Bob’s shell, open the create-harness picker → **Entry 4 (harness link)**, paste Alice’s link, and join. Bob’s identity is resolved server-side from his `gh` auth (no creds typed). Watch the join progress through the 6 steps: `oauth_attest → clone_repo → publish_binding → boot_federate → await_admission_merge → route_insights`. After `publish_binding`, repeat the Step-2 gist-ownership check for **Bob’s** file on `user/<bob_id>`.

   * If join returns **“GitHub authentication required”**, Bob’s `gh` isn’t authenticated in that instance’s `GH_CONFIG_DIR` — fix and retry.

4. **Bob admits Alice (publisher→joiner).** On Bob’s `/admin/dogfood-substrate` (or the boot-history), expect an `announce_admitted` for Alice’s device pubkey within \~30 s. `announce_pending` is fine transiently (GitHub propagation) — it self-heals via the retry; `announce_rejected` is a failure (inspect the reason).

5. **Alice admits Bob (joiner→publisher).** Symmetric: Alice’s boot-history shows `announce_admitted` for Bob within \~30 s.

6. **Alice → Bob data flow.** Alice creates/edits a feature in the shared harness. It appears in **Bob’s** queue (Bob’s PG / Bob’s harness UI) within \~30 s.

7. **Bob → Alice data flow.** Bob creates/edits a feature. It appears in **Alice’s** queue within \~30 s. (Bonus: have both claim the same feature to exercise the LWW advisory claim + clobber-toast.)

## Pass criteria

[Section titled “Pass criteria”](#pass-criteria)

* **Hard gate 1 — channel-2 anchor:** both contributors’ attestation **gists** (Steps 2 + 3) exist and are **owned by the claimed `github_user_id`** (so `verifyAttestation` returns valid). *Non-negotiable.* (This replaces the obsolete “verified commit” gate — see the R-1 Aside; no commit-verification is required.)
* **Hard gate 2 — bidirectional:** Steps 6 **and** 7 both succeed (data crosses in *both* directions, into *separate* PGs).
* **Soft gate:** ≥5 of the 7 steps land within 30 s of the triggering action.

Record each failing step as a P-027-style observation on `F-DOGFOOD-001` (per the Phase-11 plan).

## Inspecting state

[Section titled “Inspecting state”](#inspecting-state)

* **Boot/admission events:** `/admin/dogfood-substrate` (substrate diagnostic), or `GET /api/admin/dogfood-substrate-boot-history`. Kinds: `peer_connected`, `announce_admitted`, `announce_pending`, `announce_rejected`, `announce_error`, `peer_revoked`, `merge_error`.
* **Health:** `GET /api/admin/dogfood-substrate-health` (idle = `harnesses:[]`, `worstVerdict:'healthy'`).
* **Replicated rows:** query each instance’s Postgres for the harness’s feature queue / contributor tables (the read-merge projects admitted peers’ ops there).

## Troubleshooting

[Section titled “Troubleshooting”](#troubleshooting)

* **`announce_rejected` with `binding_invalid`** → channel-2 couldn’t verify the peer’s binding. Most likely the peer’s **attestation gist is missing or owned by a different GitHub id** (channel-2(c)), the contributor file is missing on the `user/<id>` branch (a+b), or the `device_pubkey` in the file/gist doesn’t match the announced key (e.g. a multi-device collision — same login on two machines). Note: a deleted gist is *also the revocation signal* (`channel2_attestation_missing`).
* **Stuck `announce_pending`** → GitHub hasn’t propagated the just-pushed file yet; it self-heals within the 30-min grace. If it never clears, the file/branch is missing or the API read is failing.
* **No `peer_connected` at all** → swarm/DHT reachability (Mode B: NAT/firewall on the DHT port). Confirm both booted with a non-null `swarm` and the **same** `topicHex`.
* **Federation only one way** → the silent side’s binding isn’t verifiable by the other (re-check that side’s Step-2 gist-ownership + that its contributor file exists, AND that the *reading* peer can actually read the shared repo — a private repo the other peer can’t access reads as 404 → stuck `pending`).

## Escalation — channel-2 gist anchor (R-1 history)

[Section titled “Escalation — channel-2 gist anchor (R-1 history)”](#escalation--channel-2-gist-anchor-r-1-history)

R-1 was the worry that channel-2(c) required a GitHub-**verified commit**, which a live probe showed is unsatisfiable (Contents-API commits return `verified:false / reason:unsigned`). **That risk is closed:** channel-2(c) now anchors on **gist ownership** (`verifyAttestation`: `gist.owner.id === claimed github_user_id` + device-pubkey match + Ed25519 sig), which needs no commit verification and is confirmed live (2026-06-01, two real identities). If a future change reintroduced a commit-verification dependency, the same escalation ladder would apply (GitHub App commit signing → registered GPG/SSH key → documented relaxation) — but it does not apply today.

A reliability gotcha the live run found: the attestation **gist filename** must use the URL/filename-safe base64 alphabet — a raw base64 pubkey prefix contains `/` (\~11% of keys), which GitHub rejects as a gist filename. Fixed in `attestationGistFilename` (`ae5e25be3`); the regression test pins it.

After this passes, the longer **P-080 soak** (Alice + Bob each use Papercusp for ≥5 consecutive working days on the harness) is the next acceptance milestone.

# Visual regression — Storybook + Lost Pixel

This page is the operational guide to Phase 4 of the testing framework (see [`testing/index`](./index)). Stories are the test cases; a diff against the committed baseline is the assertion.

## TL;DR

[Section titled “TL;DR”](#tldr)

```bash
# Local — verify your branch hasn't drifted
npm run lostpixel --workspace libs/generic/ui-primitives


# Local — regenerate baselines (intentional change only)
npm run lostpixel:update --workspace libs/generic/ui-primitives


# CI — runs automatically on `run-visual` PR label or push to main
```

## What’s covered today

[Section titled “What’s covered today”](#whats-covered-today)

| Package                      | Stories      | Baselines | Storybook port |
| ---------------------------- | ------------ | --------- | -------------- |
| `libs/generic/ui-primitives` | 6 components | 33 PNGs   | `:6006`        |
| `libs/marketplace-public-ui` | 3 components | 14 PNGs   | `:6007`        |
| `libs/agent-chat`            | 2 components | 7 PNGs    | `:6008`        |
| `apps/operator`              | 3 components | 10 PNGs   | `:6009`        |

## Adding a story

[Section titled “Adding a story”](#adding-a-story)

1. **Drop a `Foo.stories.tsx` next to `Foo.tsx`** in any `libs/*/src/` that has Storybook wired:

   ```tsx
   import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
   import { Foo } from './Foo';


   const meta: Meta<typeof Foo> = { component: Foo };
   export default meta;


   export const Default: StoryObj<typeof Foo> = {};
   export const WithTone: StoryObj<typeof Foo> = { args: { tone: 'good' } };
   ```

2. **Verify it renders** — `npm run storybook --workspace libs/<lib>` and visit the port shown above.

3. **Generate the baseline** — `npm run build-storybook --workspace libs/<lib>` then `npm run lostpixel:update --workspace libs/<lib>`. PNGs land in `lostpixel-baseline/`. **Commit them.**

4. **Verify clean** — `npm run lostpixel --workspace libs/<lib>`. Should exit 0 with all stories within threshold.

## Adding Storybook to a new lib

[Section titled “Adding Storybook to a new lib”](#adding-storybook-to-a-new-lib)

If you’re stand­ing up Storybook for the first time in a lib:

```bash
npm install --save-dev --workspace libs/<lib> \
  storybook @storybook/react-vite @storybook/addon-docs lost-pixel \
  --legacy-peer-deps --ignore-scripts
```

Then create the four required files (copy from `libs/ui-primitives`):

* `.storybook/main.ts` — story glob + framework
* `.storybook/preview.ts` — backgrounds + global CSS imports
* `lostpixel.config.ts` — paths + threshold
* `.gitignore` additions: `storybook-static/`, `lostpixel-current/`, `lostpixel-diff/`

Add four scripts to `package.json`:

```json
"storybook": "storybook dev -p 6008",
"build-storybook": "storybook build -o storybook-static",
"lostpixel": "lost-pixel",
"lostpixel:update": "LOST_PIXEL_GENERATE_ONLY=1 lost-pixel"
```

Pick a unique port per lib (`6006` ui-primitives, `6007` marketplace-public-ui, `6008+` for new ones). Wire the new lib into the `visual` job in `.github/workflows/test.yml` so CI covers it.

Lost Pixel pins playwright-core\@1.47.2

The repo’s main Playwright is `1.59.1`, but Lost Pixel ships its own older copy. The CI workflow installs Chromium for that copy via `node node_modules/lost-pixel/node_modules/playwright-core/cli.js install chromium`. Locally the same command runs on first use.

## When a baseline diff is reported

[Section titled “When a baseline diff is reported”](#when-a-baseline-diff-is-reported)

Two cases:

1. **Intentional UI change** — eyeball the diff (`lostpixel-diff/`), confirm the new render is what you wanted, then `npm run lostpixel:update` and commit the new `lostpixel-baseline/` PNG. The CI run on your PR will then exit 0.

2. **Unintentional regression** — read the diff, fix the bug. Don’t regenerate the baseline.

The threshold is `0.05` (5%); small antialiasing wobble below that won’t flag. If you find yourself wanting to bump the threshold, something is probably wrong — investigate the wobble first.

## What gets baselined vs ignored

[Section titled “What gets baselined vs ignored”](#what-gets-baselined-vs-ignored)

`.gitignore` per lib:

* ✅ **`lostpixel-baseline/`** — committed (the test fixtures).
* ❌ `lostpixel-current/` — per-run output, ignored.
* ❌ `lostpixel-diff/` — per-run output, ignored.
* ❌ `storybook-static/` — per-run build, ignored.

When the global PNG count grows past \~50, the spec (§1.11) calls for git-lfs to keep the repo light. Until then, direct-commit is simpler and avoids any LFS-bandwidth surprises in CI.

## CI behavior

[Section titled “CI behavior”](#ci-behavior)

The `visual` job in `.github/workflows/test.yml`:

* Runs on PRs **only** when the `run-visual` label is applied (matches the spec §1.11 opt-in pattern), and on every push to `main`.
* Builds Storybook + runs Lost Pixel for each wired lib in sequence.
* Uploads `lost-pixel-diffs` artifact on failure (combined `current/` and `diff/` from every lib).

To auto-apply `run-visual` when story files touch, add a CODEOWNERS or labeler workflow rule for `libs/**/*.stories.@(ts|tsx)` (not yet wired — open follow-up).
